deckinfo.name: SCG ATL (6-0) Necromonsters
deckinfo.primer:
Intro/backstory: Water is busted! Finally! Water is my favorite element. Tried some early waveshaper and even seer and could never get the decks to do what I wanted. Then came gothic and more importantly Harbinger! I love that avatar play big aquatic nightmares and pull stuff into the void! Who doesn't love that! Plus Succubus, Aino, Lilith, Raphael, failed mutation, MMC! So many great new minions. Alas The variance on harbinger means without voidwalk sometime setup takes too long. Looking at you interrogator. Then came @Ceej's water necromancer list. Saw it and thought it was super neat. Then funnily enough played against it that night on TTS by another player and was sold. The synergies between skeletons and shapeshift, gnarled wendigo, swap and your troll bridges and thin ice! Insanity, plus the impetus to play stuff early isn't there. You get to play stuff when you want/need to vs feeling like you have to have a minion to block/attack early because of the skeletons.

Gameplan: You control the pace of the game with creatures that interact with or remove stuff favorably. You always have good value minions to play and can cheat in big stuff early. Need to go aggro? Send the skeletons then shapeshift into a menace Need to play more control? Defensive sites and play back until you set up. Midrange slog? We do that to. Always need a chump blocker? Need something to feed your temple of moloch, gilman house, or panoptic manuscript? Tokens, token, tokens. Tawny who?


This deck can be built a lot of different ways. Mine is tailored to how I like to play. Which is a more tempo based game plan I like to be able to adjust to what my opponent is doing. Trade favorably. Always have something to do. Have answers into most anything. There are lot of things that can and have beaten this list in play testing but I think the best thing about it is you should almost always be able to play the game. Sometimes you have blowout control games. Sometimes you just play on curve and play valuetown minions and attrition out. I've only ever had one game even in testing where I couldn't piece anything together where I didn't feel like I could play. Super fun deck! Check out @Ceej's version super cool different take and I think he deserves credit for the Water necro archetype. I feel like the SCG ATL win was a lot of luck paired with water being in a great spot. Happy to do a write up of those matches but just wanted to give my thoughts for whatever they're worth on this super fun deck and the fact we have a super solid Water archetype to tool around with! Best of luck Water Sorcerors!

deckinfo.name: FE Archimago - Top 8 SCGCon DC Grand Contest
Afterlife 60/30
deckinfo.primer:
Value

There is not, strictly, a theme--I simply brute force good numbers. I churn out a lot of card advantage through DS-Genesis. I operate on the premise that the player who spends the most mana usually wins the game; my Avatar wants to stand on position 3/18 the entire game, so I don't waste a single Site placement--this is also why I don't run Ring of Morrigan. At its heart, this is a midrange deck:


  • 2:1s that don't set me too far behind
  • Enough life gain to survive the aggro lists while I turn the corner with,
  • High-rate creatures to maximize virtual card advantage
  • Curve that stops at 7 for high-scaling-inevitability
  • Utility lands that either slow your opponent, or create more creatures


Games where you open with Geistwood and make your Genesis creatures read from the Pnakotic Manuscript are, usually, one-sided. I don't mulligan looking for uniques--because we have strict thresholds to meet--but, sometimes, you get lucky.


Threats

Take only the best Genesis creatures. There are more available than you can possibly fit, so don't be tricked by the keyword where there are better options. Make them "sticky!"


  • The Hexham Haunts & Crown Prince (18 other mortals) keep coming back
  • Lady Iseult for infinite Genesis
  • Young Master Damion with immortal bodyguards, and two more for the road
  • Talamh Dreig with immunity to the forced-movement water menaces (also, Bury & Drown)


Answers

Avoiding cards that can get stuck in your hand vs. playing what is most efficient. I lean into consistency.


  • Lightning Bolts that have no targeting restrictions and a floor of damaging Avatars
  • Thunderstorm for similar reasons--though I often hope it deals 9 damage to Avatars
  • Bury & Cast Into Exile as emergency removal. I limit Exile to one copy, as it does have a restriction
  • Earthquakes that have no targeting restrictions and ignore Ward


Packages

  • Assorted Animals & Falconer: [Grain Sparrow, Peace Offering, Palliburie & Vampire Bats], Root Spider, White Hart, Black Cat, Gargantula, Conqueror Worm
  • Returned King: Boulevard, Master Necromancer, Damion
  • King of the Realm: 18 mortals, but I tend to avoid this King because he dies too easily for 7 mana


Threshold & Mulligans

Gothic's powerful additions come at a steep cost. As much as I love Vile Imps, I don't feel Fire Geneses scale as well as Air, or Earth. Rather than waste precious Site-equity, I cut fire. Archangel Michael is worth it, but I do miss Sir Morien.

I tend to keep four or five cards. I aim for one Earth and one Air site, and the third site is usually kept or mulled based upon the spells I'm keeping. It may surprise you that I prefer not to have Cores in my opener; I'm more likely to keep them, on the draw. They often empty my hand before I have anything else to do with DS. The exception is usually Grandmaster Wizard, which I warp my play around casting asap.


See also: (https://stattrek.com/online-calculator/hypergeometric)


Collection

I have so many mana sinks, that the collection is almost wasted. 7 slots are taken by Ghouls and Knights, and the other 3 slots are a distraction for Legions of Gall. If you find you require more answers than threats in your metagame, cut a few Gifts of the Wolf to make room for Toolboxes.


Meta

The Maybeboard is about your metagame. My list is what I would consider 'stock,' for threats and answers. If you play against a lot of Mortals, or Undead, bring in the relevant King. Up against Savior? Bane of Aventis likely turns the board around. As for what I'd call the flex-slots, I'd swap out top-end threats:


  • Adtonitum, Talahm Dreig --> Kings if you play against Undead and/or Mortals
  • Paladins of Bazia --> Bane of Aventis
  • Forlorn Keep --> Impenetrable Copse, Pebbled Path, Holy Ground, Haystack, Boulevard of Bones, etc.
  • Cloud City, Merlin's Tower --> Perilous Bridge, Fields of Phyxis, Mountain Pass

deckinfo.name: Archimago 🤌🍝 - Gothic Update
deckinfo.primer:
{{https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9iTuDvk45Qk}}


Currently testing and updates (may-26)


      You can now check my performance and latest games on sorceryrec.com!


In:

[[Gargantula]] and 2 [[Stone-gaze Gorgons]]

  • reinforcements to help stabilize the board
  • both can deal with warded minions

Out:

3 [[Kettletop Leprechaun]]

  • as much as I used to like them, I feel like they don't provide good trades anymore with water minions dominating the meta


(Be wary the average mana cost of the deck has increased, but we now have more relevant options for the Control Phase)


About the deck


This is a control deck built around [[Archimago]], aiming to outlast the opponent, dominate the mid/late game, and win through inevitability rather than early pressure.

With the Gothic card pool and the 60/30/10 deck structure, the deck leans heavily into:

  • Efficient interaction
  • Redundancy
  • High spell density
  • Flexible Atlas and Spellbook that adapt to matchups

The goal is simple: survive early, stabilize the board, then lock the game down until the opponent runs out of meaningful plays.


Strengths

  • Excellent late game
  • Strong card advantage through [[Archimago]]'s ability + several ways to draw cards
  • High flexibility
  • Very good against midrange and slower strategies

Weaknesses

  • Low minion count
  • Can be vulnerable to explosive early aggression (chargers, [[Jihad]], [[Summoning Sphere]])
  • Requires careful sequencing and resource management
  • Misplays are heavily punished
  • Can struggle if forced into low-resource games early

This deck rewards patience and precision.


Core strategy


DON'T BE AFRAID TO MULLIGAN.

Optimize the position of your sites and units.

Use your cantrips just to draw cards.

Chain your tutors.

Use [[Archimago]]'s ability.


Ok this is a control deck, but let's go more in depth and divide the main strategy into 4 separate phases:

Crisis → Control → Pivot → Win


Crisis Phase

The world is on fire and you need to survive.

  • Start the game by greeting your opponent (important!) and assuming your Avatar is already in trouble
  • Mulligan according to your opponent's Avatar and try your best to predict their main strategy
  • Buy as much time as possible in the first 3 turns.

A well placed defensive site can prevent your opponent from attacking you for 1-3 turns. Sites are your best early game answers to threats:

  • [[Pebbled Paths]] - really strong against (F) aggro, shutting down chargers
  • [[Perilous Bridge]] - good against every deck, placing this on turn 2 directly above [[Archimago]]'s starting position forces your opponent to take a detour and usually buys you 2+ turns
  • [[Gnome Hollows]] - same as above, but you can also play this as your first site if you have another defensive site in hand, as it can prevent an early [[Aino]] or from being attacked by a [[Battlemage]] or minions controlled by [[Interrogator]] later in the game.

Manage your draws and plan ahead:

  • Usually we want to draw 3 spells before drawing sites again BUT
  • Don't be afraid to draw sites for the first couple turns if you didn't get any defensive ones in your first 3 + mulligan
  • Remember: life is a resource! Don't be afraid to take some damage here and there, don't try to kill everything, you won't have the mana nor the cards to do so
  • Use your [[Bury]], [[Magic Missiles]], [[Lightning Bolt]], to handle relevant minions
  • [[Common Sense]] can be used to tutor a specific answer early, but ideally we want to chain tutor for another common sense with spare mana to fill out our graveyard
  • Unless you have a [[Root Spider]] in hand, you're probably handling one minion at a time, so your goal here is to be patient and reach (5) mana to proceed to the Control Phase


Control Phase

This phase usually starts when we hit (5)+ mana and after our first "crowd control" effect resolves, which can be one of the following:

  • [[Poison Nova]] - don't hesitate to kill your own minions, position yourself and kill as much enemy minions as you can
  • [[Earthquake]] - same as above, and always be aware of possible site placement manipulation. Be mindful of the (E)(E) cost. This can be done defensively or aggressively ([[Smokestacks of Gnaak]])
  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] - at least -1 minion to care about every turn
  • [[The Great Famine]] and [[The Black Plague]] - both can deal with troublesome minions, either by killing them or preventing them from entering affected sites for the duration of the aura. Just don't forget they DO NOT kill warded minions
  • [[Murder of Crows]] - can be devastating when cast back to back for (6). Be mindful of the (A)(A) cost
  • [[Fields of Camlann]] - (F)(F)(F) is kind of a pain to achieve early on, but if you do, this site wipes the board for (0) mana and you're able to follow it up with a meaningful play

After that the opponent might be left with little to no minions on board, or even running out of gas, but be prepared for game changing spells and keep managing your game plan:

  • You're at (5)+ mana, and so is your opponent
  • Evaluate what you have in hand vs. what threats you need to deal with
  • Don't rush! You don't need to get to that (8) mana + 1 site to cast [[Craterize]] asap (or at all really)
  • Usually it's best to settle at (6) mana and draw as much spells as you need to stabilize the board first
  • Be mindful of opponents trying to site lock and stiffle you
  • Be ready to counter or play around hate sites ([[River of Blood]], [[Haystack]], [[Kor Crematory]], [[Mismanaged Mortuary]], [[Funeral Pyre]], [[Garden of Eden]])
  • Try your best to avoid being put at Death's Door. Once you're at DD, there's no turning back and it's gonna get exponentially harder to win the match
  • Look out for [[Divine Healing]] or [[Angel's Egg]], the amount of healing provided can be overwhelming with multiple copies. Don't forget about the (E)(E)(E) cost
  • [[Morgana le Fay]], [[Merlin]], [[Grandmaster Wizard]], [[Browse]], [[Blink]] and other cantrips help you dig your spellbook
  • Keep controlling the board and chaining [[Common Sense]]. As always, look for specific targets when needed, but the last one most often should be [[Border Militia]] (see Pivot Phase)

Don't overdo it:

  • Pay attention to the time limit - usually 45 min in tournaments
  • Try not to waste time, be wary of your opponents too and remind them there's a time limit (politely, because they are also thinking hard at this point)
  • Always ask yourself "who is the beatdown?"
  • Look for windows to pivot and proceed to the next phase


Pivot Phase

It's very important that you understand this is somewhat of a trial and error phase, and you might succeed and proceed to the win or even return back to the Control Phase:

  • [[Border Militia]] - helps us defend very well but also is one of our main tools to pivot from a reactive playstyle to a more proactive one. When combined with [[Archimago]]'s ability, it is possible to create a surprising amount of [[Foot Soldier]] tokens that can turn the game upside down VERY quickly.
  • [[Guards!]] - position yourself and drop 7+ soldiers with one cast, then repeat next turn
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]] - I don't know what to say, this card is just great and depending on what you have in hand + graveyard you can wipe the board while recovering to full health
  • [[Lightning Bolt]] and [[Magic Missiles]] - cast and recast those to deal high amounts of damage. Searchable with any [[Common Sense]] left in our graveyard


Win Phase

You have become inevitable: overwhelm them with damage and win.

  • [[Craterize]] - used to be the main win condition but now with a 60-card spellbook there are games we just don't draw this elite. Still, you can use it to deal 10 damage to your opponent's avatar, probably wiping their board and leaving them at DD (or close to it), just to finish them off next turn recasting [[Craterize]] with [[Archimago]]'s ability. Don't forget you need to have 1 site in hand to be discarded. Also, be aware that experienced opponents might move their Avatar closer to you as the game progresses, so you have to be careful when casting this spell.
  • [[Major Explosion]] - redundancy, works as a mini [[Craterize]] and is castable 1-2 turns earlier
  • [[Border Militia]] and [[Guards!]] - as stated above, the amount of tokens this deck can produce is insane and can win you the game out of nowhere. Position your tokens in a way that your opponent is in check at DD
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]] - can be used to quickly drain your opponents life and is a great finisher
  • [[Lightning Bolt]], [[Magic Missiles]] and [[Zap!]] - extra ways to kill an opponent at DD


Opening hand & Mulligans


What You Want to See

  • At least one of the defensive sites
  • A stable mana setup - you must be able to cast your early spells, so consider their thresholds
  • Low-cost removal
  • [[Root Spider]]
  • [[Common Sense]]
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Highland Princess]] to get the ring

Hands with a clear plan for the first 2-3 turns are usually keeps.

What to Mulligan

  • Hands with no early interaction - ship away any sites in order to dig for defensive ones
  • Hands that rely on expensive spells or 3+ threshold spells - Don't worry, there's a lot of shuffling, you'll see that [[Morgana le Fay]] or [[Craterize]] again. Hopefully.
  • Hands that lack consistency - (E)(E)(E) sites with (A)(A) or (F)(F) spells in hand, etc

As a rule:

Focus on your defensive sites, they alone should provide you enough time to develop your game plan, everything else you can get is a bonus. Surviving the early game is the main priority.


Matchups


vs Aggro

  • Mulligan aggressively for early answers
  • Avoid greedy decisions
  • Be careful using life as a resource
  • Stabilization is more important than anything else
  • A single source of healing can win you the game

vs Midrange

  • Try and make 2-for-1 trades early on
  • Save removals for high-impact threats
  • You are favored if the game goes long

vs Control

  • Mulligan aggressively for card advantage
  • Ask yourself "who is the beatdown?" every single turn
  • Plan your game and take advantage of [[Archimago]] recasting key cards and win conditions
  • Resource management, sequencing and card advantage decide the game
  • Watch out for timeouts

deckinfo.name: Furious Witch's Road
deckinfo.primer:
(21/04/2026) Post Gothic Lament (What if...?):


We are several months into the Gothic meta at this point and it has been a truly enjoyable time updating and piloting this deck through the different decks people have been brewing up and playing with. We have come a long way since my speculative notes prior to the release and have now come to another fork in the road. The more I play, the more I feel like we want to be a singular threshold. Play patterns have become increasingly tight and decisions ever more important on even the smallest of details. Frontier Settlers/Kettletop/Land Surveyor will always be pivotal cards for the Furious Witch's Road and that mentality will never shift. What is shifting however is what the meta has been demanding of decks despite the identity a deck wishes to maintain. The main issue I have been running into is: the decks of this meta seem to be pushing me to draw more sites on a moments notice which means 2 things. 1) we cant rely on randomly drawing Land Surveyor to feed us these crucial site draw turns and 2) because we are naturally drawing sites more often, Surveyor starts to feel like a really bad, if not the worst, top deck. Let me be clear that, in no uncertain terms, I firmly believe earth to still be the best support element for this type of Witch deck. The key word here is Support. If the meta shifts in a way that suggests the support is no longer viable, or subpar, we must adapt. I am keeping this list, will continue to work on it and the second I feel things changing back to how they used to, Earth will find its way back into the list. All Earth related cards remain in my deck box to be re-slotted as soon as possible. In the mean time, I am tinkering with this:


https://curiosa.io/decks/cmo5pzisl008n04ju6ivymg81


Despite the Air sites, and couple of air cards in the collection, this is not a Fire/Air deck. Any non fire producing site, until the end game, should just be seen as a threshold-less utility site. The idea of shaving earth isnt to introduce air, it is to have a more consistent threshold baseline where drawing a non fire site does not compromise our ability to play the game since we wont have dead draws. This allows for the abusive site air got in Gothic through [[wuthering heights]] and opens up room for [[wizard's den]]. By introducing these sites (but at the same time no air cards), we increase access to what our deck is trying to achieve and remove the chance for dead draws. This gives us pure, straight gas, turn after turn.


_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


GOTHIC (They're heeeeere):


- I will be keeping all information below this section frozen in place as it provides everything you all need to know about the foundation of this deck and where it comes from (see also this deep dive deck analysis by me). Journey with me now as we see where Gothic takes us:


Gothic Updates:

  • 16/12/2025: Originally kept 8 deserts afraid of ward, but not really seeing any at the moment. I cut 2 Deserts for 2 more [[Molten Maar]]. Removed Onslaught and Detonate from the Collection to fit 2 more hellhounds. If i start missing the extra ping, ill bring it back and probably remove the Blooms, I have not been fully impressed with these sites.
  • 16/12/2025: Removed the [[corrupter freak]] since Jihad alone isn't enough to consistently drop this guy in the opponents territory. Trying [[mazuj ifrit]] in it's place, at 4 power it will have a much easier time living, can trade with [[Lugbog Cat]] and the like and with airborne can be a menace. We also only lose life on the beginning of the turn so if they do kill it right away, it causes no life loss and likely a lot of resources early on from the opponent. Also dropped 1 Trinket to try [[torrid omphalos]].
  • 19/12/2025: Replaced [[raze]] in the collection with [[flame strike]]. Raze is cute but Flame Strike is a DD finisher that we can Toolbox for.
  • 22/12/2025: debating whether or not blood mana and ghostfire belong here but I haven't yet seen them in a game. Will report back. (see 24/12/2025 update)
  • 23/12/2025: Yesterday I played against [[The Rack]] and it absolutely blew my mind. Although it truly shines in the [[Interrogator]], it still provides an insane opportunity to close the Death's Door meanwhile making it difficult for the enemy avatar to run away. It also shines a bright line on [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], [[vile imp]], [[ring of Morrigan]] and [[monstrous lion]]. It also makes [[colicky dragonettes]], [[firebolts]] and [[minor explosion]] hit their target a lot easier. As you can see, the application is insane and its value in the deck is hard to argue. I have personally not been enjoying [[silver bullet]] in this deck due to its Tapping requirement. I almost never want to tap my Witch for this application, so since I only have 2 targets in the Collection, and since our toolbox/common sense can already find ample new DD finishing cards I am cutting [[Silver bullet]] in favor of [[The Rack]]. Adding 1 [[Bury]] to the Collection.
  • 24/12/2025: I have been thinking about [[Blood Mana]] pretty much every day and ultimately came to the conclusion that we do not want to dump our hands. If the opponent is able to deal with that burst, we probably lose 100% of the time. I decided to cut it and the [[petrosian cavalry]], plus move a [[vile imp]] to the Collection to try out [[barging barghest]]. I've seen it showing up in various aggro decks and I do like the extra movement. It also synergizes incredibly (probably our best target) with [[the rack]]
  • 31/12/2025: I'm shifting completely away from Common Sense towards [[toolbox]]. Earth threshold requirements are getting lower and lower but Land surveyor, Quake and Gigantism remain ever crucial as support. Removed [[the rack]] because in the end we are attacking sites a lot more; this card is happy to be sleeved in an interrogator Deck. I also moved [[bury]] to the collection and removed [[minor explosion]] and [[ghostfire]] since Flame Rift does these things better for our purposes.
  • 02/01/2026: Decided to drop the [[slumbering giantess]]. The 5 power has been a lot of fun but lately i've been craving more and more cards that "do something" when drawn off the top of the deck. Also, previous changes have been reducing the amount of cards that can ping her awake making her less reliable. I cut 1 desert and 1 active volcano to re-introduce the multi-thresh sites. I feel more comfortable playing them knowing we now have [[vindictive nation]]. I also re-introduced [[silver bullet]] despite what was written above. Water is proving to be a serious threat in Gothic and more Mono Water or heavily water-influenced decks are showing up. We can absolutely hose these decks with [[drought]] but Drought is not a contender for the main deck. Enter Silver Bullet. It replaces 1x [[Searing Truth]] which now resides in the collection. Replacing the Giantess is 2 [[Sinterfee]] for dealing with annoying prison sites and focusing opposing removal to one of our weaker minions. I added a third Colicky since it is also a 3 drop and the projectile it fires can help deal with Necro's Skeletons or even break Wards.
  • 06/01/2026: I'm starting to doubt [[torrid omphalos]]. Every time i've drawn it in this deck, it feels clunky and not what I want to prioritize. Don't get me wrong, the Omphalos are out of this world amazing cards but for some reason, this deck is the only one so far where im doubtful of them. It feels weird typing this because I know how much we crave cards in this deck. If I do cut it, I might start by trying [[salt the earth]]. Again with more and more water decks and prison sites seeing play, these types of effects are proving to be a premium. It also works very well with Rift Valley and Sinkhole as card #5 that can wreck the opponents mana, threshold and utility site placements. Will return to this update after I spend more time thinking about it.
  • 07/01/2026: Okay finally, I decided to drop the Omphalos and the 2 Searing Truth i had in the main. I always prefer to prioritize damage dealers before card draw in a deck like this so I figured these cards are just a distraction. Searing Truth remains a two of but in the collection with Silver Bullet being increased to 2. It clicked today that it doesnt need to be our Witch who uses it as it grants any bearer the right to cast a spell. 2 bullets also means higher consistency in finding DD finishers (Truth and 1 Hotwheel which was also moved the collection) as well as Drought for those pesky mono water players. In total, I removed 2 Truths, 1 Hemogoblin, 1 Omphalos, 1 Hotwheel and added 1 Salt the Earth, 1 more trinket, sinterfee and bullet, as well as trying our [[Warp Spasm]]. Spasm can be great at being another Gigantism/Blaze of Glory (kind of), chipping away at 40% of the opponents health as well as an amazing token clearing option.
  • 13/01/2026: I played a bunch this past weekend and, despite how many new tools we have to finish the game when opponent is at DD I struggled in every game to actually find these abundance of finishers. Its either just a weekend of bad luck, or the increase to 60 cards has a larger skewing effect than anticipated. I used this update to remove powerful but inconsistent cards in order to add more cards that have an immediate and impactful effect off the top of the deck and increased DD finisher potentials. Also i have found that since the release of Gothic, opponents decks/cards are forcing me to play more than 4 sites. It is unclear if this is a me problem or a result of the new meta, but it has encouraged me to add a few more 5 drops. The changes are as follows: ADDED: [[Courtesan Thais]], [[The Inquisition]], a fourth [[Firebolt]] and the third [[Hotwheel]]. REMOVED: The great famine, salt the earth, rasputin and hemogoblin. I absolutely love Hemogoblin and I am sure he will return but for now, he is too low stat'd doesnt help in negative situations and I am simply not running into much lifegain. Also there is a bit of redundance with Blood River.
  • 24/01/2026: replacing [[angry mob]] with [[gift of the serpent]]. it costs 2 less which means we can toolbox + gift on the same turn. Mob almost always requires you to already have the toolbox in play. no body hurts, but the card draw might be interesting.
  • 02/02/2026: Really craving [[greater blood demon]] and [[grigori rasputin]]. I will go into more detail when i've got time but this is my current consideration after the past week of testing. 03/02/2026: I will either go into more detail about this or delete this update, but both are pending more data. 27/02/2026: Still testing this dooder, but I brought it down to 1 copy. I still really like the body it has and am willing to keep it but in my pursuit for more immediate damage I'm also trying 2 [[Ignited]]. I'm not initially excited about it and if I was to evaluate this card on its own merit I would not include it. Im treating it more like firebolts #5-6 that can damage sites. The more I play the more I think i actually love this card in our deck....
  • 04/02/2026: had to cut [[glastonbury tor]]. ran into a game where I needed to play a site in my opponents territory to maintain tempo and react to their previous turn. Decided to draw a site for turn, my 5th in the game, and it was Tor. Everything spiraled downhill from there. Even if this is a freak occurrence, im not willing to put myself in that position ever again. Also as a very aggressive deck by nature, we are usually inclined to build into our opponents territory for other reasons. Tor does not contribute to this plan at all. I added another Desert but we can also consider another Village or possibly even bring back [[Cursed Land]].
  • 24/02/2026: Played some games last night and in terms of site saw only deserts, villages and poisoned well. Consistently having that free soldier on turn 1 feels so incredible it truly is making reconsider the sites again dropping everything besides Steppe, Sinkhole and Rift Valley and then just maximizing Villages and Deserts. Ill have to keep thinking about it.
  • 06/03/2026: I have played too many games where the molten maar is not useable or I need to make a different play. In this games the Maar becomes the worst site in the deck. In this vein and despite that fact it hurts to do this, Im cutting them in favor of a utility site: [[Leadworks]]. The card is only for 1 turn cycle but it should be just enough to let our guys get in and do their damage. Im considering dropping the [[desert bloom]] for a third one but we will see about that with more testing.
  • 17/03/2026: I've made some big changes and I have not looked back. Really happy with the position we are currently in. With the previous update, the total changes are: Main: -1 [[toolbox]], -2 [[greater blood demon]], -1 [[hotwheel]] (moved to collection) -3 [[molten maar]], +3 [[ignited]], +1 [[grigori rasputin]], +3 [[leadworks]]. MAJOR UPDATES (17/09/2025):

(I am changing the deck often based on what I'm experiencing during gameplay. I am keeping all notations even if a card is no longer in the deck because the info is still relevant and there is always the chance that cards either return or get cut along the adapting process)


I wanted to put this update at the top so anyone reading this can see the changes I made before reading the rest of the primer and possibly getting confused by some things that may seem contradictory. The first thing I need to clarify is that although [[Frontier Settlers]] is praised in the original primer, you probably noticed it is no longer featured in the deck's current state. I still very much believe in both the card and what is written below but the reality is, meta's change, decks change, play patterns change. These are all acceptable and encouraged parts of evolving card games and player skills (both our own and our opponents). At the moment, and as noted in the "Steam Druid Reality" section below, both my own personal meta and seemingly the game's meta in general have become a lot more aggressive, and overall fast. This is due in large, if not entirely, to the rule change made where Units attacking sites now count as Strikes. This rule change improved cards like [[grim guisarme]] and encouraged a more aggro approach to competitive games. If you are simply curious to the changes made from the original list, the cards I removed can be found in the Maybeboard. The cards I added are: 1 Vile Imp, 2 Colicky Dragonettes, 3 Quarrelsome Kobolds, 1 Saracen Raider, 2 Blaze, 1 Great Famine, 1 Lava Flow, 2 Torshammar Trinket.


Let's talk about the removal of the Settlers, Cores and 1 War Horse and then we can discuss the new additions:


[[Frontier Settlers]]

Look, if you read the primer before this update, I know what you're thinking... believe me, I do. I have the same thoughts. And yes, despite them being cut, I still believe everything I wrote below. However, the reality is, one must adapt to their surroundings or get left behind. If the meta were to slow down/favor combo and/or control decks, the first thing I am re-inserting into the deck is the Settlers. For the time being though, the extreme requirement on threshold they present (needing 2 earth on turn 2 and then immediately 2 fire on turn 3 raises too many problems when your opponent throws a cat in your face on turn 2) mixed with their negligible power makes them a liability at most points of the game if you do not see them on turn 1-3. By removing them, in the context of a very fast and aggro meta, we no longer need to warp our opening sites around the above mentioned taxing requirement, we can safely mulligan spells that are suboptimal at the beginning and it allows us to play less greedy site base which protects us from very popular cards like [[earthquake]] and [[Atlantean fate]]. If there was a way to ensure this card was in the opening 2-3 turns I would never cut it, no matter how fast the meta is. For now, however, I need to prioritize the rest of the deck in the face of the aggression I'm experiencing. Without Settlers we may find ourselves naturally drawing a site one turn more than if they were there and as much as I despise this reality, we are not always seeing the settlers in every game anyways, and by reducing the early game threshold tax we are less likely to whiff on site draws, so this should balance itself out.


[[Ruby Core]] [[Onyx Core]]

This one goes hand in hand, sort of, with the removal of the Settlers. Since we are not as taxed anymore with our threshold, and we are more than happy with the way the deck curves out side by side the witch's drain, it seemed good to remove the cores since outside of turn 1, they can be awkward and outright horrendous top decks. Our deck has a singular blood-shed related focus and drawing a core off the top in the mid game can be game losing. Save your cores for the extra greedy lists or the ones that draw multiple cards throughout the game. Here, we just want to be Furious and Burn them All so lets gear our deck towards this objective removing what isn't conducive.


[[War Horse]]

War horse is great, it gets our guys in position, makes Pudge even better and also lets a unit from the back come in for a surprise attack. However, it only has 2 power. If you've ever had your Horse killed by an Imp or even worse an attacking 3 power minion then you know how detrimental the set back can be. I removed one because I absolutely still want to abuse all of its upsides, but I don't want to necessarily see it very often early on. This is not a 2 drop. Its a unit that costs 2 and is best used for utility purposes. Dropping from 3 to 2 isn't a drastic shift in visibility but it is enough to not see it as often in the opening hand and removes the temptation of just simply playing it as a 2 power charge unit too early.


[[Vile Imp]]

I'd rather have this guy at 3 than Horse. Im never sad to see an Imp and air dropping it on a Jihaded site is much better than the horse. Direct damage wins games. Id like to be able to see this guy once or twice and still have access to an additional one as a target for common sense. This addition is probably long overdue.


[[Colicky Dragonettes]]

Let's all unite in our hate for Tawny (when were not playing druid). We already want double fire on turn 3 and this guy not only sends a projectile but then also threatens to smash for 3. At the very least, firing off a projectile and then being able to defend against/trade with an opposing redcap is really nice. Worst case scenario we can use this units ping + an attack from our own redcap to make a "1 for 1" trade with pesky Cats or Bruins. Also don't forget this projectile can snipe a win from across the map when the opponent is at DD.


[[Quarrelsome Kobolds]]

Stole this from Steam Druid. I think we get the point here. Also similar reasoning to Dragonettes. Plus, give these guys a Trinket or 2 and tell me you're not in love. I dare you.


[[Saracen Raider]]

I had the slots available, and this card is amazing. Like vile imp, this addition is likely happening later than it should have.


[[Blaze]]

One of the best movement related spells. This helps us move and attack without being intercepted, getting extra damage in by attacking sites that are undefended and likely out of the way. In addition to that, it serves as secondary Bruin killer. Yes, Druid is a big problem for us.


[[The Great Famine]]

I had Cave In in this slot but Great Famine is among the absolute best removal cards in the game. They both deal well with Vampire and the fact that is also remains for an extra turn until there is nothing to kill means we have a chance to get an extra Drain in from the Witch but also deters opponents from moving in. This card is highly conducive to the decks game plan and I just wish I had put it in earlier.


[[Lava Flow]]

Death Door finisher, kills big beefy minions, deals with root spiders and also rips Bruin in half. I might replace this with a second Bury but I'm curious to try it.


[[Torshammar Trinket]]

Completely busted card in almost any deck, especially a super aggressive one. Compounded with the fact that we are draining every turn, this 1 extra damage provided is no joke and goes a long way.

Original Primer + Updates:


I love this Avatar. Everyone I speak to either really wants it to work or believes it to be among the worst, least supported Avatar the game currently has to offer. This may change drastically with the release of Gothic but until then we will use what we have available to us to make as big of a splash as possible with Frazetta's Witch.


The main goal is here is to stop playing Sites as soon as possible and start draining. Sounds familiar if you are used to playing with Sorcerer, but instead of trying to bury the opponent in card advantage, here we are just trying to bury them. The first few Drains feel slow but trust that they add up, especially when you start introducing the chip damage from your other units. The ideal site count is 4. Our top end is 5 and sometimes we may want to play two spells at the same time in the late game so 6 sites is the max. The best thing to do is stop at 3, Drain until you need the 4th site. Play it and repeat until 5 is needed. You do not need to lay down 4 sites consecutively unless you get screwed by the mulligan. Get to 3 and assess the board/your hand and only play more as needed, not simply because you can. If you need 4 sites in the first 5 turns, and in the absence of drawing sites via your units, a very strong line of play with this deck is to use your turn 4 to double draw. You play your first 3 sites and on turn 4: draw a spell for turn, tap the witch the draw a site and then play a 3 or less cost card. This sets up you to drop a site next turn and then start draining to the end game without missing a spell draw. Don't be tempted by the Tax effect. Generally speaking each time you Tax instead of Drain, you realize at the end of the game, should you lose, that this was typically where you went wrong. There is a time and place for Tax effects and it is called Death's Door. Speedrun your opponents life total to zero and then introduce the tax effect to make their remaining existence very difficult.


In order to achieve maximum effectiveness of The Witch's Drainage, we must rarely be in a position where we use a turn to tap her to draw a site. It is also highly highly recommended that you do not use a turns draw phase to draw a site due to her lack of card advantage, despite having access to [[Morgana le Fay]]. Every draw matters. Rely on [[Kettletop Leprechaun]] and [[frontier settlers]] to get you your extra Sites. [[Common sense]] for the Leprechaun is usually always a good early game play. The Leprechaun is also great at getting 2-4 additional damage in since opponents are sometimes hesitant to kill them and give you the site draw. Prioritize the Settlers if possible as they directly play a site for you. They are secretly (or blatantly) your most important early game card. Mulligan hard for them and protect them. [[Onyx Core]] goes the extra mile in this list espeically since it allows for a turn 2 settlers + drain from the Witch. Settlers can play your third site for you the following turn opening the path for your charge minions and allowing for yet another drain. In the event of Threshold deficiencies, you will need to do less favorable plays like the ones I advise against but these are exceptional situations. The [[ruby core]] helps get us to the extra red threshold we need without having to worry about too many desperate searches through our atlast.


This deck teeters between aggression and control but the plans do not interfere with each other because the controlling pieces help prolong your Avatar's life meaning she can keep draining in the absence of aggressive units/cards. [[Hillock Basilisk]] is a very annoying unit that locks down two squares and usually allows for at least 1-2 hits. It has 3 power which means the turn it swings you get a whopping 5 damage off your opponent's life (remember by this point we are definitely already or at the very least started Draining. [[Clamor of harpies]] is a card that I needed to play against a few times before understanding its power and value. Remember above how much importance I assigned to [[Frontier Settlers]]? Well harpies just smash this type of card and those exist in every deck. Then they also have Airborne so its another 5 damage swing on the follow up. highly recommend this card in your fire decks. [[Poison Nova]] and [[Cave-In]] do the thing they are here for, just efficient removal and clears the path for you as well. [[infiltrate]] is likely one of the best Aggro-Control crossover cards that exist so far. Being able to steal their minion so it can no longer pressure you and then also being able to smash one time with it really push our game plan acres forward. The rest of the magic is made up a tool box kit for [[Common Sense]] depending the situation you are in. [[Firebolts]], [[Minor explosion]] and [[Vile Imp]] help clear the way or just end the game when the opponent is at death's door.


Final Notes for the remaining cards not yet mentioned as they have highly important functions that deserve their own spotlight:


  • [[Amulet of Niniane]] + [[Root Spider]]:

We all know what spider is capable of throughout the game, with almost any deck. Its role here, alongside the Amulet is to make the witch untouchable (especially at Death's Door) while we utilize her various abilities. With the Amulet equipped and the Spider beneath her site, she is essentially untouchable. Your opponent will need multiple cards to get in and finish you off. Amulet is a flex spot though as it is technically a card that can be a dead draw. Im currently using [[Boudicca]] in its place.


  • [[War Horse]], [[Pudge Butcher]] and [[Earthquake]]:

War Horse serves the dual purpose of beating a charging beater but is also essential for moving our Immobile Pudge Butcher around to maximize the effectiveness of her Projectile. We are aiming to line the Pudge Mommy up with the opponent avatar so that we can deliver a hefty loss of 7 life (5 from pudge + 2 from the Witch drain)


  • [[Jihad]] and [[courtesan thais]]:

jihad is one of the most insane, powerhouse of a card I've played with or against in this game. Air dropping your aggressive units in their face while draining for 2 every turn is absolutely brutal. Courtesan Thais is our Death's Door finisher. Bring them to 0, slam our seductress and use their own spells against them to claim the Realm!


  • [[Queen of Midland]]:

Earth and Fire from what I have seen/experienced has the worst approach to card advantage as it focuses on other aspects of TCGs like removal and aggression. I have always had good success with the Queen of Midland and do feel like this deck reaches top tier status if we can keep our hand full. The drain for 2 feels like it is more impactful in this deck than the extra card draw provided by the Sorcerer so I wanted to fill the gap of extra cantrip/card draw with the Queen. Our hand will empty quickly, we will usually be sitting at 1-3 cards in hand which will more often than not trigger her and give us extra cards per turn while maintaining the ability to drop our opponents by an additional 2 life points each turn.


  • [[Vivien the Enchantress]]:

I started off strongly believing that the Witch is the best avatar for Vivien to be paired with but the more I play with this version, the more I feel like Vivien is better in a Tax Witch deck as opposed to an aggressive one. I write this two days after winning a game by virtue of being able to drain for 4 thanks to Vivien so I am now very confused with her privilege of occupying a card slot. I really want to add [[Boudicca]] to this deck and am wondering if Vivien gets cut for it. They share a threshold pip requirement but Boudicca costs 1 less which means we have less need for the extra site and she also provides a crazy amount of damage potential. Boudicca will likely make it in the deck no matter what, but I am still unsure if it comes at the cost of Vivien's slot.


27/08/2025: The Utility Slots:


As much as I believe this to be as close to a final list as well see before Gothic there are always flex slots. Here and in any other deck no matter how well it does. If you take this decks core you can proceed in two ways: fill flex slots with focused cards or fill them with utility cards. I've chose then Utility approach. The following cards are not required for the deck but are incredibly powerful in it, fulfilling their utility roles:

1) [[clamor of harpies]]

2) [[hillock basilisk]]

3) [[queen of midland]]


These are not pieces I am recommending to be cut from the list, I love the role they play and am very happy with their inclusion. That said, these are the cards I would cut in order to make the deck more streamlined and 100% focused. Off the top of my head the most likely cards that would take their place would be along the lines of [[ring of morrigan]], [[blaze]] and [[grim guisarme]].


10/09/2025: The Steam Druid Reality:


Early testing vs Steam Druid was honestly pretty positive. We are probably the weaker deck overall, but the games were nice. This past sunday we did exclusive testing vs Steam Druid (SD from now on) and it was a pretty miserable experience. Of course no deck or pilot is perfect, and off days happen but it still made me wonder if perhaps the matchup truly is that bad. One thing I kept noting was the fact that we have a decent amount of units with 2 or less attack that just get traded so freely into by the SD attackers like redcap. 3 power redcap killing our war horse and remaining in play is very scary. Not to mention when you start to bring the Trinket into the equation. Against other decks, efficient removal like Bury takes care of a lot of their 4 power beaters or life gain cards like Vampire. Against SD, water sites make bury cards totally meaningless until the unit enters our zone but by then perhaps the damage is done. Im not going to totally warp this deck around that one matchup, but I will be adding a maybe board of cards that can be swapped in if your meta is mostly water/SD/4+ power minion based.


Beta/AL Updates:

  • 05/06/2025: Without access to [[Highland Princess]] and considering the fact that I don't actually want to always see it, the [[Amulet of Niniane]] can be a bit awkward. Of course, there are moments where I wish It was still in the deck but it is not frequent enough to fight the decision to swap it out in favor of [[Boudicca]]. I am still pondering if the correct cut is [[Vivien the Enchantress]].
  • 19/06/2025: I removed [[Annual Fair]], [[Imperial road]] and [[Wizard's Den]] for [[Fields of Camlann]], [[rift valley]] and [[mirage]].
  • 21/07/2025: Despite the rule change only taking effect on Gothic's release and that we have no support yet for the extra 10 card collection, I decided to add to this deck to a 10 card sideboard that would turn the deck into 60/30 for preparation games. Added cards are: [[ring of morrigan]], [[onyx core]], 1 [[Saracen Raiders]], 2x [[vile imp]], [[crusade]], 1 [[common sense]] and 2x [[disintegrate]], 1 [[monstrous lion]]
  • 27/07/2025: I realized after many a games, [[philosopher's stone]] was only offering a 1 mana reduction, as I was not really double casting each turn. In this regard, [[Onyx core]] is doing the same 1 mana provision but also fixes threshold. It even allows for turn 2 draining if you have it with [[Frontier Settlers]]. Enabling a turn 3 [[pudge butcher]] is also no joke.
  • 06/08/2025: The sad, but perhaps necessary, day has arrived. [[Vivien the enchantress]] has been cut in favor of [[gigantism]]. Gigantism not being in the deck since day 1 is a big oversight. Card is clearly bonkers alone and even more so with an additional drain 2 from the Witch. Taking Vivien's slot translates to a card that costs 1 less, has 1 less threshold pip requirement and provides instant value once played. I have also removed [[caerleon upon-usk]] since it has water threshold in it and that makes no sense for a deck playing with [[root spider]]. [[Funeral Pyre]] has been doing nothing for me so I replaced it with Deserts. The sites shifting meant I could squeeze in more Ordinary sites which helps a ton vs [[Atlantean Fate]].
  • 08/08/2025: I've been thinking a lot about [[Grim Guisarme]]. It probably belongs in here but it hurts to cut anything else. It might end up replacing one of the extra 10 cards required for the deck once Gothic arrives. Otherwise the only card I can think to cut at this moment is 1 of the [[Clamor of Harpies]]. Will return to this after more thought.
  • 04/09/2025: I keep shifting between 3 [[red desert]] and 3 [[funeral pyre]] depending on the meta im playing in. Ideally I would like to keep all the deserts to deal with the abundance of Druid's out there but Funeral Pyre also works wonders vs Archi and Deathspeaker. That said, testings vs Archi indicate we might actually still be favored. I have won games where the Archi gains 14 life. Maybe I will just settle on not depending on Pyre since the MU might already be favorable. Lots to decide.
  • 03/10/2025: Im wondering if, considering the power level of Frontier Settlers, if we should put it back. The thought would be to replace the 4 Kettletops with 3 Frontier Settlers and either an Onyx Core to help with the threshold, or a Swiven Scout for extra information. If we go the swiven scout route, I might also drop 1 Common Sense for a 2nd Scout. 07/10/2025: Decided to give the Settlers + Core a try. Will Swap out the Leprechauns and report back.
  • 17/10/2025: I was trying to make a point in the past by not playing [[ring of morrigan]] but, similar to a comment I heard about using a crosshair in DOOM speed running: "If I dont use the tool that others are using, then I am the cause of my own setbacks"
  • 20/10/2025: this one is awkward because a) [[frontier settlers]] is among the best cards in the deck as an early game card and b) [[kettletop leprechaun]] is better than [[land surveyor]] because of the extra damage... however.... we are so desperate to not waste a turn drawing sites and sometimes we really need a site immediately that I am now considering if maybe the 4 slots dedicated to onyx+settlers or leprechaun, should in fact just be given to Land Surveyor....
  • 24/10/2025: okay the SCG Melbourne finals were posted recently and I saw then filthiest sinkhole line and now all I want to do is put 2 sinkhole in every aggro deck I have. This is actually very painful because this build would absolutely love to make that same play with sinkhole but sinkhole also goes against what we are inherently looking to do. It causes us to lose a site which means one more turn of drawing and then tapping the witch to regain that site. That is 1-2 self forced turns on not draining. I am writing this to imply I'm still considering the plan because it's possible the upside of sinkholing in the same way displayed in that game might actually net us more damage than we lose by having to draw and play more sites.
  • 29/10/2025: decided that I wanted more ordinary sites because I live in constant fear of Atlantean Fate. also Druid and Tawny are really annoying so I decided to replace Vesuvius and River of Flame for 2 more deserts. Essentially I replaced two "low % high ceiling" sites for 2 consistent sites. If you don't face these same issues then you can ignore this update.
  • 01/11/2025: Land Surveyor has been feeling very very good. The impact is truly felt when you top deck this type of card on turn 4/5/6 and he draws you your 5th site. You begin to see the difference with its value compared to Leprechaun. Getting sites 4 and/or 5 immediately is seeming more important than the extra power. Will keep testing but it's feeling nice.

deckinfo.name: It Takes a Village (F)
deckinfo.primer:
The idea for the deck came from seeing what the two best Avatars (arguably) in the current format do:

  1. [[Necromancer]]: Play every turn with the benefit of always being able to curve out with a [[Skeleton]] for extra value
  2. [[Pathfinder]]: Ability to draw a spell every turn while putting a site into play for "free"


Fire splash version:


[[Redmane Hyena]] mainboard and in the collection to address [[Archimago]] or other cemetery strategies. Between [[Assorted Animals]] and [[Silver Bullet]], you have several ways to access [[Redmane Hyena]] when needed.


[[Funeral Pyre]] gives extra cemetery hate while providing Fire threshold.


[[Poison Nova]] gives you the ability to destroy minions on Water sites. There are a surprising amount of Earth minion spellcasters ([[Arjaro Exorcist]], [[Mover of Mountains]], [[Paladins of Bazia]]) that are able to cast [[Poison Nova]]. [[Silver Bullet]] also allows even the most unassuming [[Foot Soldiers]] or [[Skeleton]] to suddenly wipe the board. Because you are controlling the [[Poison Nova]] you are able to limit the collateral damage greatly.


[[Balor of the Evil Eye]] is an excellent finisher that can also destroy a submerged [[Coy Nixie]], opposing burrowed [[Root Spider]], damage an [[Imposter]] out of [[Pathfinder]] mask, and remove Wards on a crucial turn.


[[Searing Truth]] in the collection helps burst your opponent down or finish while on Death's Door.


[[Onslaught]] is the card that has overperformed the most for me. It is excellent after a [[Guards!]] but your minions ignoring silence, disable, and immobile is relevant in many ways. [[Babbling Brook]], [[Quagmire]], etc. no longer stop you. [[Pudge Butcher]] is now able to attack and/or reposition. [[Sister Stefánia]] is no longer silencing your own minions so you are able to cast [[Onslaught]] and an [[Archangel Michael]] and now he can still have his genesis ability as well as his ward that turn. Another relevant thing that Onslaught can do is give your [[Root Spider]] charge in case you need to quickly disable a site full of blockers or important minions.


[[Scorched Earth]] allows you to do some niche things. Destroying everything at the sites you destroy is relevant because it gives you another card to destroy auras, artifacts (against Avatars like [[Battlemage]] and [[Bladedancer]]), and minions. [[Scorched Earth]] also gives you a spell to destroy your own [[Roots of Yggdrasil]]. A niche thing you can do is destroy your own sites so your opponent can't attack it. It has happened in several games where I destroy 2-4 of my own sites in the late game so my opponent is unable to attack the sites they thought they were going to be able to attack and put me to Death's Door. [[Geomancer]] is able to replace adjacent rubbles that are created by [[Scorched Earth]] and the tech explained above makes it worth the cost.

deckinfo.name: Scatter the Frog
deckinfo.primer:
Deck Philosophy

This is a Midrange–Control hybrid built around Tempo Manipulation, Positional Advantage, and Soft-Control rather than raw aggression or hard lockdown. The deck doesn’t try to end the game quickly; instead, it aims to outscale opponents through board control, flexible answers, and high-impact Unique threats.


Pros & Cons of [[Battlemage]]

Pros:

  • Highest starting power of any Avatar
  • Can't be targeted by hard removal spells i.e. ([[Bury]], [[Drown]], [[Disintegrate]])
  • Great target to hold and keep artifacts due to resiliency
  • Deceptively beefy when the board is clear and can start attacking sites


Cons:

  • Weak to direct damage, especially against Charge Minions and damage Spells like [[Firebolts]], [[Arc Lightning]], [[Arcane Barrage]]
  • Requires mobility from spells to get around the realm, no movement spells = Snailmage
  • Starts to lose advantage against draw based Avatars by turn 5-6 i.e. [[Sorcerer]], [[Geomancer]], [[Pathfinder]]
  • Hindered greatly by sites like [[Troll Bridge]], [[Gnome Hollows]], and [[Perilous Bridge]]



SPELLS


ARTIFACTS

[[Aquamarine Core]] and [[Amethyst Core]] allows you to begin moving your [[Battlemage]] earlier due to not tapping as often for Sites. These artifacts accelerate your deck and help with outpacing your opponent and being able to play your 5-6 cost power cards a turn early.

[[Ring of Morrigan]] is still one of the powerhouse staple Uniques of the game. This gives [[Battlemage]] a damage boost and can turn the tempo around immediately upon being played, especially with the Magics that are available within Air and Water. Because you will most likely be around the center of the board or on your opponents side of the realm, you'll be able to ping anything for much needed life gain.

[[Toolbox]] is the way we get to access our Collection. For non-[[Imposter]] decks, [[Toolbox]] is one of the only way Collections can be accessed and are very much another staple in the game now because of how useful the Collection is and being able to have a useful card in almost every matchup and board state.

[[Dank Omphalos]] essentially turns your Avatar into [[Sorcerer]] lite. You get access to another Spellcaster on the board which is a great way to counter [[Sturmgeist]] since it can cast the Spells in your own hand. It replaces itself at the end of your turn via card draw and is similar to [[Morgana le Fay]] but without the Threshold requirement and is also a bit more resilient since it can only be removed via artifact removal. Where you play this Monument is very important since it can only cast Minion spells at it's location but you also want to keep it away from a potential [[Toolbox]] into [[Dispel]], [[Disenchant]], or [[Bury]]. Region based removal such as [[Drown]] and [[Bury]] are cards that can potentially deal with Omphalos's since it would have to cast Minions in the same region. While Omphalos's cannot cast artifacts, artifacts have no element, it is still an amazing card that gets you amazing card advantage on the board and only gets better each turn it stays on the board.



AIR


MINIONS

With [[Ring of Morrigan]] being so strong it's important to get this artifact out as often as possible, and [[Highland Princess]] helps us tutor our favorite 1 cost artifact. While there are 2 other options to take with [[Highland Princess]], you will almost always be grabbing [[Ring of Morrigan]]. [[Bane of Aventis]] at worst is a 4 power bear for 4 mana. At best it can completely flip the board state by stealing your opponent's Ward minions like [[Sacred Stag]] and almost all of the different Order minions from Gothic. Game ending minion when your opponent's deck relies on Ward such as [[Savior]]. [[Hounds of Ondaros]] is a very durable unit because it doesn't die to [[Earthquake]], [[Atlantean Fate]], or other displacement type spells. [[Hounds of Ondaros]] also provides extra utility by revealing nearby Stealth units such as [[Morgana La Fey]] and [[Aino]].


MAGICS

[[Grapple Shot]] is your bread and butter in this deck because it accomplishes your main goals, additional movement and extra damage. Being able to drag your [[Battlemage]] across the board to deal direct damage is great because the struck unit does not strike back and your [[Battlemage]] is free to attack again. You would normally reserve this for extra damage on your opponent, but if using [[Grapple Shot]] as a removal spell keeps you ahead on the board it's better to use it for that purpose. [[Whirling Blades]] is the big brother to [[Grapple Shot]]. It's a great midgame Magic removal spell that can deal with multiple units and get some extra damage in without needing to tap your unit. Next we have [[Browse]]. [[Browse]] is one of Air's strongest spells that will almost guarantee a new useful card in hand. [[Feast for Crows]], another OP card in the right hands. At worst this Spell lets you see your opponents hand and entire Spellbook, which is immense value for only 3 mana, but if you have experience in a plethora of matchups you'll have a higher success rate of naming relevant cards. A great Spell to name against non-[[Imposter]] decks is [[Toolbox]], essentially removing all cards in your opponent's Collection for the rest of the game, a potential 13 card removal spell. Finally we're running one copy of [[Arcane Barrage]]. The deck typically gets above 6-7 mana each game so having a flexible damage Spell that can be used to potentially door your opponent once they're below 10 life is a great option.


AURAS

[[The Black Plague]] is an amazing Minion removal Aura that goes around Regions and Stealth that also rewards being able to displace your opponent's Minions which the deck has many ways to.



WATER

The deck is very Water heavy so most of the cards do similar things or play similar roles


MINIONS

For value minions we're running a few different ones. [[Adept Illusionist]] is probably the strongest turn 2 play you can do in this deck because of the recurring value this minion can provide. It's a Spellcaster so it can cast your position limited Magics, it thins out your deck by grabbing the second copy and being able to summon it nearby, and is an amazing chump blocker when you have the second copy online. [[Polar Explorers]] allows you to set up defensive sites and not commit to the middle of the board too early, and allows you to go around your opponent's defenses. A great minion in this meta where defensive sites are common. [[Aino]] is an amazing 3 cost Minion that has inherent movement and evasion. It's important to play this as early as you can to start getting your damage. [[Lugbog Cat]] at 4-power and the ability to be played on an opponent's water site in this Water heavy meta is a great overrate minion at just 3 mana. Great beater but with many Water decks that don't rely on damage, using sites like [[Thin Ice]], it's important to know when and where to play [[Lugbog Cat]] to be able to get at least 1 instance of damage with it. Next we have [[Order of the Sacred Oak]]. A durable Minion with Ward that provides some much needed protection for your defensive sites. [[Ruler of Thul]] is still your All-Star minion in this deck. It pumps not only your minions but also your [[Battlemage]] +1 power and connects the top and bottom realm for your units only, allowing your units to rush to your opponent's sites/units in their backline. On top of this, [[Ruler of Thul]] has charge. So he provides an immediate benefit in damage, mobility, and buffs. [[Failed Mutation]] gives the deck some better early game being a durable body that can't be targeted or damaged by Magic. [[Sacred Stag]] is another durable Minion meant to stabilize your early game and provide a beefy body that provides favorable trades and potential defense for your Sites.


Now we move on to a few disruption minions. [[Coy Nixie]] is the new queen of Water right now and many times can fully turn off any early aggression your opponent may have if you have an early [[Thin Ice]] on the board. She's also a great unit to break Ward without having to spend a card in hand, and can also be used aggressively forcing your opponent's Avatar to step somewhere you can leverage more damage away from potential blockers. Another disruptor minion is [[Abaddon Succubus]]. She's a great minion when paired with multiple movement type effects you may have on the field and being able to heal and deal damage to minions makes her a great option for removal and much needed life gain. Next for disruption/removal we're running [[Lacuna Entity]]. Amazing tempo Minion that can ignores Regions when pulling weaker Minions and can be used to banish a potentially problematic minion by pulling it into the Void. Great targets are Minions like [[Rasputin]], [[Adept Illusionist]], [[Coy Nixie]], and many more. You can also use it to pull your own Minions so it's a very flexible card. [[Lord of Lies]] is both disruption and high value, being able to provide high bursts of damage and being able to force nearby Units to fight. Great target for [[Whirling Blades]] and [[Grapple Shot]] and potentially being able to get 18 damage. Finally for disruption we're running [[The Green Knight]]. Sturdy Minion with 7 toughness that forces your opponent's Minions to attack it, potentially clearing your opponents board with proper placement.


Finally for some defensive utility we're running [[Archangel Raphael]]. Being able either Strike your opponent's Avatar or Ward your own is amazing value for 5 mana and having a 4 power Airborne minion that also has Ward makes great during the midgame.



MAGICS

[[Pollimorph]] is meant for minions that are harder to kill, i.e. airborne. This spell also banishes the minion and cannot be interacted with later on in the game via [[Deathspeaker]]/[[Pillar of Zeiros]]. Next for some more disruption we have [[Swap]]. Very flexible card to reposition Artifacts and Minions, and also potentially steal [[Toolbox]] or [[Ring of Morrigan]]. Can also be used to reposition an Omphalos, potentially shutting off your opponent's Omphalos since it can only cast Minions while on an Ally Site. [[Plague of Frogs]] is a high value card that provides a myriad of options either with placement, artifact holders, blockers, or even potential attackers with [[Ruler of Thul]]. Another amazing Unique Water Magic the deck runs is [[Mesmerism]] being able to steal an opponent's Minion and swinging the tempo and board state around in your favor. Finally for some AOE removal we're running 2 copies of [[Call of the Sea]]. With the majority of our sites being Water, and utilizing the multiple movement effects of the deck, we'll almost always be able to get full value with this Magic. It also ignores Ward and Stealth so it's a great way to devastate your opponent's board.


AURAS

[[Atlantean Fate]] is arguably still the strongest Water card in the game and is a great finisher card against opponents that keep their Avatars in sites like [[Free City]] or [[Gnome Hollows]]. The threshold conversion from [[Atlantean Fate]] is also a game finisher, but it is important to keep in mind that this Aura only affects Non-Ordinary Sites.



DUAL THRESHOLD


MINIONS

[[Sir Tom Thumb]] is great for a recurring blocker as well as a potential enabler of your [[Thin Ice]]. Sites like [[Mountain Peaks]] allows us to consistently be able to play this Minion on turn 2.

[[Blue Knight]] provides us with lance artifact tokens. These are single use tokens that give the bearer +1 power on their next strike and gives them first strike as well. This is a great combat trick for your minions and especially for [[Battlemage]] because it can help preserve your life and even allow you to still attack the enemy Avatar while you're both at Death's Door. With less [[Vile Imps]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] being played in main boards, [[Blue Knight]] is in a great position that also doesn't get submerged by [[Thin Ice]] and [[Coy Nixie]].

[[Sir Pelleas]] is possibly our strongest 3 Cost Minion because of it's movement and evasion. Being able to block and attack most of the board is extremely strong and the 4 attack power allows it to trade into most Minions. This paired with [[Floodplain]] can help connect your Body of Water and unlock additional movement.


MAGICS

[[Scatter]] is the main disruption Magic this deck has. I prefer this over [[Swap]] because it has a higher ceiling for disruption being able to push everything at a Location in different directions, including Avatars and even Auras. Possibly the most versatile card in the list because it can be used for some extra movement or even to steal an artifact your opponent is carrying since things are moved one at a time.



SITES


Air

[[Lone Tower]], [[Gothic Tower]], and [[Dark Tower]] provide an additional 1 mana on the turn they are played if it's the only copy among your sites. These sites are amazing with the [[Battlemage]] game plan since you get to play cards ahead of the natural curve of the game. Cutting down on Towers in general to be able to play a few more Air utility sites.

[[Mountain Peaks]] is part of the new series of double Threshold sites Gothic introduced. This helps activate our threshold with less sites required, potential turn 2 [[Cloud City]] and helps the deck feel like [[Elementalist]] at times. It also enables the deck to keep more Water sites in the starting hand.

[[Wuthering Heights]] is probably the strongest Air site in this deck because of how well it synergizes with other defensive sites and disruption effects, and also offers additional movement to our own Minions.

[[Perilous Bridge]] is a great defensive site that can stop aggro in it's tracks and force your opponent to play around it all game. While it also blocks our own Units, Minions like [[Polar Explorers]] and [[Ruler of Thul]] allow us to go very heavy into early defense without sacrificing potential aggression.

[[Cloud City]] is an extremely versatile site that can give you many options throughout the state of the game due to the mobility it can offer. It's also a great Site to hinder [[Enchantress]] decks since it leaves a void in its place once moved.


Water

[[Deep Sea]] similar to [[Mountain Peaks]], allowing a few earlier threshold hungry cards like [[Mesmerism]] and [[Archangel Raphael]] to be played easier.

[[Floodplain]] provides an additional Water threshold if necessary, allowing you to have a low site count and still being able to play those crucial high Water threshold Spells. [[Floodplain]] also creates a threat to any deck that uses burrowed minions, i.e. [[Root Spider]], since it can flood an adjacent site and kill any burrowed minion at that site. We can also use the Flood effect to play [[Lugbog Cat]] atop an Adjacent enemy Site and give our [[Sir Pelleas]] additional options for movement. Paired with [[Deep Sea]], the deck essentially has 6 double Water Threshold Sites.

[[Babbling Brook]] is an amazing Water card from AL. This Site definitely feels like [[Quagmire]] but with a lot more utility because it's able to remove Stealth and Ward from nearby minions. This can also cancel out your opponent's [[Infiltrate]] because it gets cancelled whenever Stealth is removed from the infiltrated minion. This Site also helps with better establishing your next turn and being able to stop your opponent's early aggression.

[[River Rapids]] is similar to [[Wuthering Heights]] because it provides extra synergy with movement as well as being able to push Minions onto an adjacent Site, a great Water Site that can be played up front as a pseudo-defensive Site.

[[Troll Bridge]] is one of the actual defensive Sites that synergizes extremely well with the decks inherent ability to move units on the board. It discourages opponents from playing and moving Units into it, and also provides potential removal during our own turn if we can push an opponent into it.

[[Thin Ice]] is another defensive Site that rewards positioning and disruption and providing extremely efficient removal. This is one of the main forms of Site based removal that you can use to great advantage with Minions like [[Coy Nixie]], Sites like [[Wuthering Heights]] and [[River Rapids]], and Magics like [[Scatter]] and [[Swap]]. You can use your Submerge Minions to activate [[Thin Ice]] at the end of your turn as a form of evasion and removal as well.


Dual Threshold

[[Lighthouse]] is the only Site in the deck that provides Water and Air so they're very important in helping smooth out your threshold requirements during the early turns. Ideally keep one in your starting hand.


Non-Threshold

[[The Void]] is the only non-Threshold Site in this list and acts as another defensive Site that can be used as removal by pushing or pulling your opponent's Minions into it. You can also enter this Site with your Avatar and being protected against attacks from non-Voidwalk minions. Your opponent can also use this Site to their advantage as well, so be wary of having your own Minions being forced into [[The Void]].


Starting Hand Tierlist (Not Legible on Mobile) WIP

S-Tier: ____________A-Tier: ____________B-Tier:

[[Sir Pelleas]] ______________[[Daperyll Vampire]] _____________ [[Magic Missiles]]

[[Polar Explorers]] ______________[[Shrink]]

[[Grapple Shot]] _________________[[Pollimorph]]

[[Gyre Hippogriffs]] ______________[[Screaming Skull]]

[[Ruler of Thul]] _________________[[Questing Beast]]

[[Ring of Morrigan]] ______________[[Disenchant]]

[[Feast for Crows]] _______________[[Blue Knight]]

[[Lugbog Cat]] ___________________[[Atlantean Fate]]

[[Browse]] ______________________[[Sugarplum Pixies]]

[[Highland Princess]] ____________[[Wizard's Den]]

[[Phase Assassin]] _______________[[Cloud City]]

[[Mask of Mayhem]] ______________[[Observatory]]

[[Torshammar Trinket]] __________[[Merlin's Tower]]

[[Pond]] _________________________[[Troll Bridge]]

[[Lookout]]_______________________[[Tactical Move]]

[[Floodplain]]

ANY TOWERS

ANY MULTI THRESHOLD SITES

ANY CORES


The deck is always a work in progress, and as of now this is the current version I play exclusively.


Leave a comment if you have any suggestions and have fun!!!
