deckinfo.name: Vel'Koz
deckinfo.primer:
Currently testing double Vanishment + Witherwing + Tombstone Wardens


Setup

------------------------------------------------------------------

Go second if you win the roll. Scry advantage allows you to hold onto Forsaken Crypts/No threshold sites more confidently. Most starting hands are perfectly fine to use as is. Adtonitum starting is very risky cheese play; it's better to draw it later. I would'nt recommend it unless you pull all the One-Shot w/Kill Secure cards starting hand. Thunderstorms interfere with Phase Assassin/Nightgaunts early - pick one or the other for turn 3-5 agro. Hippogriffs, all uniques but Adtonitum always good. Hexham Haunt, Recurring Specter, Black Plague + Temple of Moloch is fun and forces limited opponet counter play.



Mulligans

------------------------------------------------------------------

One-Shot w/Kill Secure - Adtonitum, Silver Bullet (Whirling Blades), Static Servant, Amethyst Core, City of Glass, Spore Spouts, Beacon/Tower/Ghost Town

Strength: Adtonitum deals 18 damage with Whirling Blades

Weakness: Infiltrate/opponets turn after casting Adtonitum

------------------------------------------------------------------

Minion Agro - Forsaken Crypt, Open Masoleum, Phase Assassin, Gibbous Nightgaunts, Gyre Hippogriffs

Strength: card advantage, constant board state pressure

Weakness: Earthquake, Poison Nova, AOE removal

------------------------------------------------------------------

Magic dump - Lightning Bolt/Magic Missiles, Murder of Crows, Skeleton Mage, Merlin, Merlin's Tower, Orb of Baal Berith, Cloud City, Geistwood

Strength: 16 Lightning Bolt casts with 3x Skeleton Mage + Orb + 1 dead Skeleton Mage on Geistwood

Weakness: Undefended sites

------------------------------------------------------------------

Anti-minion econ - Hexham Haunts, Recurring Specter, Black Plague, Poisonous Dagger, Temple of Moloch, Silver Bullet (Evil Presence), Toolbox (Teleport)

Strength: Hexham Haunts 2 damage per turn for 1 mana, Recurring Specter 1 for 1 mana - spark cannot be defended

Weakness: Dealing damage to enemy avatar, Teleport/Blink or tap to move needed

------------------------------------------------------------------

Lightning control - Thunderstorm, Lightning Bolt, Black Plague, Displace, Manor at Daperyll Hill, Bane of Aventis, Toolbox/Silver Bullet (Disenchant)

Strength: Displace + Manor = free kill + 3 health

Weakness: Opponet healing

------------------------------------------------------------------

9-Volt Battery - Poisonous Dagger, Ring of Morrigan, Blink/Gift of Raven, Murder of Crows, Arcane Barrage, Browse, Toolbox/Silver Bullet (Teleport, Zap!, Poisonous Dagger)

Strength: everything dies except adjacent voidwalk in the void - need to tap to play site and must take minion damage 1 turn

Weakness: Mana curve, need 6 or 7 sites minimum



Start

------------------------------------------------------------------

Hang out on starting site for most of the game to defend your sites with spark. Play Assassins, Nightgaunts, Specters, Haunts, and Masoleums early and forward. Layer in Forsaken Crypts for Ghouls along the way. Hold onto your anti-minion spells and use them after their minions get in spark range. Hover at 5 sites with 1 Spore Spouts and Static Servant in hand, then start blasting.


You want pairs of 2 cost and 3 cost double air threshold spells to remove 4 power minion threats. After you play 6 sites/have 6 mana per turn, use Bullet/Toolbox to Teleport on enemy Avatars location and spark them each turn. Kill all enemy 4 or more power minions immediately, Lightning Bolt + Static Servant + Spouts. Don't waste Murder of Crows/Arcane Barrage/Browse until you can get a good spark off with it, like vs 6 power minion or wards. Hold onto Static Servant and Spore Spouts for Deaths Door kill secure. 7 mana needed for Silver Bullet > Toolbox > Grappleshot kill secure. If you end up drawing an Orb, these spells can go a long way. A triple cast of Murder of Crows (once off Orb) can spark for 6 and kill all their 3 power minions with 1 card. Pay 2 mana double Blink draw 2 spark for 2 feels very nice.



Deck Theory

------------------------------------------------------------------

My attempt to bring Vel'koz to Sorcery Contested Realm. Vel'koz is a League of Legends glass cannon champion relying on speed, mid range CC control, and long range poke but he dies if anyone touches him or if he misses his projectiles. Spells cast by Vel'Koz that hit an enemy create a stack counter and at 3 counters True Damage is applied. This is somewhat mechanically similar to Sparkmage - his spark ability scales damage with air threshold spells cast. Random effects determined by die rolls will help bring back that feel of physical dexterity from League into Sorcery.


Q -> Lightning Bolt, Magic Missiles, Spectral Stalker (Mana regen swapped for health regen with ring)

W -> Murder of Crows, Thunderstorm, Skeleton Mage

E -> Disenchant, Black Plague, Displace

R -> Arcane Barrage, Adtonitum, Grappleshot, Zap!

Passive -> Poisonous Dagger, Sparkmage ability

Flash/Ghost -> Teleport, Blink

Twin Shadows -> Recurring Specter, Hexham Haunts


Good:

Avatars cannot burrow or submerge so you can always spark an enemy Avatar nearby (except when they are on The Void), which allows you to engage diagonally to help dodge projectiles + 2 step away magic damage spells. The spark is not magic damage (it is air damage) AND the spark cannot target your own Sparkmage, so enemy Avatars using Kythera Mechanism, Amulet of Niniane, Goswhit Helm, etc cannot prevent the spark damage in 1v1 on the same site. The best they can do is put a blocker on top of themselves to help randomize the spark.

Bad:

You're limited to 1 spark per turn. The spark requires tapping so he has to get nearby without tapping to move, which requires Blink or Teleport. Card draw is also difficult to obtain and if you use all your spells early, you cannot win and will run out of gas. Without Arc Lightning or Dagger, dealing 6+ damage to enemy minions is hard without 6 mana for double Murder of Crows cast.



Fun tricks

------------------------------------------------------------------

Play Cloud City on your avatar. Then play 5 sites in front of your Cloud City like this.

[ ] [ ] [o] [ ] [ ]

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

[x] [x] [x] [x] [x]

[ ] [ ] [x] [ ] [ ]

Don't play 6+ sites and shift the Cloud City left and right. This allows for significant board state advantage. It gives Sparkmage +1 movement, and creates a void sandwich that prevents most minions from attacking and spellcasting. You can camp in this position, gain card advantage, Orb it up with a Geistwood.


Poisionous Dagger and Ring of Morrigan are your best friends. Dagger gives Sparkmages ability lethal damage so only 1 damage from a spark will kill any minion. Ring with dagger gives the ring lethal damage as well. When you first play the ring and dagger, it doesn't activate lethal ping until you play an additional spell. For example: If you play dagger first then ring, ring doesnt trigger at all - if you play ring first then dagger, you do get 1 ring trigger but it executes before lethal is applied to bearer, so it only deals 1 damage.


You can draw for 2 infinitely with Pnakotic Manuscript, Recurring Specter, and Wild Hunt/Horen of Caerleon.. for 1 mana with Major City - Recurring Specter will die from 99% of cards you draw (Arcane Barrage 0 cost) then can be bounced back due to his passive ability. If you have Ring of Morrigan and Major City near Sparkmage, you can infinitely ping your Recurring Specters (you need both specters, you cant ping the same minion you cast with the ring) to gain +1 spark damage for 1 mana to "charge up" his spark - make sure to have 1 Teleport and zap zap.


Merlin's Tower can cast the spell underground and target burrowed units and is a spellcaster for the turn it enters play.


Use Recurring Specter and Black Plague to infinitely keep Black Plague in play, summoning the specter each turn to satisfy the damage proc of plague.

deckinfo.name: Cruel Waters
deckinfo.primer:
Best [[Waveshaper]] I’ve built so far.




Very similar list to my [[Spellslinger]] (BUT SCARY GOOD). I based CRUEL on that list but Slinger has a little higher ceiling and a few more huge minions alot of fun, bigger bombs but less control.

(full primer update in [[Spellslinger]] recently Feb.27.2026 here https://curiosa.io/decks/cm7mf7rrm001ele03o1xweti9 a lot of similar cards and playing this deck like slinger is pretty much how I play CRUEL)


Going second seems to be a good idea most games getting the extra card draw and scry can be really helpful


I will update this soon to but man these primers are HUGE now lol




2025 PERSONAL ACHIEVMENTS:




August 2025 - EU Sorcerers at the Core WINNER!

Just found out I won the league for the month of August! Happy too cause my boy Faces won that league before and now we’re tied !!


6/9 - 14th at SorceryCon Unland Cup missed top had a lot of weird hands. Should of topped tho


5/14 - Won my locals again recently thought I'd throw that in here too


4/19 Top 5 Season 7 of League!

Barely lost to an [[Archimago]] (who won the whole league btw nbd) just didnt draw my wincons at all after dooring him crazy early unfortunate but thats how it goes

(Apparently the first ever [[Waveshaper]] in top 8 possibly even top 16 for the online league? Very cool! Top 5 insane to me! Need to win a big one.)


3/5 Won my locals at GG pretty competitive scene! Deck surprised me first time even bringing it out to a comp! Tuning up now!




GUEST PILOTS:

(Decent amount of people playing the deck would love to hear the how, what, when, and where anyone else does with this list!!)


@LRowe SCGcon Atlanta 12th 4-2

"I played a version of this, had to make changes based on card availability(don't own all the cards) at SCGcon Atlanta and went 4-2 (12th/43) was super fun."






MATCH UPS (Us vs Them)


( need to test a lot more especially with Gothic and really think about certain matchups - will add more soon )







OPENING HAND


Spells

Draw 3 spells and pretty much always mulligan 3 of them unless you already have a ramp card in hand such as [[Mix Aqua]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]] or [[Aquamarine Core]] you're looking hard for these opening hand. If you already have one you mulligan whatever else looking for bigger cards to play or more ramp. Mainly something big to play to apply pressure when possible.

Possible cards to keep in hand besides ramp are game changers like [[Atlantean Fate]], [[Ring of Morrigan]], [[Ruler of Thul]] and definitely [[Mesmerism]].

[[Lugbog Cat]] can be a keep card very strong early game but still nice to dig into the deck for bombs



Sites

Almost entirely water sites so not super important what the sites are early as long as you have 2 water sites in hand should be fine.

Always nice to see [[Troll Bridge]] or any river site early.

If you already have a perfect opening hand you can always mulligan sites searching for a [[Maelstrom]] or [[River Rapids]]. Can be so strong for control if you play your sites in a “T” every pull is to the middle and enemies can be tapped down there easily. Also you can play minions back row and start of turn pull them forward into attacking range. Gives allys a little more survivability and can be a sneaky way to attack unsuspecting opponents!


Early river sites are looking for ramp cards or something big to play with a ramp card already in hand.

Late game use the rivers to find a final kill spell. [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Ice Lance]] are probably the best options but you can also look for [[Questing Beast]], [[Mesmerism]], [[Truesight Crossbow]], or maybe [[Riptides]] when needed.






TIPS/TRICKS?


Try not tap down with the [[Waveshaper]] ability until you have at least 4 sites getting behind on mana early is very hard to recover from


I normally prefer to go second for the added draw (especially in league with the added scry right now) but sometimes it can come in handy.

if you have a [[Mesmerism]] and go second an opponent can build their board big fast by turn 4 and instead I can take away the threat become the threat and push back right away especially if they just played a big minion, on my turn its summoning sickness is already gone and starts doing damage.

[[Mesmerism]] is just so good will win the game most of the time! Use it wisely!







EVERY CARD AND WHAT I THINK




AVATAR:


[[Waveshaper]]

The ability to tap down opponent minions is extremely strong. Enemy minions with submerge not being affected can sometimes be tricky but most decks dont run submerge minions luckily. A flooded enemy site provides protection for ally minions from bury spells and gives a site to attack if minions are restricted by waterbound. BIG note is the flood ability says NEAR so body of water doesn’t necessarily have to be connected to flood and tap down!


SPELLBOOK:




• AURA


[[Atlantean Fate]] (x1)

Can be a game winner! Setting an opponents threshold to water only can hurt bad, especially if they don't run water spells. Just be careful ordinary sites not being affected can be tricky to play around at times. Can be a huge buff for any [[Anui Undine]].






• ARTIFACTS


[[Aquamarine Core]] (x1)

Always nice to see early. Helps get the deck running a little faster. Simple and effective.


[[Mix Aqua]] (x2)

RAMP O’CLOCK! Everything is a water spell and can always use a mix. Really hoping to see some ramp early for some big plays to apply pressure whenever possible. Usually a good idea to wait to crack a mix until there is a 5-6 cost water spell needing to be cast but in an emergency these can come in handy to combo out whatever is needed.


[[Ring of Morrigan]] (x1)

Such a win more card. Can gain just enough life to outlast opponent and helps with trades or removal in general. Great to see for a Deaths Door final avatar hit. Keep hidden until door if game doesnt need it. Ring hate makes sense and is growing.


[[Four Waters of Paradise]] (x1)

RAMP! Try to save for bigger costing/threshold spells. Always on the hunt for this card to cast heavier combos.


[[Pnakotic Manuscript]] (x1)

Simple draw support can be used on smaller minions mainly especially a twin [[Adept Illusionist]] but with all the river abilities (such as [[Winter River]]) it can be easy to know what will survive the draw or if youll only take a small amount of damage to the avatar. Playing against another water deck [[Anui Undine]] underwater becomes a great option for manuscript or even [[The Green Knight]] with so much defense.

+ FROGS LOVE TO READ! [[Plague of Frogs]] or [[Tadpole Pool]] combo so well for easy draw engine


[[Truesight Crossbow]] (x1)

Mainly for when an opponent is at deaths door, can be a sneaky way to avoid blockers with a snipe. Gives some extra range to waterbound creatures! Seeing this late game is preferred but if you see it early play it on your avatar and wait it out. Avatars gain some range and can target stealth minions with spells!!! (can be big for kill spells or [[Mesmerism]]). My favorite tech has been strategically placing either [[Plague of Frogs]] or my minions on board, in a way so that I can run a [[Truesight Crossbow]] from my avatar to whatever minion can tap in range for game.


[[Grim Guisarme]] (x2)

The updated rules absolutely MAKES THIS DECK EVEN MORE BRUTAL. Can swing for door at any point almost a must add. Save for door in most cases




• MINIONS


[[Fenvale Muse]] (x1)

With all the rivers this extends the dig for any of the ramp cards [[Mix Aqua]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]] or [[Aquamarine Core]]. Could be (x2) but I dont like to many 0 power non token creatures so only 1 for tech when seen. Great option for [[Shapeshift]].


[[Adept Illusionist]] (x2)

A staple in any water deck for me. Just feels like so much value, constant chump blocks or [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] draw. He is also a spellcaster so he can bring out his buddy ol’ pal and start casting [[Ice Lance]] or [[Mesmerize]] from farther for game.


[[Tide Niads]] (x1)

Tech card. Can help waterbound minions move around easier like [[Floodplain]] but keeps the site flooded on opponents turn. Extends [[Waveshaper]]s ability range and is a great target for [[Shapeshift]].


[[Fey Changeling]] (x2)

Helpful for blocker removal and can set an opponent back a turn if they play some huge minion. Just send it back to the hand and continue on about your business. Sending certain genesis cards back to hand can be tricky so watch out for those. Great target for [[Shapeshift]].


[[Lugbog Cat]] (x3)

It’s extremely hard not to put 3 of these in every water deck. Just value. 3 cost 4 power can cast to any water site. Cast to an enemy back row water site if possible or even better back row on a [[Pristine Paradise]] and just attack.


[[Nelly Longarms]] (x1)

Can be easy removal especially against bigger minions. Normally just a deterrent threat defending her range of sites. If she isnt taken care of can be a good option for [[Shapeshift]]

Love to combo with [[Riptide]] and just pull into the right angle and drown something.


[[Sea Raider]] (x3)

Here for much needed card draw. Ability still works even if he dies attacking and is usually worth the sacrifice to help with hand advantage. Decent target for [[Shapeshift]].


[[The Lady of the Lake]] (x1)

Cycle any mortal you need! Mainly [[Pirate Ship]], [[Ruler of Thul]] for charge sneak attacks or [[The Green Knight]] feel the best.


[[Captain Baldassare]] (x1)

Here for extra draw similar to [[Sea Raider]]. Pure water list just need more draw and this gives some hand advantage, use enemy spells whenever possible. Decent cycle option for [[The Lady of the Lake]].


[[Lord of Unland]] (x1)

Usually feels best played submerged at first for a few turns. The +1 in his body of water always feels strong especially with all water sites and the avatars ability. Was doubting this cards worth and then he came in clutch a ton of times. Combos well with [[Ruler of Thul]] giving a bunch of bonus’. Can be [[Selfsame Simulacrum]]’d for more buffs! Dont forget to move him along under water either toward an enemy avatar at door or towards our own [[Waveshaper]] for defense.


[[Pirate Ship]] (x4)

Just a strong staple for [[Waveshaper]] 4 cost 5x5 BEATER. Can easily attack because of avatars ability. Want to keep water sites connected whenever possible especially so [[Pirate Ship]] can defend easier.


[[Ruler of Thul]] (x1)

Top tier card giving +1 power to allies on the TOP and BOTTOM of the realm + unexpected movement. Very good for sneak attacks for door especially with [[Plague of Frogs]].

Can be cycled with [[The Lady of the Lake]].


[[Selfsame Simulacrum]] (x2)

Tech card! Love to copy pretty much any unique / big minion card in this list but pretty much if something is good on board copy it!


[[Anui Undine]] (x2)

with 97% of this deck being water sites she will always be considerable strong and able to attack with [[Waveshaper]]s ability. If opponent has water site shes even more insanely powerful if that is the case I like to put her underwater with a [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] for consistent draw when possible. If not possible just attack.


[[Questing Beast]] (x1)

Really great card all around, 5x5 power is always strong. I like to use this for a final stealth strike at Deaths Door especially with the movement at the end of turn. Just the pressure of a 5 power swing + the added movement feels great. When playing against Earth opponents the movement at the end of turn can be used to move back onto a water site for safety.


[[Mester Stoor Worm]] (x1)

Fits beautifully with [[Waveshaper]]s ability. Waterbound and Submerge hard to kill giant 7 power. Just all value basically a constant smaller [[Poison Nova]] threat on top of that. Can be used to board wipe with the lethal ability and ping for a Deaths Door final blow! Decent combo for [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] for a draw engine it will always stay alive but not attacking for 7 or using ability is tough lol


[[The Green Knight]] (x1)

Can win you the game! Forcing the enemy movement and crushing smaller minons is so good I forget about the strike he does at deathrite! Feels best when played on a [[Troll Bridge]]. This turn 3 with a [[Mix Aqua]] can really set the tone for a game. Also great option for [[Pnakotic Manuscript]]








• MAGIC



[[Plague of Frogs]] (x1)

Great defensively mainly, can buy some time. Crazy draw when paired with [[Pnakotic Manuscript]]. [[Ruler of Thul]] and [[Lord of Unland]] can turn these boys up +1 power for a sneak attacks. Can be used to run artifacts around to different units! Easy target for [[Shapeshift]]



[[Geyser]] (x1)

Testing this out for now. Hoping to use it for surprise attacks and possibly drowning pesky burrowed minions especially [[Root Spider]]. Can help with [[Wavshaper]] tap abilities range + it draws a card might be solid.


[[Polymorph]] (x2)

Banish the original minion so it never sees the cemetery leaving only a little baby enemy frog. Pairs really well with [[Sea Raider]] and [[Captain Baldassare]]


[[Riptide]] (x4)

Helpful movement spell for your own minions but it can also target enemies. Moving them out the way or closer for whatever you need. Can help facilitate a final blow at Deaths Door. [[Floodplain]] can help with range when needed and of course [[Waveshaper]]s ability as well.


[[Drown]] (x1)

With so many water sites and the flood ability this is very strong removal. Really helps remove pesky artifacts especially ring with an enemy avatar on the move for door or any crazy artifact really.


[[Ice Lance]] (x1)

Not my favorite Deaths Door spell but water doesnt have a ton of options. Usually best to hold until late game if found early, only to be used in emergencies to get rid of some flying or huge minion threat. Being able to pierce and choose any target per space is very good but damage starts at casters location 3, adjacent site 2, next adjacent site 1. Range is a little weaker than I thought but still usually does the job. [[Adept illusionist]] work well with this being a spellcaster the 1st copy can bring out the 2nd and should be in range for a final blow.


[[Mesmerism]] (x1)

Might be one of the best cards in the deck. Taking someone’s untapped minion and swinging especially if theyre huge feels very good. Can swing the momentum greatly.


[[Shapeshift]] (x1)

Looking to shift into something big preferably [[The Green Knight]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], [[Anui Undine]], or [[Questing Beast]] for a sneak attack. Shifting into any waterbound minion may need the [[Waveshaper]] flood ability so keep that in mind.









• SITES


[[Autumn River]], [[Spring River]], of course [[Winter River]] (x4), + [[Summer River]] (x2)

Searching hard for ramp cards such as [[Mix Aqua]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]], or [[Aquamarine Core]] pretty much always. Once found start looking for something big to play like [[The Green Knight]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], [[Anui Undine]], or [[Questing Beast]]. Repeat this until you get close to the end game where it’s best to start looking for Deaths Door spells. Late game [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Ice Lance]] are probably the best options but you can also cycle for [[Questing Beast]], [[Mesmerize]], [[Truesight Crossbow]], or maybe [[Riptides]] / whatever is needed in the moment.


[[Floodplain]] (x3)

Really helps for attacking with any of the waterbound minions without having to use [[Waveshaper]]s ability. Can combo with [[Waveshaper]]s ability to flood and tap down deeper into the realm. [[Riptide]] combos similarly, you can flood for more reach and hit some forced movement when needed.


[[Kelp Cavern]] (x2)

I think of this as a better [[Observatory]], searching the bottom of the deck instead, giving you more card selection and much appreciated water threshold.


[[Maelstrom]] (x1)

Should of had this in here the entire time!!! Can play minions back or to the side pulling them next start of turn to then be in attack range feels very strong. Doesn't always have to be used either but in a full body of water pulling everything in and [[Waveshaper]] tapping it down feels way to strong!


[[Mirror Realm]] (x1)

Really just here to copy any river site to look at the top card. Can be used to copy enemy sites mainly any tower for more mana or for defense. Copying [[Maelstrom]] can add up to insane hard to defend movement!


[[Tadpole Pool]] (x1)

x3 little tadpoles can be used as chump blockers mainly, but if you're lucky you can combo with Ruler of Thul for a +1 power sneak attack style or my favorite [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] to get an easy x3 draw. Good targets for [[Shapeshift]]


[[Troll Bridge]] (x3)

Staple for any water deck. Helps with defense and provides threshold. [[Riptide]]-ing someone into here feels great.


[[Under Tow]] (x3)

Comes in clutch for extra movement can help pull an ally into better attack positions or pull enemies away from their intended defensive position. Alot of options and is a must trigger ability not a may.


[[Wizard's Den]] (x2)

Draw and hand advantage is top tier. Even if you have to discard later in the game the draw was a card you didn't have before and sometimes people arent even able to attack the site and its just a free draw. Very underrated I believe it should be in pretty much any deck that isn't to threshold stressed.







MAYBE CARDS


[[Observatory]] (x2)

Provides some useful information giving a little advantage to the next few turns. I was always skeptical of this site might be better to have towers and push but if used correctly can feel like it extends your hand size. Might be worth a pen/paper or pad.


[[Sneak Thief]] (x1)

Can put pressure on an avatar with any important artifact causing them to move to get away from this card and setting them back slightly. Can be used to sneak a final blow at Deaths Door with stealth or at the very least a great target for [[Shapeshift]]. Once I used this ability to take an [[Iron Shackles]] off a stronger minion setting them free to attack!


[[Brobdingnag Bullfrog]] (x1)

Can be used to disable attacking enemy minions hoping he stays around a turn or two atleast. Can attack whats in its belly. Combos really well with [[Sea Raider]]. If needed it is a decent 3 cost 3x3 beater minion.



Deck surprised me don’t be afraid to [[Black Obelisk]].


[[Black Obelisk]] (x1)

Not my favorite option for ramp in this list but is still worth it for the combos it unlocks. Play on turn 3 if possible don't be afraid to play this card but it always feels risky. TAKE THE LEAP! Unless youre already getting pummeled [[Waveshaper]] can usually buy some time.


[[Iron Shackles]] (x1)

Replacing the second [[Black Obelisk]] cause second one is always dead so a little stall that can combo with [[Sea Raider]] to help draw. Or just completely shut down some big minion.

deckinfo.name: 🇧🇷 Savior Steampunk - Aggro Tempo 🐎🐈🐦
deckinfo.primer:
{{https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sD_UNEkIU0s}}


Introduction

This deck was born from a simple idea: build an aggressive strategy capable of fighting the current water-heavy meta while still using the raw efficiency of Fire creatures.

At the center of the deck is [[Savior]], an Avatar whose ability to grant Ward fundamentally changes how aggressive creatures behave. In a normal deck, small creatures trade once and disappear. Here, they often survive multiple combats, forcing the opponent to spend far more resources than expected.

Spiritually speaking, [[Savior]] is also a pretty interesting Avatar. In this list he represents something closer to shamanism and chaos magick — animals, fire, protection and controlled chaos. Which feels extremely appropriate when you see how the board develops.

Instead of relying heavily on card draw engines like many Water decks do, this deck focuses on extracting maximum value from each card played. Creatures stay alive longer thanks to Ward, removal becomes asymmetric, and mass removal spells often hurt the opponent far more than they hurt us.

Another important pillar of the deck is the strategic use of board wipes. Because many of our creatures are protected, these spells often create devastating tempo swings.

Testing updates and meta adjustments appear at the end of this primer.


About the Deck

This list plays best as an Aggro Tempo strategy.

The goal is not simply to flood the board with creatures, but to create efficient threats that survive longer than they should.

Thanks to [[Savior]], creatures can often:

  • attack
  • trade
  • survive
  • receive Ward again
  • continue applying pressure

This creates asymmetric trades, meaning each of your creatures can force two or more answers from the opponent.

The deck also treats sites as strategic tools, not just mana sources. They help control positioning, punish certain strategies, stabilize thresholds and sometimes function as removal themselves.

In most matchups, you are the beatdown.


Who Is This Deck For?

I built this list specifically to satisfy my urge to play aggro while still leveraging the strongest Fire cards I already owned, combined with the new Gothic Water staples.

Aggro Heads

If you enjoy putting pressure on the board and attacking constantly, but feel frustrated with the dominance of Necromancer and Water control shells, this deck gives you the tools to fight back.

Druid Fire Widows

After the errata, many players abandoned Druid Fire entirely. This list gives those cards a new home and lets them shine again with Ward synergies and asymmetric trades.

Necrowater Haters

If you enjoy anti-meta strategies and dislike seeing a single archetype dominate the environment, this deck is extremely satisfying.

Steampunkers

If you always wanted to combine Fire and Water but felt limited by the lack of a dedicated Omphalos, this list finally makes that combination work.

Alternative Spiritual Paths

Since [[Savior]] grants Ward as protection, I like to think of the deck as representing broader spiritual paradigms — something closer to shamanism and chaos magic rather than rigid orthodoxy.


Core Strategy

The game plan can be divided into three phases.

Early Game

The early game is about developing efficient threats while preparing your mana base.

It is usually correct to draw sites in the first two or three draws, while keeping at least two sites in hand.

A strong opening hand usually includes creatures costing (1), (2) and (3).

Important early cards include:

  • [[Redcap Powries]]
  • [[Redbreast Robin]]
  • [[War Horse]]
  • [[Pied Piper of Hamelin]]
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]]
  • [[Philosopher’s Stone]]

The ideal hand also contains a containment plan such as:

  • [[Atlantean Fate]]
  • [[Peasant Revolt]]
  • [[Fields of Camlann]]

Mid Game

This is where the tempo advantage becomes decisive.

Your creatures continue applying pressure while the deck uses powerful reset tools such as:

  • [[Peasant Revolt]]
  • [[Atlantean Fate]]
  • [[Fields of Camlann]]
  • [[Poison Nova]]

These spells often become one-sided board wipes thanks to Ward.

This is also the stage where creatures that generate card advantage should enter the game:

  • [[Captain Baldassar]]
  • [[Maiden, Mother, Crone]]
  • [[Morgana le Fay]]

Late Game

The deck does not aim to prolong the game, but it still has powerful finishers.

Common ways to close the game include:

  • [[Searing Truth]]
  • [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]]
  • [[Redbreast Robin]]
  • [[Saracen Raiders]]
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]]
  • [[Flame Strike]] (collection)
  • [[Minor Explosion]] (collection)
  • [[Flayer]] (collection)
  • [[Colicky Dragonettes]] projectiles

And when [[Boudicca]] enters the board…

MAMA IS COMING.


Resource & Card Advantage

This deck does not rely on heavy draw engines like many Water decks.

Instead, it creates card advantage through survivability and efficient exchanges.

Ward already generates huge value by allowing creatures to survive longer than normal.

Additional draw sources include:

  • [[Captain Baldassar]]
  • [[Morgana le Fay]]
  • [[Gift of the Serpent]] - Combine with Redbreast Robin, Quarrelsome Kobolds or Colicky Dragonettes and see the magic happening
  • [[Maiden, Mother, Crone]]
  • [[Searing Truth]]

Together these cards provide just enough card flow to maintain momentum without slowing down the aggressive plan.


Key Cards

[[Redbreast Robin]]

This is my secret weapon.

I learned the importance of having my own Robin from Batman.

The card is incredibly versatile:

  • removes tokens
  • deals finishing damage
  • controls sites
  • attracts removal

Many players underestimate it, which makes it even more dangerous.

[[Redcap Powries]]

Three power for (3) cost and fully compatible with Ward.

They are responsible for much of the deck's early and midgame pressure.

[[Adept Illusionist]]

One of the most interesting engines in the deck.

Because it enters with Ward, it usually survives long enough to fetch another copy from the deck.

After that, it becomes extremely hard to remove and is excellent for defending frontline sites.

[[Lugbog Cat]]

Four power for only (3) cost.

In a meta full of water decks, its restriction of only being played on water sites often becomes an advantage.

With Ward it becomes an extremely efficient attacker.

[[Quarrelsome Kobolds]]

Possibly the strongest Fire minion.

They enter the battlefield already dealing unavoidable damage.

With Ward they often survive long enough to attack again.

They also combine well with:

  • desert damage
  • [[Colicky Dragonettes]]
  • [[Redbreast Robin]]

[[Boudicca]]

An extremely powerful damage amplifier.

With just two or three creatures attacking sites, she can easily push the opponent into Death’s Door.

And when she enters the battlefield…

MAMA IS COMING.

[[Ruler of Thul]]

Another strong damage amplifier.

With Charge and buffs it helps your creatures reach the opponent's Avatar quickly.

[[Sacred Stag]]

Four power for (4) cost and already protected with Ward.

With [[Pond]] it can even enter play cheaper.

It defends, attacks and almost makes coffee.

[[Failed Mutation]]

An unusual but extremely powerful inclusion.

Although it cannot receive Ward, it has a form of natural protection since it cannot be targeted or damaged by spells.

This allows it to ignore most removal in the game.


Sites and Their Roles

Instead of grouping them as mana sources, it is more useful to understand their strategic functions.

Threshold Correction

These stabilize the elemental requirements of the deck.

  • [[Active Volcano]] (f)(f)
  • [[Deep Sea]] (w)(w)
  • [[Caerleon-Upon-Usk]]
  • [[Joyous Garden]]

Swarm Control

These help control wide boards.

  • [[Fields of Camlann]]
  • [[Remote Desert]]
  • [[Arid Desert]]
  • [[Vesuvius]]

Lifegain Hate

Prevents stabilization.

  • [[River of Blood]]

Graveyard Hate

Essential against recursion decks.

  • [[Plague Pits]]
  • [[Kor Crematory]]

Control Sites

These provide board control.

  • [[Fields of Camlann]]
  • [[Garden of Eden]]

Movement

Helps reposition threats aggressively.

  • [[River Rapids]] - You can put Quarrelsome Kobold in front of the enemy Avatar.

Ramp

Provides mana acceleration.

  • [[Imperial Road]]
  • [[Pond]]


Advanced Play Patterns (Extra Section)

Ward Sequencing

Creatures are usually only played without Ward if they must remove an immediate threat.

Otherwise:

  • if the creature would die in combat → Ward first
  • if it survives combat → Ward after

Asymmetric Board Wipes

Mass removal should be used when:

  • it removes key threats
  • it leaves the opponent far behind
  • or when the exchange is almost unilateral

The most powerful wipes are:

1 [[Peasant Revolt]]

2 [[Poison Nova]]

3 [[Fields of Camlann]]

Imperial Road Timing

[[Imperial Road]] is best used once the opponent has no sites left in hand.

It allows you to:

  • advance aggressively
  • gain extra mana
  • keep pace with Savior’s Ward cost

Boudicca Pressure

If you have two or three creatures hitting sites, [[Boudicca]] can quickly push the opponent into Death’s Door.


Common Mistakes (Extra Section)

Bad Mulligans

Players often keep slow hands.

The deck must start applying pressure early.


Playing Creatures Without Ward

This often leads to losing tempo unnecessarily.


Poor Site Positioning

Sites should be played dynamically depending on the matchup.

Most of the time it is safer to play backwards, advancing only when necessary.


Stacking Creatures

Placing multiple creatures in the same site makes them vulnerable to spells such as:

  • [[Earthquake]]
  • [[Call to the Sea]]
  • [[Atlantean Fate]]

Unfortunately, these cards affect warded minions.


Not Attacking with the Avatar

If the opponent relies heavily on removal, advancing with the Avatar can sometimes be the correct play.


Matchups

vs Aggro

Generally favorable.

Decks like [[Interrogator]], [[Persecutor]] and [[Battlemage]] can be controlled through efficient trades.

vs Midrange

This is usually the hardest matchup.

Large creatures combined with heavy removal can disrupt your tempo.

vs Control

Very good matchup.

Decks like [[Archimago]] and [[Deathspeaker]] struggle to keep up with the early pressure.

vs Water Decks

The most challenging matchup.

Cards like [[Coy Nixie]] can remove Ward through forced movement.

Positioning becomes extremely important. Sometimes attacking from the sides helps avoid dangerous movement effects.

Against [[Waveshaper]], placing earth sites in front of the opponent can help limit the expansion of water bodies.


Testing & Updates

The local meta in São Paulo, Brazil has shifted quite a bit.

Players here tend to build their own decks instead of following established metas, and due to both card availability and preference, we are currently seeing far fewer Necromancer and Water-based decks. Instead, a new challenge has emerged: Earth/Fire Savior builds.

These decks bring a very different kind of pressure. Instead of relying on spells or control, they present durable board states and efficient creatures that are much harder to break through.

The main problems I’ve been facing are:

  • [[Shield Maiden]] making trades extremely inefficient
  • [[Root Spider]] slowing down positioning and tempo
  • [[Assorted Animals]] creating constant board presence

This shifts the matchup significantly. Instead of fighting removal or combo strategies, the deck now has to deal with resilient midrange boards that absorb pressure very well, making it harder to close games.

Some players in my group have started adapting their lists with cards like [[Royal Bodyguard]] and other defensive tools, which makes the matchup even more challenging.

At this point, I’m still evaluating the best way to approach this shift. It may require adjusting the balance between aggression, removal, and reach, or even reconsidering how the deck closes games against more stable boards.

  • More testing is needed, and I’ll report back with further updates.


One of the most memorable moments with this deck happened on turn five, when I cast [[Peasant Revolt]] against an opponent who had only one unique unit and four unique sites in play. GG



Everything disappeared.

He conceded immediately.

Sometimes the deck wins through steady pressure.

Other times…

It wins through absolute chaos.

deckinfo.name: Murmuring Dust | Animist Supremacy
deckinfo.primer:
The Dust whispers - The Animist listens


Mindrange Animist with a Beast Package (WIP)


Hit me up with suggestions.




Also check out realms.cards you can play me and others there


Mulligans:

This part is WIP as I dont get many games in


If you have creatures in your opener you can almost alway put them away, what you really want to see are non-cantrip 2 and 3 drops, also Wiccan Tools feels very good




Card Choices:


AURA


Evil Presence - This one is a No-Brainer and probably the most synergistic card Animist has right now


Sow the Earth - Not only does it Ramp you to 6 Mana as early as turn 3 if City of Glass or Tower is in play, 2 Mana (or 3 if we hit a Tower) become available immediately for double spelling


ARTIFACT


Cores - Ramp, might get cut


Silver Bullet - Access to Collection Cards,

casting from Collection Exceptional Minions which are neither Beasts nor Spirits seems really interesting to me, might get cut


Toolbox - Collection Access, its so sweet not having to play Zap! and Artifact Hate in main


Wiccan Tools - card is here right now for testing as Treshhold is sometimes a problem in this deck, so far feals really great as basically a cantrip


MINION


Carion Beetles - Graveyard Hate


Frisky Red Squirrel - Artifact Hate


Gyre Hippogryphs - Flexible Aggro Beast


Root Spider - its just to good of a card to not play


Squirming Mass - I wished this card had Burrowing but it stays for now as its grows big and it grows fast when timed correctly


Hounds of Ondaros - Midrange Beaters, super flexible movement, might go if to slow but excited to see how they fare in testing


Gargantula - Root Spiders Cousin, very nice Tempo Play


Draco Corvus- the Top End of our Curve and Removal on a Stick, closes out games fast enough to earn a slot (also maybe just a Pet Card)



MAGIC

This is where Animist shines, in raising the Floor for Magics to always be a Minion, we get a broad selection of usually Mid spells to be game winning cards

This section is probably also the one where most things will be changed over time


Arcane Barrage - One of the best examples of what you have just read above, X-Spells are highly synergistic with Animist, remove stuff or make creature as big as you want. Makes it important to have some Spellcasters in our List


Assorted Animals - this card led me to the idea for this deck and is the reason we play Beasts, right now the only X-Spell requiring only 2 Threshold so its much more feasible to play early


Browse - will mostly stay Magic as its too good to be a onedrop, great card selection


Tithe - we want to draw as few Sites as we can get away with, this helps


Common Sense - Not much to say here, incidentally the next few Magics in this List are the ones we want to fetch with this Tutor


Gift of the Raven - Cantrips are one of my favourite things with Animist

this might be removed sometime tho as we only heal when striking units but for testing it stays now


Gift of the Wolf - Simple Combat Trick that replaces itself, what more do we want?


Blink - Cantrip and Movement Trick


Magic Missles - our main spell to break Wards


Bury - Just some good removal, could even be used to bury our Hounds to protect them


Feast for Crows - Combo hate, also great in the Mirror Match to disable their Evil Presence


Kiss of Death - even better Removal with Animist


Murder of Crows - Spells that can be cast again from the graveyard really intrigue me, they bring another layer of flexibility to the deck. This one is to beat Necromancer


Witching Hour - This card has surprised me in how potent it is in taking over the game quick. Will probably stay as a staple for Animist


Vanishment - Replaces itself and protects our board


Cave-In - nice Removal


Gigantism - one of the best cards in Earth, makes us win fast


Unlikely Alliance - with so much different rarity among our Spirit Magics, drawing 3 or 4 Cards is quite realistic, makes it a staple in Animist


Earthquake - R E M O V A L


Whirling Blades - can turn the tide of the game in our favor especially if we stack this with one of the Gifts / Witching Hour




SITE


Bower of Bliss - Turn your enemys Mortals to Vanilla Creatures


City of Glass, Dark/Gothic/Lone Tower - Mana acceleration and our best hits of Sow the Earth


Cloud City - double dare your opponent to attack this Site


Fertile Earth / Mountain Peaks - we are a HEAVY Threshold Deck, these two are essential


Fields of Phyxis - great for dealing with any Sites that annoy us


Haystack - Tutor Hate


Merlins Tower - a free Spell? what not to like, also if your in Europe get your copy NOW, it was almost impossible for me to find


Observatory - smooths out our next Draws


Heirloom Lost - Site Hate


Pebbled Paths - Aggro Hate


Perilous Bridge - for Defense, best placed on the middle column


Pillar of Zeiros - super sweet as all our Magic Spirits are Magics again in the Yard


Rustic Village - gives us a cheap blocker


Treetop Hideout - if manage to give Stealth to White Hart we are probably winning


Varmint Warrens - more synergy for our Beasts


Windmill - Color fixing


Wormelow Tump - Protects our reanimation Side-hustle



Collection


Zap! - Removes Deaths Door as a mechanic from the game


Dispel/Disenchant - Artifact Hate


Pith Imp - if you give him Wiccan Tools he gets to cast the stolen card now????


Flanking Maneuver - Big Movement that Cantrips, might be moved to Main Deck


Order of the Pale Worm - Ward Hate


Another Gift of the Wolf


Pudge Butcher - Big Value Creature


Daperyll Vampire - Big Value Lifegain







Considering


Craterize - Big Finisher


Onyx / Amethyst Core - Ramp, gives insanly fast starts


Torshammer Trinket - Utility to enable profitable attacks


Sisters of Avalon - Support Card for our Deck, another Spellcaster is always good, they help with bad Mulligans and play nicely with Skeleton Mage


Skeleton Mage - Skeleton Mage gets a Slot as he is also a Spellcaster and reanimates our best Utility Cards


Divine Healing - against Aggro, if we play against Control its a Minion, thats the beauty of Animist


White Knight - no direct synergy with this Deck but 3 Mana for 3/5 is a Treat for this Midrange List, also it being Exceptional makes them important Blockers against Aggro


Squirming Mass - This one I am quite unsure about, its a target for Assorted Animals and could scale nicely in aggro matchups, but might as well be removed if testing shows its to slow


White Hart - AA Target, one of the best Defensive Cards there is, especially if we manage to give it Stealth with Treetop Hideout

deckinfo.name: Animist - Spirits on Strike
deckinfo.primer:
You will always have a minion able to be cast.


primary game plan is using strike effects


secondary game plan is using hard removal


the 3rd option is just mix it all together and hope for good play lines. infiltrating and betrayal into attacking their site that has a plague or famine feels great, same thing with infiltrate and warp spasm just odd ways to remove their minions. vampires healing twice with strike effects is a nice back up plan.


Leaning heavy in the 4 and 5 power range.


With alot of strike effects to push alot of damage as removal and to end the game on deathsdoor.


That is the name of game, get them to door at all costs and you will more than likely have a way to end it from there.


Evil presence feels like the real mvp here.


Really trying to line up an early 4 power threat that is either hitting hard with a strike effect or using the strike effect to clear a defender and get an attack in.



The extra towers here are to try to consistantly be able to rush out a very early threat or double spell with 6 or 7 mana



added watch towers to really protect against infiltrate.


so far in testing this deck has not held up to the current meta. sadly vanilla minions are not that impactful. this deck is a fine line balance of knowing when to use the magic for its ability compared to when to turn it into a minion and hope it sticks around for you to be able to use on your next turn.
