deckinfo.name: Thermodynamics
deckinfo.primer:
Walling up with defensive minions so that I can get to 5/6 mana and surprising the opponent with in your face fire spells.


[[Avatar of Water]] has amazing mobility, allowing it to be exactly where it needs to be.

  • Throw around powerful close range removal like [[Disintegrate]], [[Mesmerism]] and [[Poison Nova]].
  • Hit with [[Lava Flow]], [[Snowball]] and [[Flame Strike]] the best possible angles.


AoW can be set up to reach most of the board. Any dedicated fire sites can be put to one site to not break the body of water too badly.


You don't need to utilise AoW's effect every turn, the quality of water minions is good enough to build pressure.

  • [[Shellycoat]], [[Tufted Turtles]] and [[Failed Mutation]] are able to ignore [[Poison Nova]] and take some small splash damage from other spells
  • Most high costed water minions are potent enough to be threats on their own.
  • I am still working out if [[Great Old One]] is necessary or if it is a vanity pick.

deckinfo.name: Sea of Thieves
deckinfo.primer:
Sea of Thieves


point of this deck is to use pirate ships and cats to gain an early advantage


turn 4-5 use your avatar of water ability to flood the sight right in front of enemy avatar, you can now use nearby control/damaging spells to make it so you can beat down with your ships and cats


Avatar of water can help “nearby” spells (arc lighting, love potion, mesmerism, etc) be more effective with out spending extra mana on blinks/teleports + you can flood sight to activate waterbound creatures


control and damage options with Arc lightning make it feel like it can be aggressive or control


devil egg can secure placement on opponents site while teleporting and sitting there with them


fun tricks like telekinesis/replication and all sorts of fun things


AoW movements helps you be aggressive against Archimagos that use craterize forcing them to take damage also


AoW against Druids can use Anui submerged to avoid Drums of Doom, use your Avatar of Waters ability to flood their site and control Druids minions to do heavy swings that they cant prevent. This is more viable if the druid plays water, which is quite common and after using an Atlantean Fate.


4/2/2025

Won local event - will provide more updates to the deck shortly.


11/12/2025

removed the vampires and griffins, because of rivers of blood only healing for 2 didn’t feel well, to help with aggro and early game I put in 3 tufted turtles to help stabilize


12/8/2025

added Iron Maiden and thumbscrews, being able to replicate these and instantly teleport to them with AoW ability is great value and doesn’t change the deck to much, they can also punish interrogator decks by drawing to many cards/combo decks


4/16/2026


Making quite a few changes using spells like recall to make our movement even better with AoW. Playing defensive then setting up a AoW ability to recall we can set up men of leng, fin wifes, and more. We can keep our ships back as defense units and do a surprise attack with AoW water teleport flood/recall combo

deckinfo.name: Welcome to the Forest (Gothic Update)
deckinfo.primer:
Welcome to the Forest


The deck is meant to lean more toward the midrange category, with the ability to hold its own in the late game and potentially take the wind out of aggro decks’ sails—at least until the Battlemage and his horde of pigs and beasts have built enough board presence to turn the game around.




Gothic Update:

Using a bit more Waterspells...the Forest is turning more and more into a Swamp. Also some Knights joined our Beasts on their Quest to defend the Forest.


Primer Update 30/05/2025


The biggest change is, that the deck doesn't include Squeakers etc. With 60 Cards in the spellbook it feels nearly impossible to make it work and is most of the time frustrating.


I also decided to go with 2x Toolbox instead of common sense and added a little beastpackage for Assorted Animals (maybe a second copy is also good).


If I could get a Gargantula or two and a second Sacred Stag this would be really good additions for the deck. Also 2x or 3x Invigorate would be good and better as the muddy pigs. You see over long time all pigs in this deck will sadly be gone. Maybe 1x Muddy pig will stay for the Assorted Animals package.


The Crusade Aura is also not that good anymore because i added many water minions.


Fine Courser is because of our many movement spells irrelevant now. We are not that aggro in our playstyle so no need to hurry and ride a horse.


An idea i got is to combine peace offering with river rapids. Play it and push it for the effect. Next turn return to the river and push it again. Could be really frustrating for the opponent. But i am missing a second river and a peace offering.


I added 2x Malakhim because with Mix Terra it is a really good minion that can be cast early in the game. And in my Lore for the deck, Malakhim is the Angel which protects the Forest, the Knights are praising him and following his path to protect the forest from evil.


Primer Update 13/12/2025


I took out the Arc Lightning for a Pollimorph. Because it banishs the minion and could do this also to minions over 4 Power, which is good against those big harbringer minions. Also the frog is a free card to draw when killed by Battlemage. The only reason to keep Arc Lightning would be the possible damage to an Avatar and the possibility to search for it with common sense.


I also added a third Shrink for the Disenchant. We have still the Dispel, which can be searched with Common Sense if artifact removal or aura removal is really needed. It's more a personal preference.


Primer Update 10/12/2025


I decided to cut the Master Tracker for a Replication.

Master Tracker is most of the time just a 2 Mana Minion with 2 Power, so i think replicate a Ring of Morrigan, the Amethyst Core or a Crown of Victor (if i have one) is much stronger.


Primer Update 09/12/2025


I added two Floodplains. They are good for three different things:

  1. Fixing water threshhold
  2. Flood enemys site, so we can cast our cats there for more pressure
  3. Remove burrowed enemy Minions like root Spiders or Pit Vipers by flooding them


I took out the Wolpertinger for a Selfsame Simulacrum. Because Wolpertinger is just a big minion in the best case. (Graveyardhate is thing now). Selfsame Simulacrum can copy my and my opponent’s minions. So it is a more situational card. Thanks for the idea in the comments Minkdinker.



Primer Update 08/12/2025


I added 4 Ponds because of the threshold ability for beasts and the costreduction. This site feels so good for this deck. I'm also thinking about adding two Kelp Caverns to get the Pigs of Sounder or the Grand Old Boars from under the deck on top of it. I think in some situations it could be a cool play.


When my gothic order is arrived (europe located, so i have to wait for my predorder) i would like to splash a little bit water for cards like Invigorate or Swap and maybe the Lugbog Cats from arthurian legends. A 4 Power Beast cast for 2 with the Pond ability or cast for 3 mana to an enemy water site is really good. Shrink is also good option.

Maybe i will take out the rootspiders when water is splashed.


I also want to use some cards in the collection but at the moment it is used to remember the next possible good cards for the deck.


Edit:

I couldn't resist to add some water cards right now.

I added Shrink, Lugbog Cats, Geyser and Questing Beast.

I added also two Kelp Caverns and a Lighthouse.


Shrink is good to stay alive while killing big minions.

Lugbog Cats are good because of the reasons above.

Geyser is good for flooding burrowed minions or helping out with water threshold. (Besides getting airborne and a card.)

Questing Beast is a big Minion with Lethal and implementet Stealth and Movement. Nothing to explain here.


Took out some Villages, a Quagmire and a Holy Ground.

Also Took out one Unicorn and the two Root Spiders. They are good but are easy to remove and sometimes blocking our own minions. With the new more aggressive playstyle they are not that important. For locking problematic minions we still have two iron shackles.


With Gothic and rivers of blood i think two sinkholes or fields of phyxis could be important and instead of Divine Healing adding Invigorate for the lower healing with powerboost should be fine.

Divine Healing with Rivers of Blood is just +3 Lifepoints. Invigorate is just +1 Lifepoint with river of blood but still boosts for Damage, its like a four Life Difference and a bit more flexibel for combats because the powerboost could also effect minions and not just the avatar. In addition the artwork of invigorate is fitting more the theme of the deck.


Primer Update 30/11/2025:


An update which makes the deck more aggressive.

And maybe a bit more competetive.

Added Ring of Morrigan, Grim Guisarme, Highland Princess, Sir Galahad, Amethyst Core and Earthquake. Took out the Vampires, Valor, Poisonous Dagger, Flaming Sword, one Iron Shakle and a Common Sense.

I also added 3 Windmills and a Mirror Realm.


Primer Update 28/11/2025:


I added Fine Courser for more movement instead one Pallibure Bat and for the second Bat i added a Poisonous Dagger for Lethal as an extra removal option.


Took out the Entangle Terrain, because it also affects our airborne minions.

Took out the last Horn of Caerleon, because it also gives nearby enemy minions charge.

-> I Added Kettletop Leprechaun instead, so we don't need to draw extra sites in the best case.


I also added one Arc Lightning for bigger minions or as a death blow, when enemy is on death's door. It is also not random like the Lightning Bolt.


Primer Update 22/11/2025:


I added Master Tracker because of units like Sir Agravaine or Morgana le Fay.


"Starting Build of this Deck":


Key Creatures – “Beasts”


Squeakers, Pigs of the Sounder and Grand Old Boar are pretty self-explanatory here and, together with other Beasts, are intended to form the main theme of the deck.


The Wolpertinger can become very powerful as the game progresses.


The Gyre Hippogriffs, with Airborne and Charge, are excellent creatures for applying pressure.


The two Daperyll Vampires are useful later in the game, as they either attract the opponent`s removal or, in the best case, help regenerate some life.


Hounds of Ondaros can be really frustrating for the opponent.


Ramp


The deck includes 2× Mix Terra in case the large boar is drawn and cannot be played from the deck via the effect of the smaller pigs.

--> You can also cast Root Spiders, Pigs of the Sounder or Autumn Unicorns with it for free.


Frontier Settlers are like little Pathfinders, I like the concept - You don`t need to draw a site or use your battlemage to draw/play sites and have a body for blocking/attacking.


Movement


Blink, Grapple Shot and Tactical Move are included so you don’t end up being a Snailmage.


Tutor


With Common Sense, you can search for the appropriate Ordinary depending on the situation.


Tempo Tax


Entangle Terrain, Iron Shackles, Root Spiders, Quagmire and Pebbled Paths help slow down the opponent.


Artifact/Aura Removal


One Disenchant and one Dispel for Aura- or Artifact-Removal, since they can be searched with Common Sense and I want to play both because of the artwork.

--> You can also use Bury for Artifact-Removal if needed.


Burn and Removal


Bury is good against creatures without Burrowing.


Lightning Bolt serves as cheap removal for small creatures or as a finisher when the opponent’s Avatar is at Death’s Door.


Magic Missiles are used depending on the situation.


Aggro


Crusade and Horn of Caerleon are good cards for applying pressure.

--> A 5 Power Autumn Unicorn with charge cast to a Site of your opponent is really good. (You can also use a Mix Terra if needed for the Unicorn)


Healing


Daperyll Vampire, Divine Healing and Holy Ground are good to keep you away from Death`s Door.

--> Grapple Shot in combination with Daperyll Vampire can get you a massive heal and damage output at the same time.



Lands


The lands are taken from my available collection, so the list is not yet optimal. A more refined concept may come in the future.


Suggestions for Additional Cards


White Hart is planned to be added once available.


Highland Falconer is maybe also a good option. Because you can thin out the deck, which is better for the boars and if a Grain Sparrow is searched we have 2 bodys and gain 2 life for 2 mana. (I have no Falconer yet in my collection)


Assorted Animals is also a good option to search wanted beasts and thin out the deck. Two copys will be added in the future if i get my hands on them.


If you have any ideas that fit the theme of the deck, feel free to leave them in the comments.

deckinfo.name: Tempo of the Dog
deckinfo.primer:
Arthurian Legends has made this deck the low-curve aggro/tempo deck I always hoped it could be. The low curve means you can afford to cap out at 3-5 sites and maintain efficient tempo and not have to load the deck with too many minions to defend them. Try to mulligan for a Ruins or at least one site for each element, and always be applying pressure to the opponent by any and all means at your disposal. A deck this light on minions is not meant for much grinding, but it can still go the distance if you're smart about how you move your avatar around and use your resources.


Artifacts


Amulet of Niniane: This fancy trinket is an amazing bargain at a mere one mana and is one of the artifacts that allowed me to drop Daperyll Vampire from the list. Having this on your avatar early means you don't have to worry about being whittled down by magic and is a major advantage in the mirror match and against Archimago.


Ring of Morrigan: The other fancy trinket that allowed me to tighten the curve on this deck and forego Angel's Egg as well. With twenty-nine magics in the deck, this thing will be firing off quite a lot if it's on your avatar or anyone else when paired with Merlin's Staff.


Torshammar Trinket: Not so fancy, but its low cost and versatility makes it worth including a single copy. You can put it on your avatar or any minion about to make an important attack. It can be a consistent source of damage for Far East Assassin, or allow you to push a bit of extra damage every turn against an undefended site or smaller enemy minion depending on what other artifacts you've already played.


Merlin's Staff: Can turn your avatar or a minion into a dangerous attacker very quickly given that most of your spells only cost two mana. This is one of the cards that can allow Grim Reaper to weed out several enemy minions and decimate your opponent's offensive options by enabling it to survive multiple attacks.


Crown of the Victor: Best put on your avatar in most situations. However, this can go on Grim Reaper and significantly increase its longevity if it has already killed something and survived with the help of another clutch card like Grapple Shot. Has a similar effect of buffing Far East Assassin significantly with relative ease.


Screaming Skull: Another artifact that works most efficiently when on your avatar and turns it into a card advantage machine against aggro decks that play a lot of smaller minions. Alternatively, it also allows more offensive versatility by making it easier for your avatar to hit and run, attacking and killing a minion then moving back to make retaliation on the following turn harder for your opponent.


Seven-League Boots: The best movement boost mana can buy. This lets your avatar get around very easily and skirt around being intercepted, in some sense saving you a lot of potential life loss in the long run (no pun intended) without having to use up so many spells like Teleport and Blink. It's also another option for Far East Assassin and War Horse, as few minions are safe against them especially if there's also a Poisonous Dagger on the board.


Minions


Far East Assassin: Kind of works like a shadow copy of your avatar. In situations where your avatar is preoccupied, these guys can put pressure on the opponent from another angle. Their stealth ability allows them to approach close enough to pose an imminent threat, especially if you choose to arm them with an artifact like Merlin's Staff.


Grim Reaper: Should be held in hand until it has a high value target on the board to erase from your opponent's deck, ideally with War Horse or Seven League Boots to help it get around. It becomes a veritable milling machine if it manages to survive long enough to make use of Merlin's Staff and cast some direct damage spells with multiple potential victims like Firebolts.


Highland Princess: Only has three targets in the current list, but two of them (Amulet of Niniane and Ring of Morrigan) are indispensable assets to a Battlemage.


War Horse: Helps your avatar and all other minions be more aggressive by essentially giving them an extra point of movement as needed, which can be crucial to extending the life of smaller minions with potentially high impact like Grim Reaper and Far East Assassin.


Cerberus in Chains: Takes a lot of pressure off your avatar by serving as a big defender as early as turn three. You can be much more aggressive with this three-headed guardian always at your side. Putting Amulet of Niniane on it early makes it extremely difficult to kill until late game when it likely no longer matters that much. Also a good target for Grapple Shot since being dragged is not a voluntary action, and it will teleport back to your avatar once the spell resolves and your avatar moves again.


Magic


Blink: Worth a full play set for the fact that it's a cantrip and a cheap and versatile movement boost. Keeps your avatar out of harm's way after an attack and gets it around annoying sites like Free City and Troll Bridge in an instant.


Critical Strike: Functions essentially like another direct damage spell. Can make War Horse and especially Cerberus much more dangerous if you have the mana to pair it with something like Blink or Grapple Shot.


Firebolts/Magic Missiles: Simple and effective direct damage spells. Can ruin your opponent's day if cast by Grim Reaper wielding Merlin's Staff.


Blaze: Movement tech with a little damage tacked on to get through smaller minions and annoying tokens like soldiers and frogs that can otherwise slow your offensive to a crawl.


Disintegrate: Kills any unit that can be targeted regardless of its size. The range is limited but shouldn't be much of an issue given all the movement-boosting cards in the deck. Also useful if an enemy minion manages to steal an artifact and you can't afford to spend time and resources trying to retrieve it.


Grapple Shot: Amazing damage and movement tech all in one affordable package. This can enable Grim Reaper to nix multiple minions on the board or turn Cerberus into a high caliber bullet. You'll most often use it on your avatar as a kind of free attack as needed. It can also serve as a way of getting a small unit like Wisp or Princess through Gnome Hollows to finish off an avatar at death's door hiding for its life, costing you a friend but gaining you infinite style points.


Sites


Dark/Lone/Gothic Towers: A little bit of ramp to help your early tempo. Being ordinary means they won't get hosed by Atlantean Fate and leave you without Air affinity.


Dwarven Forge: Not many eligible cards yet, but invaluable for the potential to give you a turn one Poisonous Dagger or Merlin's Staff.


Funeral Pyre: Can save you some headaches against Deathspeaker if Grim Reaper doesn't show up in time to take enough victims. Also slows down Archimago if you manage to draw it early enough to matter.


Mirage: Handy tool for repositioning sites like River of Flame or Cursed Land as needed. Also good for letting you get more mileage out of sites with genesis abilities like Observatory.


Observatory: More spell selection for no mana cost. In fact, it gives you mana and Air affinity! Probably one of the most useful Air sites in the game right now and I can't find a reason not to include it.


River of Flame: Gives you a stationary Fire spellcaster that can't be destroyed as easily as most spellcaster minions. Has enough spells to work with to make it a worthwhile inclusion in the current list.


Ruins: Great to see in just about any opening hand and often worth taking a mulligan for to keep your site count low and your elemental affinity adequate.


Watchtower: Great site for protecting your side of the board from annoying trash like Infiltrate and stealth units armed with a Devil's Egg. Even better in multiples so enemy units have to fight fair while your Assassins don't.

deckinfo.name: 🇧🇷 Smoke Battlemage 🗡️🤚🔥
deckinfo.primer:
{{https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hOxOJ1Zp9Yg}}

VAI BRASIL🇧🇷


WORK IN PROGRESS


AGGRO UPDATE - March, 11th


Spell Changes:

[[Ruby Core]] and [[Amethyst Core]] - Felt like having the curve at 4 and using both cores on the deck just wasn't right. 2 chances in 60 cards, and drawing them late game when I needed some more gas was just terrible. Dead draws just lose you the game. Replaced by [[Key to the City]] and a [[Torshammar Trinked]]. Key can counter movement-imparing sites and the Trinket can not only give me more damage but also make my minions come out of fights alive.


2 [[Angel's Egg]] and 2 [[Daperyll Vampire]] were removed because as I stated before, I'd try to forget healing and just go straight for my opponents face. You don't need healing if you hit hard enough. Replaced by 2 [[Devil's Egg]] and 2 more [[Saracen Raiders]], this is just to put more pressure on the opponent and get that clocking ticking in my favor


[[Truesight Crossbow]] - Not facing many stealth units at the time and we got a better option with [[Peacemaker Arbalest]]


[[Telekinesis]] - Drew it once in all games I've had so far and have to say it I'd much rather have some minion with Charge instead, so I added another [[Recap Powries]]. Maybe running [[Sir Balin]] wouldn't be a bad choice, with the [[Grapple Shot]], [[Blink]] and [[Teleport]] it's just a great card, what kills it for me is it being Unique...(I know, i know, it's already powerful but I'm talking about how often I'd draw it)


Added a [[Sword and Shield]] just because I didn't like the idea of running 3 Trinkets.


[[Minor Explosion]] on the collection just felt redundant, still looking for a viable replacement but currently running [[Fade]] to have more utility


CONSIDERING: Maybe [[Sinterfee]] for the early game, idk


Site Changes:

Removed 1 [[Dark Tower]], 1 [[Lone Tower]], 1 [[Updraft Ridge]], 1 [[Sinkhole]] and both [[Remote Desert]]s. Felt like the changes favoring (F) would allow me to replace the (A) sites generating more mana with something more useful and aggressive such as [[Spore Spouts]] and since I'm running less Airborne creatures, figured [[Cornerstone]] would be the right choice with that idea in mind. Sinkhole is gone for [[Free City]]. I'd rather not sacrifice a site when I just need 4


_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


﻿



Introduction to Yours Truly


First off, let me say that playing Battlemage makes me feel like that kid that booted up Skyrim for the first time, picked up an Imperial Sword and selected ''Sparks'' on the spells menu. I get that feeling back every time I sit down to play with this Avatar, and ever since it came out, it became my obsession.


I got into MTG back when Brother's War was released, and started playing EDH and dipping my toes in Pauper from time to time. I've quit Magic for the many reasons everyone points out nowadays and started playing Sorcery by October,2025.


That being said, I'm doing my best to become a better competitive player and thought of coming out with this Primer to do just that. Plus, I get to help you guys out too!


I'll post some updates here whenever something changes or I come up with new ideas, explanations or even if someone points out something i didn't notice before (this happens frequently lol). Please forgive me if something isn't clear and point those out in the comments so I can fix it.


THIS IS BY NO MEANS, A META DECK. It's fun tho, lots of fun.


This primer attempt is inspired by my friends' primers, in which they did a great job at building. You can check them out below:


Archimago 🤌🍝 - Gothic Update - https://curiosa.io/decks/cmjn91zow1ye1zofnw1jhzth0 - By @gcampopz0r

Savior Steampunk Aggro 🐎🐈🐦 - https://curiosa.io/decks/cml9ursx601fb04l7dgolu81b - By @RaphaelFernandes



The Battlemage


Why him?:

Battlemage just fits my playstyle perfeclty. I think he's the best Aggro avatar out there, or at least with the most potential! I really don't care for making huge setups, waiting long for the perfect moment to do something or take the game to the 40+ minute mark. I just want to sit down and deal a lot of damage and finish the game so fast, people will think they just played cEDH and witnessed a turn 0 win (JK). Plus, since we're talking about an Avatar that is the actual star of the show, it is practically immune to Keyword effects, such as Mortal, Evil, Spirit, Undead etc...


Why (F) and (A)?

C'mon, I guess you guys already know why (F) is here...In case you don't, it's the aggressive creatures with Charge and spells that enable Battlemage to dish out some nice damage. The reason I picked (A) as the second element here is...the movement-GOD, THE MOVEMENT (A) GIVES YOU...ahem. Air is just perfect for movement and being able to assert presence on the realm anywhere, not only though Battlemage, but through your minions too. And don't get me started on [[Zap!]]. In my opinion, it just doesn't get any better than this.


What does it do?:

My Gandalf-Wannabe old boy here wants to get to your side of the realm ASAP, being the irremovable pesky 3-hitter he is at his basic level. He wants to be there hitting you and your minions on the face, with the support of his... and his equipment of course. And he'll be chasing you around the realm like you owe him a Foil [[Philosopher's Stone]] from Alpha. And, don't mind the damage taken, they're just minor flesh wounds anyway!



Strengths and Weaknesses:

This part is, I believe, to be somewhat subjective since I see a lot of diversity being present around BM from deck to deck, I'll use my deck as the baseline here:


Strengths:

  • Able to put A LOT of pressure at the early game
  • Has a ton of utility to really adapt to situations
  • Most of the time against another aggro deck, you have the upper hand
  • Foot soldiers and Skeleton Tokens are basically ''Hey, here's another card for you''
  • ''Charge'' creatures + BMs power really gives your opponent a beating


Weaknesses:

  • [[Witch]] is a very bad matchup. In my headcannon, she's his ex-wife or something
  • WARDS (F*ck those wards man)
  • [[Sphere of Animosity]] just completely shuts you down
  • Late game happens? Well, you sure are in a pickle
  • Opponent heals definitely put you behind on the clock
  • Sites that impair or prevent movement ( [[Gnome Hollows]] , [[Perilous Bridge]] etc,)



STRATEGY:

Now we're talking, here we go:


But first, a word from our sponsor


Just kidding, this is how it goes:


What you want to do is aggressively position your sites, directing them towards the fastest way to the enemy avatar. This is the general idea, most of the time I open the game like this:


S - Your site

O - Opponent's

X - Void


X X O X X

X X O X X

X X S X X

X X S X X


This site placement is perfect for you to get in there and just wreak havoc. Opening with a [[War Horse]] , [[Wild Fanatic]] and especially if there's already an enemy minion on your opponent's second site, [[Vile Imp]], is the best play here. I would also make a case of starting with any of the rocks: The Stone or the Cores. The cores would enable [[Cerberus in Chains]] to be present really early on here, and boy is that a power play


If you look to the decklist, you'll see that I designed the deck with a (unintentional, I swear) ratio of 50/50 Minions and Artifacts (Subject to change of course). Too often I see BMs with way to many Artifacts making it WAY Voltron (which if like I said before, you get Sphere'd or controlled or they bury your artifacts, you're toast) or using way too many minions (at this point, you're better of playing other Avatars)


AGAINST AGGRO


This is the base strategy you want to chase at turn 0 and if they're aggro, cause if you ''out-aggro'' them, you'll end up killing their minions and ''forcing movement'' of the enemy avatar or at the very least making them tap for sites. IF YOU KNOW WHAT YOU'RE PLAYING AGAINST and/or after you identify what is your matchup (Are they controlling? Are they taking this to the late game?) you adjust your strategy.


If you're hit with sites that deny your movement, you need to use [[Teleport]] , [[Blink]] or pincer your opponent with your sites, like so:


X X O X S

X O O O S

X X S S S

X X S X X


OR


S O O X X

S O O X X

S S S X X

X X S X X


[[Grapple Shot]] is awesome for dealing with these things, especially because of the ''may strike''. This means you can use your own minions to traverse the realm and not actually strike them. Perfect for dealing with [[Root Spider]]s


AGAINST CONTROL


When playing against Control decks, you KNOW they're gonna want to keep you at bay and take your minions out. In this case, the best thing to do is to be patient, lay your sites on your back row and let the enemy come to you.


X X O X X

X X O X X

X X O X X

S S S S S


''But Lentilha, what if by turn 3 the dude just casts some huge creature or something'' - Well, this decklist was tailored to my LGS meta, so if you find yourself somewhere with a lot of big creatures on tables, I'd recommend putting in some [[Disintegrate]]s, [[Poisonous Dagger]]s and [[Gift of the Serpent]].


Remember: You've got to beat them on the clock. You are gonna get hit, it's just a matter of who hits the most


MANA BASE:


If you pay close attention to the deck list, you can see that it doesn't go over (5) mana, with the exception of [[Poison Nova]] and the [[Daperyll Vampire]]s. That's because in most games, and mostly when you control them, I find that (4) mana is enough for the Battlemage to have a safe reserve to cast 95% of the deck. Mind you that a simple [[Critical Strike]] or a hit to a site + a [[Grapple Shot]] or [[Firebolts]] / [[Magic Missiles]] to the enemy avatar will deal 6 damage at the very least. So imagine what a BM could do if he has his equipment and minions on the board.


SUSTAIN:


(Little disclaimer: A friend of mine told me I need to reconsider this part right here and just change it for more damage output. I still want to try the healing here just in case things go south midgame, but I'll test a version without the sustain and will update the decklist accordingly)

Daperlly Vamp ladies that hurt the enemy AND HEALS YOU? FUCK YEAH I'M IN

This is important! Presta atenção!!! (Go Brazil🇧🇷)

  • [[Sandstorm]] - Maybe this will give you an extra turn on the clock or save at death's door for that ''Dude i'd would have had you next turn''

  • [[Spin Attack]] - Basically, A emergency [[Flaming Sword]] on a budget

deckinfo.name: "Pandemonium" SC 26' 12th Overall (6-2)
deckinfo.primer:
Sorcerer's Summit (Season 2)

This season, Bladedancer was able to perform fairly well against the field with a record of 16 wins and 10 losses. Below you'll find the performance against other Avatars.


Necromancer: 4-1

Druid: 2-1

Imposter: 2-1

Geomancer: 2-0

Corruptor: 2-0

Sparkmage: 1-1

Savior: 1-0

Enchantress: 1-0

Duplicator: 1-0

Archimago: 0-1

Avatar of Air: 0-1

Pathfinder: 0-1

Elementalist: 0-1

Battlemage: 0-2


On the Draw: 66.7% win rate

On the Play: 56.2% win rate


Deck Philosophy

This list focuses on fast, relentless pressure, using charge minions and equipment to overwhelm opponents before they can react. Every play is designed to maximize tempo and force your opponent into an immediate defensive stance, embodying the Bladedancer’s ethos of speed, precision, and relentless offense.


Strengths

  • Fast early aggression
  • Strong equipment with minion synergy
  • Keeps opponents constantly on defense
  • Flexible with targeted spells
  • High burst and finishing potential


Weaknesses

  • Low powered minions
  • Struggles vs board clears
  • Weak in late-game scenarios
  • Equipment dependent
  • Exploitable attack patterns


Sites

Understanding site placement and their effects are fundamental and is the difference between average and good players. It's the first (and easiest) concept you should learn about your deck.


[[Accursed Desert]]

Wards can be a pesky thing to deal with and if you're going up against [[Savior]], these sites may be useful early game. However, since Water seems to be prominent in the current meta, breaking [[Order of the Sacred Oak]]'s ward always feels good.


[[Active Volcano]]

Double Fire threshold. Need I say more?


[[Bureau of Occult Control]]

This site is criminally underplayed. If you're running a mono Fire list, consider going without [[Toolbox]] / [[Silver Bullet]] and run this site to force your opponents to pay an extra 2 mana to access their cemetery and collection. If your opponent is forced to [[Dispel]] or [[Disenchant]] your equipment or auras, it's going to take a total of 6 mana to get it done. Bureau is also effective against [[Imposter]] forcing them to pay 5 mana to transform. Guess they won't be transforming into [[Pathfinder]] anytime soon ¯\_(ツ)_/¯


[[Fields of Camlann]]

A well timed Fields of Camlann can tilt the odds in your favor if you allow your opponent to build their board. Look to play on turn 4 (on the draw) or turn 5 (on the play).


[[Forge]]

There is no other site I would rather play on Turn 1. Getting a [[Lance]] immediately in hand is like getting the corner slice of a brownie.


[[Plague Pits]]

Death is coming and there are usually at least 3 minions between both cemeteries by turn 5. Effective against any decks using recursion or utilizing the cemetery like [[Archimago]], [[Deathspeaker]], [[Flamecaller]], and [[Necromancer]].


[[Poisoned Well]]

This is another site that requires patience. Opponents are usually punished if they play sites all the way up to you, but if they remain hesitant for long, a well placed Well can deal 2 to 3 damage.


[[River of Blood]]

Many speculated that this site would deter players from utilizing [[Ring of Morrigan]], but that card is still strong simply for it's ability to deal damage by casting spells. You cannot allow your opponents to stabilize. Blood for the Blood God!


[[Sinkhole]]

There are a few sites out there like [[Troll Bridge]] and [[Perilous Bridge]] that are quite annoying to traverse through in order to reach your opponent. [[Gnome Hollows]] is also sometimes annoying if you already have [[Sword and Shield]] equipped. Then of course, there is [[Pebbled Paths]] which shuts down your charge minions. Blow up these sites and clear the way for you and your minions. If you're going first, a Turn 3 Sinkhole followed up with a [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], or [[Redcap Powries]] feels really good, putting more pressure on your opponent to draw a site on their next turn.


[[Vast Desert]]

Great for popping [[Skeleton]]s and [[Foot Soldiers]] or hitting 4 powered minions for 1 then trading a [[Redcap Powries]] into a [[Autumn Unicorn]] or [[Failed Mutation]].


[[Vesuvius]]

Blowing up and damaging all units around you for 3 can really save you in some tricky situations. Not only does it hit units on the surface but also the subsurface. Great for taking out a number of [[Frog]]s, [[Skeleton]]s, [[Foot Soldiers]], [[Coy Nixie]], [[Root Spider]], and any 3 powered minions. You can play this site in front of your starting site, but if somehow you can place it nearby your opponents starting site, that's even better.


[[Vindictive Nation]]

There is nothing worse than getting blown out by [[Realm-Eater]]'s site destroying capabilities. Second to that, is having all your minions killed by [[Earthquake]] and then rearranged. Nation forces your opponents to think carefully about the risk vs. reward of manipulating your sites.


[[Wizard's Den]]

There is no denying that card advantage comes at a cost. This site is particularly good in more aggressive decks, increasing the odds of you obtaining the cards you need early on to get the job done. Not much can be done against [[Phase Assassin]] or other stealth minions who are able to reach this site. I would always advise playing this site on your back row, but to the left or right of your starting site on turn 2 or 3.


Spells

Even in a Minion, charge-centric [[Bladedancer]] build, Magic spells are crucial for answering bigger threats and breaking through defensive walls that pure minion aggression can’t bypass. They provide targeted removal and control and tactical utility to keep your momentum intact and ensure your rush doesn’t stall against high-value or sticky enemy minions. Equipment-based Artifacts are exceptionally powerful on the [[Bladedancer]] because they directly amplify her damage output, turning her into a mobile, scaling threat rather than just a support piece. Since she can step and attack a unit after her first strike each turn, every equipment buff compounds across multiple attacks, allowing her to deal explosive damage and pressure multiple units in a single activation.


Minions


Charge Minions


[[War Horse]], [[Wild Fanatic]], [[Redcap Powries]], [[Monstrous Lion]], [[Saracen Raiders]], and [[Rebecks]]


These Charge minions are vital because they convert resources into immediate pressure, denying opponents the safety of a setup turn with opportunity of applying damage, reducing your opponent's life total the turn they are summoned. Instead of waiting a round to impact the board, they threaten damage, trades, or positional advantages the moment they enter play, keeping tempo firmly in your favor.


Low Impact Minions


[[Vile Imp]], [[Colicky Dragonettes]], and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]]


These minions influence the board the turn they’re summoned without needing charge or combat. Instead of relying on an attack step, they generate value through enter-play damage, chip pressure, or direct pings that soften targets, finishing weakened units, push incremental damage, and defeating opponents that are on death's door.


High Impact Minions


[[Cerberus in Chains]], [[Morgana le Fay]], and [[Boudicca]]


These minions must be dealt with by your opponent the turn they come into play or else their abilities allow them to heavily influence the match. [[Cerberus in Chains]] is a high-powered minion that follows [[Bladedancer]] and acts as both a great blocker as well as a minion that can dish out a high amount of damage. [[Morgana le Fay]] provides card advantage allowing you with more ways to deal with threats. It's worth noting that attacking with this minion while they have stealth is worthwhile as getting in 3 points of damage before casting her spells is ideal. [[Boudicca]] is useful because [[Bladedancer]] gets the added bonus +3 damage bonus on their first attack when hitting a site.


More to come on this primer...

Win the game without damaging your opponent and never leave your first site!


Stall out by playing everything to your first site, (deck plays bluecap so land is optimal) build a shell draw into mill combo and win. :)


Going to door is okay

Establish the shell and make them pull it apart to strike for deathblow.


Shell

A mix of...

Old salt dude

Tragedy dude

Shield maidens

Bodyguards

Baileys

Scarecrow

Or whatever stalls


Extra stuff for when shell is established

Queen of mid

Mother nature

Lilith (1 of a few good tutors for mother maiden crone with demonic contract)


Infinite mana

7 mana is needed with 1 turn of setup.

The site town with a homecoming aura in play nearby a horn of caerleon. On your next turn you will need to play out a lady isuelt nearby a town site and 2x bitten.

Play bitten with charge from horn nearby on the town, tap after the genesis ability strikes a bigger nearby evil unit and not the lady isuelt herself. Proceed to tap bitten to net 1 mana. Play second bitten out to town striking the tapped bitten which returns to hand via lady.

Cycle to net 1 mana each time.

(you do not need to chain off mana combo until you have a mother maiden crone in hand)


Infinite draw

Play her and pay 3 to draw from your deck until you hit all mill combo pieces


Infinite mill

The site town makes town priest free.

deckinfo.name: Transformers: Eldritch Horrors in Disguise
deckinfo.primer:
The Concept

This deck combines [[Blaze]], [[Mad Dash]], [[Leap Attack]], and [[Poison Nova]] along with submerge minions.

  • [[Blaze]], [[Leap Attack]] and [[Mad Dash]] can let your submerged minions surface and attack adjacent sites or minions.
  • [[Poison Nova]] can clear your opponent's minions without killing your submerged minions.


The Plan

Survive the early game with [[Porcupine Pufferfish]], [[Lake Afanc]], [[Adept Illusionist]], [[Plague of Frogs]], [[Tadpole Pool]] and [[Hillock Basilisk]].


Stabilize in the mid game with [[Panorama Manticore]], [[Selfsame Simulacrum]], [[Lord of Unland]], [[Ruler of Thul]] and [[Captain Baldassare]].


If you are being overwhelmed, your options are: [[Atlantean Fate]], [[Poison Nova]], [[Boil]] and [[Flame Wave]].


Put your opponent to Death's Door with [[Diluvian Kraken]] or [[Great Old One]]. Play the [[Great Old One]] or [[Diluvian Kraken]] below the surface then attack a vulnerable site with the help of [[Mad Dash]] or [[Blaze]].


[[Blaze]], [[Ruler of Thul]] and [[Flame Wave]] are good ways to finish your opponent once they're at Death's Door.


Arthurian Additions

  • [[Grim Guisarme]] makes a [[Great Old One]] a potential one-shot.
  • [[Shapeshift]] can transform a frog token into a [[Great Old One]]
  • [[Mester Stoor Worm]] can be surfaced with [[Leap Attack]] and then you can use it's ability at the surface.

deckinfo.name: Corrupt the Town
deckinfo.primer:
Welcome to the BEST combo deck Sorcery has EVER seen!


The plan is shrimple:

Assemble a Town (or Donnybrook Inn) with a Town Priest and Ring of Morrigan in hand!


With this, you can bring an opponent to Death's Door as early as turn 3, with enough card draw and life gain to sustain yourself against ANY deck!


Cards of note, if you plan on trying this deck out:

Silver Bullet and Call to War will always find you Town Priest if you do not already have one.

Ersatz Platz with almost ALWAYS grab you a Town. Usually your goal is to not draw a site for your card draw for turn unless you absolutely NEED to.

Highland Princess and Dream Quest should ALWAYS be used to find Ring of Morrigan if you do not already have it in your hand. Ring is the hardest card to find in your deck, so make sure to grab it ASAP!!!


Since there's no recursion for your Ring, ONLY play it when you assemble the full combo and intend to kill your opponent. If your Ring happens to accidentally be removed (through cards like Feast for Crows), then IMMEDIATELY swap to a Midrange gameplan. Stay alive, take out your opponent's minions, the swoop in for the kill! You'll have enough damage, trust me!


If you find any success with the deck, feel free to let me know on Discord (MVMagic), or find me on my YouTube (again, MVMagic)!


Happy slaughtering!

deckinfo.name: Storm of the light's bane

An angel bewitched by the shadows

Seduced by the whispering lies


This deck will use the synergy of demons with the addition of some angels, that, with the passive power of the corruptor, are also demons. There are demons who are stronger than Angels, or have the same power, but, with cards like fallen angel, witching hour and sites, the angels will have a good amount of power + ward and other effects


The overall strategy is use the demons and evil minions with the buffs they can gain to make good trades and get damage. The deck also has a good amount of spellcasters for an arcane barrage, or other good spells like pact with the devil, but also, to tap a shackled demon.


The deck works well with the minions being used with its strengths, but I think what make this deck have a lot of potential is doomsday cult, allowing evil to be cast from the top of your deck makes summoning demons much more fluid, and also allows you to focus on building your mana up for some more expensive minions. Of course, if you're facing someone that also has a lot of evil minions, you'll need to be Careful to where you position your doomsday cult, but in case you need, the deck also has disintegrate and other magic to deal with it.


So, good cards to have on your starting hand are: doomsday cult, fallen angel, the amethyst and ruby cores to help achieve the mana necessary for the bigger minions, or to be able to summon more minion with doomsday cult, Wich speaking of it, you can use the demonic contract to search for it, but remember that you'll need a elite demon to do it. It is Also important to hold sites that have (F) so you can play the important cards that require 2 (F) threshold

I didn't update it for Arthurian Legends due to me not thinking enough was added to make it worth playing, and other life situations that caused me to not be able to play as much. However, in Gothic, my passion has been rekindled.


I haven't tested the deck much yet, but based off of testing other decks and seeing where the meta is atm, this seems like a solid list.


I personally prefer another spirits list to this one, but I wanted to update this to be true to the OG Deathspeaker spirits. I don't think this is an amazing list as with the new 60/30 deck sizes, hitting your Ghost Ships and Evil Presences aren't as likely as they were in 40/20, but I don't by any means think it's a bad list; I wouldn't post it if I did.

deckinfo.name: SCGCon Atlanta 2nd place 5-1 Deathspeaker Earth Air
deckinfo.primer:
If you’re wondering “Why not card X?” Well…I’ve been playing this game for less than a month if you can believe it. I fell in love with the game and dove right in. During the event I traded my tickets for AL packs and opened the ring you see in the list at the end of round 4!!! I was so excited =). No Decklists…so in it went. Edit: I was asked to add a note to the primer. Judges were aware that I replaced a card in the middle of our no decklist tournament that wasn’t at compREL. Is it technically allowed? I honestly don’t know. I wasn’t shy about how excited I was and was telling everyone around me though =)


There were a lot of cards that didn’t really come into play much, but the early game and the repeated value are the core of the deck. We can play 1:1 removal because we’re going to get SO much value out of our cards. The mill sites were amazing. Observatory plus rats is incredible. Archangel Michael and Gargantula along with grandmaster wizard and master necromancer are our all star value cards to play from the cemetery.


The bolts and gifts were very often used to surprisingly put our opponent to door when they least expect it, doing 10 or more quite suddenly in one turn using the skeletal mages.


I’ve already taken the silver bullets out. Added a shrine of the dragon lord picked up at the event and making room to bump apprentice and novice back up to 4. Removed Gall as well. My opponents just weren’t using their collections enough, although I could see those coming back later in the year.


I want to try the 6 cost angels but I’m just trying to stay VERY focused on our plan at the moment and they don’t do anything from our cemetery.


My first 3 rounds all involved root spiders. I read the card before the event but didn’t realize so many people play these things. They constantly locked down angels, but I still found a way to chip damage and close with blots plus zap. After my third round I brainstormed with my opponent how to kill root spiders and all we could come up with is a burrowed rat with gift of the wolf for now. Every time I drew a toolbox I made sure to ask myself “should this just be zap or do I need it now”.


Water opponents are a problem. I lost to Mitch who played an unanswered Lilith into Pied Piper, two cards I didn’t even read before the event. After reading pied piper I just said “uh…yeah okay, I’m gonna go walk the hall. Congratulations.” lol…maybe I should have toughed it out, but he had already lured a unit, got a hit off of Lilith and established a frontline of troll bridge and thin ice. It was round 5 and I made the choice to relax before the last round.


6 rounds of Sorcery was incredible. I would repeat that day several times over if given the choice. I’ll definitely be back! Thanks for reading =)


Things I want to try next: I want to find some more room for top end. We can get a bit grindy with our tiny dudes and have some trouble closing. The bolts and gifts are really important for pushing damage but a touch more top end or mid could help. I want to try splashing red, but I feel like the double threshold sites really reward us for playing two elements right now with these powerful angels and triple threshold cards like gargantula. I do see how the red cards could give more closing power though. I didn’t like the tap requirement of silver bullets and the fact that we only have 2. I’m not sure what else to do with our collection yet but honestly it could just be 10 ordinaries.


I also want to try playing all of the cores with the red splash and the tri sites to have more access to playing from the opponents cemetery. ATM I do think the consistency of two elements is worth it.

deckinfo.name: Necronomicon - Meta Deathspeaker Updated for 60/30/10
deckinfo.primer:
Welcome to Deathspeaker 101!


This deck is adapted from the old Deathspeaker meta of the alpha days. The idea is to chip away at your oppnent's life total whilst controlling the battlefield and outlasting them with card advantage.


Of course, the old [[Nimbus Jinn]] combo still reigns supreme (draw cards and discard your genesis cards for "free" damage).


Deathspeaker ain't what he used to be, but he lives still!

deckinfo.name: Earth, Wind, & Fire
deckinfo.primer:
This is a “Jinn Combo” variant of deathspeaker that tries to use utility spells, removal, and prison sites in order to stall out the game long enough for you to a mass a large number of cards in your hand using wizards and wayfaring pilgrims.


Individual card breakdown:


Land surveyor, apprentice wizard, vile imp:


these are the bread and butter of most deathspeaker decks and more often than not these are going to be the targets of your common sense spells as well.


grandmaster wizard & wayfaring Pilgrim:


These are also card drying engines for you. Pilgrim is not really meant to go all over the board as that’s generally not possible unless you have a globe in play instead build towards one of your corners and use pilgrim as a pseudo wizard or land surveyor.


Morgana: she gives you more options when you first play her obviously, but she also can be used to mail yourself if you have a boneyard in your hand and need to look for a good target to resurrect.


Grain sparrow: at one point this deck had two grain sparrows which allowed for an infinite loop using Hamlet, ring, and lady iseult. I decided to cut one because I think it’s better off as a common sense target that can help gain you four life and defend against an attack.


lady iseult: this is one of the best minions in the deck as it allows you to recast your genesis minions over and over again.

deckinfo.name: DeathIsJustTheBeginning
deckinfo.primer: Greedy 4 color, mulligan wisely, watch out for charge, and ward. Gothic giving Deathspeaker a hard time.

deckinfo.name: Competitive - Gothic Deathspeaker is not Dead
deckinfo.primer:
Deathspeaker. He's back, but he never left. He's dead but never died. He actually got a bunch of new toys, like Arjaro Exorcist, Redmane, Jack the Ripper, One-shot Wizard, Flayer/Hotwheel, Legion of Gall, and Young Master (a.k.a. the late 90's Vampire:TM goth kid).


Magic is simply the greatest hits. And with more spellcasters in the deck now, Pact with the Devil is much more viable.


For Artifacts, the ramp is still there, you'll need it because you should have more cards than you can play in addition to your cemetery at any given moment. The Silver Bullet is slow but ensures you have whatever best spell you need. Use one of your Land Surveyors or some other dork to tap to use it. The Char Omphalos is on a probationary period, we'll see if it stays. And Ring. Just play the d*mn RING.


For Auras, Summoning Sphere for the OTK w/Nimbus Djinn and to allow you to better position your Genesis effects (like Imp, Hotwheel, etc.) Having both The Black Plague and The Great Famine gives you the ability to basically take out any minion on the board. And with the 41 other minions in your deck, throw one into the Aura's region as a sacrificial lamb to keep the effect going. Don't worry, you'll bring that minion back next turn for its Genesis ability. As it tries to scream but its brief existence precludes its ability to utter any sound. Salt the Earth is there to take out really annoying sites, like Kor Crematory. It’s a good tempo builder taking them down 1 mana and can more impactfully choke them out on threshold. It can also trap Pathfinder and slow down their minion’s path, especially with Perlious Bridge.


Sites. The double threshold sites are simply amazing in a three-color deck to drive consistency. I would add Mountain Pass, but the Towers, Bridges and Manor are simply too powerful. Geistwood and Boneyard remain as the sole non-threshold sites, they can be game-changing. Temple of Moloch is incredible with stuff you want to die anyhow so you can revive its wretched existence for a fleeting moment of sheer pain only to reclaim their last hope, like Princess, Land Surveyor, One-shot, and Apprentice Wizard.


Overall, don't fear all the new cemetery hate. Simply do what you do best. Draw more cards than them, cast them more quickly, and bring back the lifeless corpses of your allies to milk their Genesis abilities for fun and pain like the Gothic sadist you are.

deckinfo.name: DRAGONLORD
deckinfo.primer:
This is a ramp heavy midrange deck looking to take the initiative and produce threats quickly, breaking mana parody through cards like [[Dragonlord]] becoming [[Caelestis]], [[Black Obelisk]], the Cores and [[Shrine of the Dragonlord]], on-color Mixes and [[Four Waters of Paradise]], [[Cradle of Etherrum]], [[Frontier Settlers]], [[Camelot]], the air Towers, and [[Dragonlord's Lair]], and produce above rate threats quickly to outpace enemy minions and win quickly.


[[Azuridge Caravan]] is a huge connecting piece for the deck. It can be played with Caelestis for 0, reanimated by [[Dame Britomart]], buffed by [[Blunderbore]] and [[Rebecks]], summoned quickly by either of the Mixes, and be summoned through [[Crusade]] or [[Jihad]]. Crucially, it can also be summoned through [[Cradle of Etherrum]], which I think would be far less good without them in the deck (there are hardly enough good dragons to make Etherrum consistently cast dragons off the top when they can be).


[[Colicky Dragonettes]] is a card I don't think I've seen any other Dragonlord decks trying, which surprises me. Again, the deck needs dragons for some of the cost reducers to actually get value, but beyond that, this card is actually quite good. [[Moonsong Talagelum]] is, in my opinion, worth it here simply as a 3-power airborne that can be reduced down to potentially 0-mana ([[Camelot]], [[Dragonlord's Lair]], and [[Cradle of Etherrum]]).


Just to briefly explain some of my other card choices: [[Imperial Road]] can function as additional air Towers, except the mana is lasting. Yes, your opponent can also develop their mana quicker, but as you'll be the first one making use of that mana, you'll be slightly advantaged by it. [[Kingdom of Agartha]] effectively disables effects like [[Bury]] from destroying your expensive threats. [[Queen Guinevere]] allows you to attack twice with a single minion each turn, pretty significantly increasing your clock. [[Castle's Ablaze!]] and [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]] lets you gain and retain a mana advantage, which is pretty important for the deck to do. [[Cave-In]] can effectively do the same, but is more focused on removing artifacts like Cores or removing equipment from [[Battlemage]] (Cave-In will not kill minions if Agartha's effect is active). [[Excalibur]] is a huge boon for cards we already want, like Caelestis, Azuridge, and Guinevere, as well as [[King Arthur]], which protects your expensive stuff from cheap theft effects. I have specifically not chosen to include [[Wedding Hall]] because it overall weakens the deck significantly, and is an unreliable win condition, especially as Arthur should very much be sent to the front line quickly (that's not to say Wedding Hall is a bad card, but you need to specifically build with that plan in mind).

deckinfo.name: Joven's Dragonlord
deckinfo.primer:
Hello! I'm Joven, and this is my 4-Color Dragonlord Caelestis control deck. I really wanted to play something like this, and I am so excited to continue to work on and evolve it! "Next-Level Dragon Lord"! I've always had an obsession with 5-color control decks in magic, from Keeper in oldschool, to Chapin's Next Level Blue. This is my sorcery take on that style of deck, but with more DRAGONS!!


**Update - I have removed most of the Water element for consistency's sake, still tweaking!**


Here are explanations for my card choices:


Mana Rocks

  • Cradle of Etherrum, Four Waters, and Shrine are all well known and solid.
  • The real standout and best addition to this deck from Gothic (in my opinion) is Wiccan Tools! It might not seem amazing at first, but being able to have the threshold for a timely piece of removal or defensive creature is often great, but the REAL place this shines is when you have a dragon rotting away in your hand these, in combinations with the Dragonlord Caelestis ability, act like mini Dragon Lord's Lairs! AND THEY DRAW A CARD! Lovely. (Originally, I hade cores in here, then I tried Mixes, but I have to say, Wiccan Tools blew them out of the water in here!)


Other "Rocks"

  • The Toolbox tutor package opens up the ability to have solid answers when needed. Having 3 of these main, and 1 Common Sense side (and 3 main) is VERY important, as it allows you to Toolbox for Common Sense, then search your deck, later in the game this can be insanely helpful.
  • Angel's Egg is great, playing it early helps you stay in the game, and playing it late in conjunction with a Poison Nova/Earthquake/Murder of Crows wipe can completely flip things around in your favor.


Minions of the Dragonlord! On top of the (Obvious) dragons, the minions in this deck have been meticulously chosen, and I am constantly testing new ones. Here is where I am currently at:

  • Apprentice/Grandmaster Wizards draw cards and are spellcasters, that's enough for me!
  • Leprechaun trades and draws a site
  • Root Spiders are amazing, hard to remove and stop enemy minions dead in their tracks, an amazing defensive option.


It's Magic!

  • Dream Quest/Pact With the Devil - We are already playing 6 spellcasters, but now that we have Wiccan Tools, ANY of our minions can be spellcasters.
  • Disenchant, Lightning Bolt, Minor Explosion are the Common Sense package. They are interchangeable based on the meta, and I would consider Magic Missiles over Lightning bolt, but these are up to your local meta/preference.
  • Poison Nova, Earthquake, Cast into Exile solid minion removal.
  • Chaos Twister - I think this card is way underplayed, it guarantees you will kill 1 minion, but then it can ALSO wipe out all the minions on a site! And don't forget, if it the minion lands on the void and it doesn't have voidwalk, its banished!
  • Whirling Blades - Card is busted.

Sites

  • Dragonlord's Lair...duh.
  • Multi-Element lands: This deck needs to hit its colors, so it is playing all the fixing I own! If I get more, I will add it. I have also moved one of each Water Element dual site to the collection to fetch with with Ersatz Platz, as water is not a super important Element in this list, and this gives access to any other element needed.
  • Utility Sites - I chose to go with Cloud City and Rift Valley as a way to disrupt enemy plans, the towers for a little mana boost, Observatory as filtering, and active Volcano / Mountain Peaks as these thresholds are important.


The Collection:

  • Zap! / Grapple Shot- FINISH HIM!
  • Blink - Movement option
  • Magic Missiles - Removal
  • Common sense - This allows you to Toolbox for Common Sense, then search your deck, later in the game this can be insanely helpful!
  • Firebolts - Good cheap projectiles.
  • Unravel - Great against undead AND Weapons/Items!
  • Boil - There's a lot of water floating around, let's punish them!
  • Murder of Crows - Can wipe out a necromancer's army...TWICE! Can also sweep up 2 power minions late in the game.
  • Just a Rock! More like, just a way to painfully disrupt an opponent! A super solid piece of tech for getting rid of weapons and items, also tutorable with common sense!
  • Just a Rock!


Well, that's it for now! This is what I have come to from the limited testing I have done so far. The more I play, the more I will learn and I am positive this deck will evolve and change over time. Thanks for checking it out!


-JOVEN

deckinfo.name: Two Hotdogs
deckinfo.primer:
"Your avatar lets you have TWO hotdogs?"


For the record, I hate this avatar. More than I hate the Magician, despite both basically compromising the fundamentals of the game. This one has the highest chance to do the most damage, to the meta and to the market. Most people who have made lists thus far have no idea what they're doing, or are ignoring it because it prevents them from playing their favorite staples and it's just not feasible for such a young game.


But despite how limited the card pool is (only 256 uniques in the game, only 59 of them being sites) there's a surprising amount of variance in the possible builds.


Four options present themselves:

-Fire Evil spellcasters with Rasputin, Ompharoi and Pact with the Devil for draw

-Waterboys: Duel for Atlantis (Golden Dawn plus Ruler of Thul is really funny)

-Knights of the Round Table with all the four-element cards and a pair of round tables

-THE STONE OF ERECH AND THE PATHS OF THE DEAD, NEED SHALL DRIVE HIM aka Lord of the Rings Pinball


This is the last option, every good Mortal and Undead option possible within Earth and Air. Keeping it simple for release weekend. Can't run King Arthur because it shuts off the other kings.


Garden of Eden and Black Mass is a bit of a nonbo, but Garden is an absolute must for any deck with this avatar. It turns off the gas for aggro and makes common cantrips into a joke. You cannot afford your opponent to get any further ahead than he already is with your reduced starting hand size from holding your two hotdogs, and there's no other Archie counter in this rarity. If you don't draw into it, all your other draw effects will kick in at full power, and since most of them allow you to choose to draw sites, they can still get around it. You could run Gigantism instead of Black Mass to take advantage of Galahad's lifelink and recover from an aggro push more easily.


There is a very silly possibility of repeatedly abusing Death's Door. Playing Orpheus' Crossing after Mount Ussar Sanctuary to repeatedly give yourself a Ward. Basically make it Death's Revolving Door.


If you're enough of a madlad to throw upwards of a thousand dollars at dwindling singles, but not mad enough to get two Cornerstones worth of Dragonlord, this is the deck to prove your dad lets you have two hotdogs. Yeah yeah, Jake decks named after food, funny that it happened twice.
