deckinfo.name: 🇧🇷 I G N I S D O O M †  ::  Harbinger Smoke Competitive
deckinfo.primer:
{{https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jG3rZMAu9gU}}


I G N I S D O O M † 🌪️🔥


Hi!

Here i bring you my take on a midrange smoke (A)(F) build on the coolest (and sometimes underestimated) Gothic avatar: [[Harbinger]]!

Let’s start our doom chants and begin to summon devilish creatures from hell!



0. WHY HARBINGER?

You go for Harbinger, if you like ✅:

a) Luck-based “mini games”: You start the game already playing against your luck: three rolls that can define your opening hands, site’s placement and how much of aggro or control you will be in the starting turns.


b) Big bad creatures: Harbinger truly shines outpacing your opponents, curving big minions with the discount, even better if putting them in the opposite sites for good trades and early aggression.


c) Midrange strategy: With this deck, rapidly you can switch from aggro to control (and vice versa) and often the best moments for you are in the midgame.


Maybe don't go for it, if you prefer ❌:

a) Consistent openings: The portal placements can be brutal sometimes, leaving you already in disadvantage before the game really starts.


b) Fast-aggro or hard-control: The super fast and cheap minion strategy lovers, as well as the hard-control players, can find this strategy clunky, with heavy (and sometimes hard to cast) minions or not so much flexibility and gas in the late game.


c) Super strong meta killer decks: Although i think this deck can be really strong (specially if well played and with some luck with the rolls...) this is NOT a tier-S meta killer deck. If you want to go for the obvious options, maybe Harbinger is not for you.



1. THE IDEA

ex abysso ignis nascitur

The main idea behind the deck is how to better leverage from Harbinger’s passive signature ability: get 3 minion spawn squares – possibly including your opponent’s sites and also voids – with the discount of (1), once per turn.


Harbinger can be built on a wide variety of elements, but after some tests, my preferred one is smoke: air (A) for better exploitation of voidwalk, positioning, removal and overall good collection options and fire (F) for great aggressive minions and finishers.


My first take on [[Harbinger]] was oriented towards water (W), which can also be very good, considering the wide variety of great powerful new minions from Gothic (you can check the list here: 


Water (W) w/ splash Air (A) List : https://curiosa.io/decks/cmim4cz4o0084lc04os56yuvs


After some tests (and also considering the growing popularity of mono-water lists with [[Necromancer]], [[Pathfinder]] and even [[Savior]]) I switched to Air (A) + Fire (F). So let’s dive in!



2. THE ELEMENTS

silentium mundi frangitur


a) AIR (A):

Arguably the best color in Sorcery (sorry wet-heads (W)!) here is the place [[Harbinger]] shines the most. The main collaboration for the deck are:


AURAS

Three great auras that can impact game: [[Summoning Sphere]], because as you will see, sometimes the luck is against us with Harbinger passive ability and we need more strategic spawning options. [[Eclipse]] again can help us a lot with positioning and also beef-up our Evils (we have +25 sinful dudes around). [[Sphere of Animosity]] because it can be just backbreaking in some match-ups (hi [[battlemage]], hi [[pathfinder]]).


MINIONS

In the minion’s realm, for air, we have two great keywords at our disposal: airborne and voidwalk. [[Gibbous Nightgaunts]] is our bread-and-butter here, specially if it can be cast on turn 2, using the (1) discount. We also have a sub-theme here: VAMPIRES! Come on in, [[Daperyll Vampire]] and [[Renatus Trueblood]] two amazing flyers that can really outclass races with aggro match-ups and put us back away from death’s door. [[Hounds of Ondaros]] is a BEAST that is hard to remove and can be summoned early in the void.


MAGIC

Finally, the real spotlight for air (A): the magics. We have [[lightning bolt]], [[grapple shot]] and [[whirling blades]] as flexible cards that can be used aggressively our defensively (these ones specially effectives if combined with a vampire). Great to close the match.

 

b) FIRE (F):

Fire (F) brings more relevant options of minions: [[Barging Barghest]] for another dude that can be cast on turn 2 in the void with good mobility, [[greater blood demon]] for a cheap, dumb beater and [[clamor of harpies]] and [[askelon phoenix]] for two more flyers that can devour weak minions. Fire true stars are [[infernal legion]] (imagine casting this bad boy in a opponent’s site for (5) mana, burning their minions and/or avatar on turn 4 with the help of a ramped [[Lone Tower]].. just…. *chef kiss*.



3. DECK COMPOSITION


a) STRENGHTS:

  • Strong and impactul minions, which can often be cast with discount (1), in your opponent's site and also have a lot of mobility (lot's of flyers);
  • Flexibility to switch between aggro and control stances;
  • Life gain with vampires;
  • Reliable options to close the game after death's door;
  • Overall good control and reach of the realm, including voids;
  • Can make epic swing backs (heavy burst damage if not responded);
  • Good match-ups: [[Witch]], [[Necromancer]], [[Pathfinder]]


b) WEAKNESSES:

  • Weak against heavy removal / board wipe decks;
  • Difficulty to deal with wards (dependent on one [[bane of aventis]];
  • Can be outrun by fast aggro, while also be outclassed by late game control;
  • [[Harbinger]] ability progressively loses relevance through long games;
  • Portal rolls can be dentrimental for your strategy;
  • Early game can be slow;
  • Bad match-ups: [[Savior]], [[Archimago]], [[Deathspeaker]] and some Fury Roads

 


4. SET UP - OPEN THE DOOM PORTALS 🌌🎲

ignis portas abyssī aperit

Well, let's talk about portals. Before you keep your hand, you roll the three squares on the realm where you will place your portals and see where you will have the advantage to cast your hordes. As already mentioned, luck can be on your side (or not!).


______Opp Avatar_____

A. [01] . [02] . [03] . [04] . [05]

B. [06] . [07] . [08] . [09] . [10]

C. [11] . [12] . [13] . [14] . [15]

D. [16] . [17] . [18] . [19] . [20]

_____Your [[Harbinger]]___


Let's say your opponent's avatar starts at square 03 and you on 18.

At the first glance, you can think that the best portal places are 02, 03 or 04, right?

Although, yes, they can be awesome depending on your oppening hand and opposing deck, they can also not be ideal.

The same goes for, let's say, portals on 17, 18 or 19 - at first you can think they are bad places to have portals because it's not on your opp's face... but these can also be great for defense against aggro decks or saving you in the late game!


So, it's good to remember:

  • It's best to have the portals spread out through the realm, spammimg different rows, for maximized options of aggro and control positioning along the game;
  • Defensive portals matter;
  • Outer colums kinda suck, but here voidwalkers can be your friends;



5. EARLY GAME / OPENING HANDS

After your portals are active and ready to go, you see your opponent's avatar and you see your first 6 card hand.

What you want to see?

In general:

  • At least one offensive and one defensive portal - preferable in the 3 mid colums;
  • 1-2 minions with airborne / voidwalk / mobility;
  • Opportunity to leverage your portals in the first 2-3 turns with good minions;
  • Varied threshold (A) (F) and acceleration ([[lone tower]], [[gothic tower]], [[dark tower]] and [[city of glass]]);
  • Utility sites for mid rows ([[wuthering heights]], [[fields of phyxis]] and [[vindictive nation]] are relevant here);


BE CAREFUL!

Don't overpush it and put all your threats fast. You need to be aware of board wipes and bad trades that can threaten your mid game.

Try to save some gas for your opponent's response.


Watch out for [[Root Spider]], [[coy nixie]], [[thin ice]], [[Chains of Prometheus]] or bigger early drops as [[lugbog cat]] and [[Autumn Unicorn]]



6. MID GAME

Here is your time to shine. Ideally, in the mid game you have good minions in place and you are the aggressor, while also having some other threats in hand for scalability. Focus on pushing the damage and keep the minions comming and be mindful of your mana usage. Use your portals wisely, flanking your enemy army and opening different attack opportunities on different places of the realm. Your main goal now is to lower your opponent's life fast for a death's door - a well timed [[desecrate]] or [[grapple shot]] can be key.


Sometimes, in heavy control / attrition games, at this point you can have difficulties in asserting a constant wave of threats, so it's important to secure a "refill option". Try looking out for [[grandmaster wizard]] or even a [[book of the dead]].


Watch out for [[earthquake]], [[atlantean fate]], [[the black plague]], [[poison nova]], [[Divine Healing]]



7. FINISH IT UP

ignis ultimus omnia devorat

If everything went well, now your opponent is already at a low life and you have controled their threats.

Be careful with big late game decks, such as [[archimago]] and [[deathspeaker]]. The correct philosophy for this deck is "strangulation due to constant pressure" and not only as a glass cannon that only leaves your opponent at 1, 2 our DD life but can't finish it up.

Try to save a [[hotwheel]] in hand, or maybe even a [[infernal legion]]. We have great options in the toolbox as well with [[lightning bolt]] and the classic [[zap!]].


Watch out for [[Craterize]], [[Amulet of Niniane]] or big comebacks with [[infiltrate]], [[ruler of thul]]

 


8. THE COLLECTION

Finally, for the collection i bring flexible options:

  • 1x [[Desecrated ground]]: Part of [[desecrate]];
  • 2x [[Ghoul]]: Could be summoned with [[forsaken Crypt]] and [[Young Master Damion]];
  • 1x [[Disenchant]]: Getting rid of [[Atlantean Fate]], [[ring of morrigan]] or other trouble-makers;
  • 1x [[Displace]] and 1x [[Teleport]]: For positioning;
  • 1x [[Lightning Bolt]] and [[Zap!]]: Insta damage / finishers;
  • 1x [[Minor explosion]]: As a more tactical removal for stealth / grouped enemies;
  • 1x [[Murder of crows]]: Recursive global chip damage / removal of skeletons against [[necromancer]];



Have fun opening portals! 🌌

Thanks for reading!

By: machinagro 🇧🇷

deckinfo.name: 8 mass 🧂 Imposter Site Denial
deckinfo.primer:
# Overview


Another site destruction deck, huh? Site destruction decks have a bad rep because Magic-brain has told you it won't work in Sorcery. After all, you destroy a site then next turn they just draw another one. You destroy another site and they just draw another one. Again and again. A temporary stalemate until they eventually blow you out with all their minions that you left on the realm because you were busy wasting your time on their sites. However, I have an alternative theory:


Fill the [[Rubble]]. If you fill the [[Rubble]] that you created from destroying their site, you close off the options your opponent has to keep playing sites. If you do it right, they'll have no ability to play more sites and you'll control the entire realm. This is why site destruction is different in Sorcery than it is in Magic. You can contest the realm.


This doesn't solve the fact that if you're busy killing sites while they're busy playing minions, you'll lose. However, I'm asking you to shift your mindset a little bit with this deck: The primary goal isn't about site destruction, it's about locking them out of the realm. Then, that's when we focus on destroying the sites they do have in order to completely lock them out from the rest of the game.



# The Game Plan


Phase 1

Your strategy is to race, and you're racing specifically to lock your opponent out of the realm. This means that we care deeply about playing extra sites and you do this with [[Landmass]], [[Common Sense]], and [[Frontier Settlers]]. In fact, you should care so deeply about this, that you probably want to mulligan anything else with the hopes of finding one of these. If you're still not finding anything, mask up [[Seer]] and start searching harder. Utilize what you have to try to cut them off and then you can pivot to phase 2.


Phase 2

You're done racing and now you're going to try to pivot to controlling the mid-game. This means controlling the minions on the board with spells like [[Cave-In]], [[Poison Nova]], and [[Earthquake]], and site destruction with [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]], [[Castle's Ablaze!]], and [[Raze]]. You also want to be building up card advantage, which you can start doing by masking up [[Pathfinder]]. This will allow you to play sites while still drawing spells. Once you're done playing sites with [[Pathfinder]], switch to [[Sorcerer]] and begin getting as much card advantage as you can.


Phase 3

Now you need to close out the game. Hopefully, your opponent sees the writing on the wall and concedes. But sometimes the salt gets the best of people and they hold out hope that their deck will provide a miracle. Mask up [[Necromancer]] and begin flooding the realm with minions. There are also a couple heavy hitters in the deck like [[Lord of Destruction]] which will help speed things up, but slow and steady is fine here. If minions aren't doing the trick, mask up [[Witch]] and start using the tap ability to make your opponent lose 2 life.



# Imposter though, really!?


Some of you might be wondering why we're not just using [[Pathfinder]] or [[Realm-Eater]] and building a more traditional site destruction build. The answer is simple, I think this is more versatile.


[[Imposter]] gives us the ability to switch to those avatars when it makes sense and get some extra value, but it also allows us to build a more traditionally tuned deck and not have to have filler cards to compensate for their weaknesses (i.e., movement or site restrictions).


Learning how to play [[Imposter]] is complicated. But when you master it, you'll feel like you're a chess grandmaster with a vibrating device inside of you, giving you all of the right moves to make.



# Notes Worth Sharing


🧂 Use [[Root Spider]], [[Entangle Terrain]], and [[Quagmire]] to lock minions into a [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]] or [[Castle's Ablaze!]] The spider will survive and be burrowed under the [[Rubble]]. Also [[Root Spider]]s are amazing for [[Raze]], again because they survive the destruction and usually go under the radar beforehand.


🧂 [[Sow the Earth]] doesn't say adjacent to your other sites... it can be played to any void square. Use it to cut your opponent off.


🧂 IMPORTANT: The "Establish your Domain" rule only counts for turn 1 of the game. After that an avatar can play a site either adjacent to an existing one they own or as close as possible to their avatar if no other sites exist. This means that if you destroy all their sites but there's still some empty voids around the realm... they can play a site on the other side of the realm. So don't cut them off entirely until you've already filled up the realm yourself, or you could end up with a minion on your doorstep.

deckinfo.primer:
TESTING IMPOSTER AT THE MOMENT! Feel free to swap out Imposter for Seer and add in a playset of toolbox plus whatever toolbox targets in the collection instead.



(OUTDATED PRIMER)


THE DECK THEME: This is a versatile, combo/control  deck that focuses on playing [[Roots of Yggdrasil]], [[Candlemas Monks]], & [[Orb of Ba’al Berith]]. These three cards are the bread and butter of the deck & they are the keys to tipping the scales in your favor to win the game. 


THE COMBOS: 


[[Roots of Yggdrasil]] + [[Sinkhole]] & [[Bedrock]]

  • Roots of Yggdrasil destroys everything in the realm, including sites. You can take advantage of this destruction by playing BEDROCK. 
  •  [[Bedrock]] gets around the wrath of [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] and does not get destroyed. Smart placement of BEDROCK can put you up on mana & block your opponent from playing sites after blowing up [[Roots of Yggdrasil]]. 
  • SINKHOLE & CRATERIZE is the only way in this deck to destroy your ROOTS so use them wisely. 


[[Candlemas Monks]] + [[Crave Golem]] 

  • When you play a Candlemas Monks in range of a Crave Golem and pass the turn, it will skip your opponents entire next turn, (except for start of turn triggered abilities). Which essentially gives YOU an EXTRA TURN!
  • You can then chain this combo by playing your Candlemas Monks Raise Dead + Kythera Mechanism to skip up to FIVE TURNS!!!


THE FINISHERS: 

  • [[Amazon Warriors]] is a 5 power 5 cost minion that you can tutor with common sense and play after destroying a roots with at least one earth threshold out. This puts your opponent on a four turn clock if they don’t have an answer. 
  • [[Roaming Monster]] is a 4 power, 5 cost minion with one air threshold. If you can spare the time to wait one extra turn to destroy roots, you can destroy roots and then play an air site to summon roaming monster anywhere on the board where you can get damage in. Also ordinary for common sense! (OMITTED FROM LIST)
  • [[Highland Clansmen]] is a 5 power, 7 cost minion with CHARGE. This can be a beater in a game where you aren’t finding roots and the charge ability can guarantee your swing for 5 with proper placement. It is also an ordinary which can be tutored by Common Sense. 
  • [[Orb of Ba’al Berith]] is one of the best value engines in the deck. With enough setup this can outright win you the game if left unanswered. Orb of Ba’Al Berith can let you copy any magic spell cast nearby ONCE PER TURN. Gigantism, Browse, Divine Healing, Raise Dead, Border Militia, etc. all of these casting twice can swing the game in your favor if you are able to stabilize. Remember Orb of Ba’al Berith includes your opponent and opponents spell casters so your placement matters if you don’t want your opponent to get those free copies!


P.S. Play this deck with caution. It will make your friends sad :,(

Deck Philosophy

I started out learning to play Sorcery in March of 2026 trying to make aggro work. The Gothic water meta made that very hard. I bounced off of [[Persecutor]] and [[Bladedancer]] and had some fun learning (F)(E) Furious Road [[Witch]]. The latter drew me in because of the very tight game plan: Ramp asap to 4-5 mana, and burn them down with aggro minions and [[Witch]] tapping.

This wasn't quite good enough and couldn't often compete with the card advantage and card power other decks have.


I then realized Imposter could solve all of these problems and make an even better deck. This deck removes the ramp and combat tricks found in earth (E) from Furious Road for the [[Pathfinder]] mask for consistent ramp. You upgrade the earth combat tricks for air (A) ones, and add a few other cards that synergize with other masks you have access to. You lose [[Witch]] deal 2 tap ability but I think I'm dealing more average damage per game with [[Flamecaller]] mask than I ever did with the [[Witch]] ability. On top of that, with Witch you have to tap 4 times get to 8 damage, Imposter does it for (3) mana and a single tap which is cheaper and I regularly get 8 (F) in my graveyard (my record is 18). On top of all that, early aggression is a perfect match to the critical [[Imposter]] problem of keeping heat off of the avatar while wearing the [[Pathfinder]] mask.


After some tuning this deck is running between 75-85% win rate on the Sorcerer's Summit.


Game plan

Start off as strong as possible with aggressive turn 2 and 3 plays, setting your opponent up for a difficult decision when you put on the [[Pathfinder]] mask. Leverage the card advantage from [[Pathfinder]] and your suite of high pressure minions and spells to close the game out, often with a big [[Flamecaller]] tap. Keeping the [[Pathfinder]] mask on for 2-3 turns is huge card advantage that is very difficult for enemies to deal with when they're trying to stay above deaths door against a low curve aggressive deck.


I've added [[Mix Ignis]] and [[Four Waters of Paradise]] as [[Imposter]] loves mana. Even drawing a mix late can enable mask changes that would have otherwise been impossible. They work great making [[Archimago]] turns possible, and they really shine enabling strong turn 2 and 3 plays setting you up for a solid few turns on the [[Pathfinder]] mask.


This deck is setup to execute on that plan as consistently as possible. I've tried to only keep cards that do one or more of the following:

  1. Make my first three turns as consistent as possible and trick out higher cost minions if possible.
  2. Threaten damage to the enemy avatar.
  3. Are great cards that are made even better with a specific mask.
  4. Are incredibly strong cards.


Weaknesses

  • Artifacts: In this meta I haven't been seeing many artifacts that blow me out. That being said matchups like [[Battlemage]] and [[Persecutor]] can be tricky if they get good artifacts out. Depending on the meta you may need to tech a [[Toolbox]] for [[Dispel]] or [[Shatter Strike]].
  • Early combo: Decks that can trick out early bombs with cards like [[Four waters of Paradise]] are hard for anyone to deal with when they hit. Your turn 2 and 3 is stronger than most decks so you can start pathfinding but if you're on the back foot already, things are very difficult.
  • [[Interrogator]] decks can be tough to deal with. All their cards that hit your avatar directly make it very difficult to keep a mask on and cards like [[Sphere of Animosity]] stop you from pathfinding. You'll need to try to play defensively and stabilize as your later game will be generally better.
  • [[Savior]] and decks with lots of ward. In higher ward metas you probably want to tech in more desert sites. As is, you can deal with 1 or two a game with cards like [[Colicky Dragonettes]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], but lots of ward becomes tough to deal with. Your minions won't often out-power your opponents so dealing with them might require 2-for-1ing your self.
  • [[Mismanaged Mortuary]] is rough as it stops [[Flamecaller]] which a lot of this deck is built around. [[Bureau of Occult Control]] is also annoying as well as it makes [[Pathfinder]] inefficient to cast though it doesn't stop your [[Flamecaller]] plan. Get [[Asmodeus]] or try to silence these sites.


Mulligan

Here's what I'm thinking about during the mulligan in rough priority order.

  1. Look for a strong turn 2 and 3 play. Any (2) mana minion will be fine on turn 2, though 2 (3) drops with a tower can feel very oppressive. Plan on playing cards like [[Hemogoblin]] and [[Sinterfee]] on turn 2 even without effect so that you have board presence when you put on the [[Pathfinder]] mask. Remember they are worth [[Flamecaller]] damage in your graveyard and if your opponent is dealing with them, they're not taking you off of the [[Pathfinder]] mask.
  2. The threshold to play your turn 2 and 3 play.
  3. Depending on your matchup you'll want to prioritize the following next.
  • Against non-Pathfinder decks you suspect to be running water look for site disabling abilities. [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] and [[Fields of Phyxis]] both feel amazing in the center of your second row. So many defensive sites slow down your game plan and removing your opponents ability to rely on them is pretty critical. [[Sinterfee]] counts here too. Especially on the draw, you can often play her turn 2 to disable the site in front of you. Pathfinder, even mono-water has less control over site placement and silencing is less important.
  • Against other decks look for anti-healing cards. This becomes even more important against earth, but air also has all the healing minions. No matter the match-up, I rarely mulligan [[River of Blood]]. [[Hemogoblin]] is also a very nice card here as it can block cards like [[Divine Healing]] from having any effect and 2 threshold also feels very good when counting pips for [[Flamecaller]].
  1. Turn 4 and 5 plays that can pile on the pressure or turn it back on after putting on the pathfinder mask. Cards like [[The Black Plague]] feel amazing on turn 5, after pathfinding, followed up by a turn 6 [[Enchantress]] and a (2) or (3) drop (animating the aura) is very strong.


The best possible sequence looks something like this: 1. [[Active Volcano]] -> 2. [[Dark Tower]] + [[Màzuj Ifrit]] -> 3. [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] + [[Redcap Powries]]. Its hard to deal with seven power (4 of it airborne) coming at you with no site defenses. You might be able to skip pathfinder and just go for the win if both minions hit.


[[Mix Ignis]] enables turns sequences like 1. [[Mix Ignis]] 2. [[Asmodeus]] 3. [[Redcap Powries]]. Destroy their site and get in damage.


Depending on your opponent and play/draw you can also consider using a tower to go to (3) mana on turn 2 to play [[Pathfinder]]. This works better on the play, where your opponent will only have 2 mana to react with to take the mask off. Playing [[Pathfinder]] turn 3 instead of a minion play can be a worst case last resort, but I've found that the your opponent will often have an answer that takes the mask off and means your turn 3 did nothing. The pressure even a 2 site [[Pathfinder]] mask applies with this deck is hard to handle, but skipping a turn early makes this deck pretty tepid if it doesn't work out.


In 90+% of games after turn three you should either have 2 minions in play or have the pathfinder mask and a (3) minion out as well.


Deck Tech

  • [[The Black Plague]], [[The Great Famine]], and to a lesser extent [[Wildfire]]: The enchantress mask makes these so dangerous for your opponent. Both of the uniques are a minimum 1 for 1, but then any cantrip or [[Grapple Shot]] turns them into a massive damage threat as well as a 2 for 1 if they move on top of a new minion.
  • [[Grigori Rasputin]]: You love to see 2 fire pips here, and it feels great to flash him back onto [[Vile Imp]] or [[Mazuj Ifrit]]. I haven't yet double cast [[Bane of Aventis]] using him but one day...
  • [[Hemogoblin]]: One day this card will probably get cut, in lower healing metas I could see cutting him now but 2 mana, 2 fire pips, and block healing is very good for this deck. Think of cards like this as having a +2 damage on them for flamecaller later. It makes including them and even drawing them early feel pretty good.
  • [[Morgana le Fay]] is a uniquely powerful card, and pretty unfair but there are a couple reasons its even better than average in this deck. It fills up your graveyard for [[Flamecaller]] with just this card (3 from morgana, and any you discard when she dies). She also can't be blocked from stealth so three damage from her attack is wonderful. I regularly cast her adjacent to an enemy site, then before casting a spell on a subsequent turn, attack from stealth, then cast one of her spells. I don't see her survive long after breaking stealth either way, I love to get some damage out of her.
  • [[Màzuj Ifrit]]: A recent include to make my turn 2 and 3 more consistent and higher pressure. (4) damage fliers are amazing and even better on turn 3 (or even 2 with a tower). In a pinch they can also deal with a vampire for you.
  • [[Sturmgeist]]: You gotta have good reasons to be missing fire pips on your minions, but Sturmgeist is one of them. Its amazing early game pressure, and synergizes very well with [[Interrogator]]. Early game make sure you have the threshold to play it, and late it feels amazing to put on the [[Interrogator]] mask, hit with a minion and then play [[Sturmgeist]] to put your opponent in the blender.
  • [[Saracen Raiders]]: An obvious include, I just had to cut one to fit an extra (2) or (3) drop, probably should add a third but struggling to decide what to cut.
  • [[Sir Lamorak]]: A very oppressive fire/air card. No immediate damage, but very hard to play around and deal with.
  • [[Browse]]: Without my more evenly split site base I'd cut this card, but too often it can find me the answer to close the game. It also is a nice graveyard filler for [[Archimago]] mask.
  • [[Warp Spasm]]: Love this card, with all the combat tricks you can end up in pretty crazy turns, buffing a charge minion to close the game.
  • [[Mix Ignis]], [[Ruby Core]]: Early 1-drop ramp feels great on turn 1 and not horrible later. It enables access to top end cards that are harder to get out otherwise. They also make cards like [[Death Dealer]] and [[Major Explosion]] a lot easier to cast. Having an extra mana late game might mean an extra card draw from [[Sorcerer]] mask instead of just burning 2 mana.
  • [[Asmodeus]]: A great site destruction card, can take effect right away with some forced movement.


Sites

Even Though I'm mostly in fire I run lots of air sites to make the higher threshold air cards like [[Browse]] more consistent, there's also a ton of great air sites like, [[Wuthering Heights]] and the towers. I'd love to fit cards like [[Open Grave]] for turn 1 plays but haven't found the room if I want the full suite of anti-heal and silence (which I do). [[Forge]] is in there for a turn 1 play but will probably eventually be cut. [[Mirror Realm]] Is a standout, allowing multiple plays of your unique sites. I often keep [[Mirror Realm]] if I have it in my starting 3 and draw a site instead of playing it so I can surprise opponents with it later.


Cut

There's a lot of great cards out there that raise the ceiling of this deck. I've often made the conscious decision to lower that ceiling for early consistency.

  • [[Torshammar Trinket]]: I ran 2 trinkets for the first few weeks of running this deck, they're definitely great with all your charge minions and cards like [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], but ended up cutting them in favor of early fire minion consistency. I found my losses were to early combos and aggression and trinket didn't ever feel good to draw early. Artifacts also don't synergize with any of my masks. I think cutting it raises the floor of this deck while lowering the ceiling a little bit. The trade off is worth it.
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]]: Pretty much the same issue as trinket. Its a great card, even if I'm often not getting the heal since I play [[River of Blood]], but in a [[Swap]] meta I've found it doesn't stick very often. Not to mention I have so many combat tricks to close the game, I'm not really missing the Death's Door utility.
  • [[Toolbox]]: I ran 2 of these for a while as well. They're obviously good, but I found them to be too slow too often. I already have so much flexibility with [[Imposter]] I found I'd rather be drawing a (2) or (3) drop directly than a toolbox. You also get access to lesser used but still powerful avatars if you run 10 avatars in your collection. [[Persecutor]],[[Interrogator]], and [[Sparkmage]] might all be cut to make toolbox worth it, but each of those are useful in specific contexts. There's a real cost to fit it in.
  • [[Boudicca]]: I probably should be running this card, but I rarely have 2 minions on board ready to swing, and [[Boudicca]] for one proc of three damage doesn't feel amazing. Charge minions are better. That being said its 3 fire pipes which fits right in. I don't mind cutting it and definitely will in paper where this card is pricey.
  • [[Bane of Aventis]]: I used to run it but added deserts to more consistently deal with ward, its floor is a little low for my taste.

deckinfo.name: Brown Stax
deckinfo.primer:
This is my attempt at an Earth "stax" style deck, locking the game down and winning with some direct damage or grind. But it can pivot a few ways.


--


Gameplan


Go [[Pathfinder]] early and generate sites while you play lockdown stax pieces to gum up the board.


Pivot into [[Archimago]] (with good spells in cemetery, like [[Craterize]] or [[Divine Healing]]) or [[Witch]] (-2 repeatedly) to win the game.


Go [[Ironclad]] if you get the [[Golden Harp]] or [[Goswhit Helmet]].


The remaining Avatars are situationally good.

  • [[Enchantress]] can be used to animate opposing auras and destroy them.
  • [[Sorcerer]] is great late game when you need raw draw to grind the win out.
  • [[Geomancer]] can be a Pathfinder alternative and a recovery after [[Roots of Yggdrasil]].
  • [[Seer]] can be effective in digging for our Roots package.
  • [[Avatar of Earth]] can be a huge surprise damage source, even if you only attack once or twice before the mask is removed.


We are also running a [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] package with [[Bedrock]], [[Sinkhole]], [[Crossroads]], all of which can be fetched out with [[Pathfinder]] potentially. We are fine blowing up the board and replenishing our sites relatively easily with [[Geomancer]].


[[Assorted Animals]] helps us get [[White Hart]] or [[Root Spider]] for lockdown, or [[Gargantula]] for removal.


Most of your minions and artifacts are prison/stax pieces, with a lot of disabling and silencing effects. Our sites are also very defensive. We aim to win via our Avatar abilities.


--


Thanks for reading!

deckinfo.name: Landmass Imposter
deckinfo.primer:
Use defensive sites and minions to make it hard to directly damage your [[Imposter]]. Ramp with [[Landmass]] and mana rocks to give yourself plenty of mana for morphing.


Playing against aggro? You're [[Ironclad]]. Small enemy minions nearby? You're [[Battlemage]]. Ready to turn the corner and pressure back? You're [[Avatar of Earth]].


Playing against midrange? You've got access to [[Sorcerer]], [[Savior]], and [[Archimago]] for huge value.


Playing against control? Put your first three sites into play and then morph into [[Pathfinder]]. Opponent has a strong site nearby? You're [[Realm-Eater]]. Got some minions near their avatar? You're [[Interrogator]], closing the game.


This deck doesn't have a ton of fire minions, but by the end of the game, it is likely that you can deal the killing blow with [[Flamecaller]].

deckinfo.name: Dungeon
deckinfo.primer:
I didn't think Snagged would survive into Gothic, but Erik's Curiosa blessed me with some new cards, so I present the successor to Snagged, Dungeon! Many adjustments to come and you can see my introduction video here on my channel Lord of Itza!


April 28, 2026


Removed


Spellbook

Added


Spellbook

As great as Gargantula is, the three earth threshold was hold to come up with, so it has been replaced by the versatile Arjaro Exorcist.


March 13, 2026


Removed


Spellbook

  • 4 Drowned
  • 1 Kettletop Leprechaun
  • 3 Order of the White Wing
  • 2 Overbearing Bailiff
  • 1 The Lady of the Lake
  • 2 Mimic
  • 1 Lilith
  • 2 Bury

  • 1 Ice Shards

Atlas

Collection

  • 1 Extinguish
  • 2 Shoggoth


Added


Spellbook

  • 2 Polar Explorers
  • 3 Autumn Unicorn
  • 1 Failed Mutation
  • 2 Gargantula
  • 1 Ruler of Thul
  • 2 Sacred Stag
  • 2 Lord of Lies
  • 1 Led Astray
  • 1 Swap
  • 2 Into the Abyss
  • 2 Smite
  • 1 Call of the Sea


Atlas

  • 1 Gliman House
  • 2 Mismanaged Mortuary
  • 3 Pond
  • 2 River Rapids


Collection

  • 1 Bury
  • 1 Drown
  • 1 Ice Lance


This is a massive update for Dungeon and represents my most recent build. A large number of minions were changed in the deck, many that were personal favorites of mine like Drowned and Overbearing Bailiff, but were less effective than other options. I also finally gave up the Mimics, as Swap is a superior choice and more than enough, especially with 2 Dispels in the Collection as well. I also removed the Order of the White Wing, though I am still waffling on this decision because this minion is quite sticky and has a nice additional ability. In place of these minions, cards like Ruler of Thul and Polar Explorers were added to provide my minions with another option to strike the enemy avatar. In addition, more beasts entered the deck, including Autumn Unicorn making a return, as well as Sacred Stag and Gargantula. I also revamped the removal spells considerably to try out some new cards from Gothic, most notably Into the Abyss and Smite. Earthquake was also traded out for Call of the Sea given the heavy prevalence of water in the current meta. The Atlas also saw some changes, removing Deep Sea since it was redundant with the Flood Plains, as well as the creature generating sites. In their place, new staples from Gothic stepped in, and Ponds made a return due to the large increase in the number of beasts in the deck. Finally, a few cards left the Collection to be replaced by some of the removal that was in the main deck previously.


I am strongly considering Innsmouth Dock and Abaddon Succubus, but deciding on which cards to remove for them has been a struggle.


December 20, 2025


Removed


Spellbook

  • 3 Autumn Unicorn
  • 3 Estranged Loner
  • 3 Guile Sirens
  • 1 Ruler of Thul
  • 2 Gloam Toads
  • 1 Questing Beast
  • 1 Kiss of Judas


Atlas

  • 2 Pond


Collection

  • 1 Horrible Hybrids


Added

  • 2 Acid Rain
  • 4 Drowned
  • 3 Order of the Sacred Oak
  • 1 The Lady of the Lake
  • 2 Failed Mutation
  • 1 Bury
  • 1 Ice Shards


Atlas

  • 2 Peculiar Port


Collection

  • 1 Extinguish


This updated version of Dungeon went 3-1 in the Newport, Kentucky Cornerstone. Cutting the Gloam Toads really hurt my heart, but they just did not feel effective. Kiss of Judas was also a card I hated to cut, but every time the card came up, I hated seeing it as my draw. Cutting the Autumn Unicorns was a big change, but with site destruction lurking, I felt the Order of the Sacred Oak was a better option. The one change I may rescind is returning Ruler of Thul and removing Lady of Lake. I also felt that the Guile Sirens were overkill with Coy Nixie in the deck, and the Estranged Loner were cut for Drowned. I found that having an additional two drop, especially one that could hide submerged, was most helpful.


I did learn a lot at this event. Ward is far stronger than I ever imagined, and the Orders in this deck did a ton of work. The ward was able to protect an Order in my opponent's subsequent turn and then it would be primed to Meathook in the next turn. I was extremely disappointed with Lady of the Lake and I think Ruler of Thul would have been the better option. The Acid Rain were also very helpful, shutting down my options sites, particularly those that silenced my own defensive sites. I will say that I encountered one Savior with considerable warding, and so I may look into Silence effects to help remove them.


December 11, 2025


Removed

  • Fertile Earth
  • Pond


Added

  • Watery Grave
  • Mirror Realm


Somehow I forgot Mirror Realm, which can be another Thin Ice or Troll Bridge. Watery Grave could also be a nice token generator with the Thin Ice and Nixie/Siren combo. I was hesitant to remove a Fertile Earth, but it seemed like the best opponent among tough choices. The Pond was also a tough choice, but it feels less reliable with the increased Spellbook.


Decemeber 10, 2025


Removed

  • 2 Root Spider
  • 2 Failed Mutation
  • 2 Order of the Sacred Oak
  • 1 Deep Sea


Added

  • 3 Order of the White Wing
  • 3 Guile Sirens
  • 1 Thin Ice


Bruce at Golden Eagle Cards tried my deck out and said that Thin Ice with Coy Nixie was incredibly powerful. So, I added a Thin Ice and opted to remove a Deep Sea since there is so much water threshold in the deck. I also decided to cut the Order of the Sacred Oak because even though I am terrified of site destruction, I think Necromancer and token hordes will be more prominent initially. I have also found that effectively getting Root Spiders into play can be difficult, so they were cut as well. Finally I removed the Failed Mutations. While they are an awesome card, there cost of 4 means that they cannot Meat Hook until turn five. In the place of these six cards I added three Order of the White Wing for anti-token and collection plays and 3 Guile Sirens to maximize Thin Ice. Guile Sirens is limited to only moving minions, but their three power means they can submerge on Thin Ice by luring in anything of 2 power or more, so they feel worth testing. I am also strongly considering getting more copies of Led Astray into the deck because of the power of Thin Ice.

deckinfo.name: Voidwalker Aggro
deckinfo.primer:
Hello There Sorcerers!


I've wanted to build an Aggro Voidwalkers Deck ever since i realized the power of Voidwalk, this is my shot at that. This Decks Theme focuses heavily on getting in your opponents face extremely early to do direct strike damage against their Avatar using Voidwalk Minions, Stealth, and other Sneaky means such as Betrayal. Card draw is the name of the game with Interrogator so we want to make sure 2 things happen.


  1. If our opponent plays an early Garden of Eden we want to get rid of it fast. I usually despise using Land Hate cards but in this deck it's necessary to counter The Garden of Eden's effect. Land hate in the deck includes Castle's Ablaze, Salt The Earth, Year of The Blaze, Lord of Destruction, Asmodeus, and Lord of The Void. I've thought about adding a Key to the City as an extra counter to Garden of Eden, but as the current rulings stand Players and Avatars are defined differently therefore your avatar would still be restricted to you only being allowed to draw 1 Spell a turn.
  2. We want to make sure we're able to deal direct strike damage to the opponent's Avatar to gain extra cards. This deck has a myriad of ways to hit your opponent very early and consistently. Giving your Minions Stealth using Spells like Fade or Vanishment is a guaranteed way to deal direct damage, and can add serious insult to injury if you repeatedly Stealth cards like Asmodeus or The Lord of Destruction. Another excellent way to deal direct strike damage is by using spells like Whirling Blades, Blaze Of Glory, Shatter Strike, or Leap Attack.


Notable Synergy Cards


The Malleus Maleficarum - You just drew The Malleus Maleficarum? Congratulations, you just unlocked all your AOE spells and game finishers like Zap and Lightning Bolt. Replace your Collection with what you please and have fun.


The Rack - This card can win games quickly and efficiently by dealing extra damage to your opponent and forcing their avatar to take up more space, therefore making it much harder for them to escape your Minions.


Lord Of Fear - He works great with Interrogator's triggered ability. It's easier to hit your opponent's Avatar when they need 2 blockers for each attack you're sending at them.


Lord Of Destruction - Don't even get me started on this fella, he's nuts. If you can get this guy out on turn 3 or 4 using Gothic/Dark/Lone Towers, Ether Core or a Four Waters Of Paradise it's going to be a serious issue for your opponent. Not to mention if you use cards like Fade or Vanishment on him you can destroy your opponents sites for free without fear of being blocked.


Asmodeus - Continuously Stealth him and break Stealth to eat sites or use him to deal direct Avatar damage and draw more cards.


Char Omphalos - Gives extra card draw


13 Treasures of Britain - Gives extra card draw, even more powerful when combined with Kythera Mechanism.


Kythera Mechanism - Can be used in conjunction with the 13 Treasures of Britain for extra card draw. It also can control where you teleport your Headless Haunts and Hauntless Heads.


Darkest Dungeon - This one is perfect for pulling the enemy Avatar over to our side of the board and going to pound town. Just be aware it only drags the enemy avatar if your minion and them can both be drug in a path on sites across the realm. You can't just hit your opponent on turn 2 with a Hauntless Head and teleport them over to your side of the board before a "bridge" of sites has been made to the enemy Avatar.


River Of Blood - It's essential to have 3 of these in the deck to counteract Healing effects from our opponent. This pressures them to continue to let us draw cards from Interrogator instead of taking the 3 damage to then heal themselves the next turn.

deckinfo.name: Scour the Mind
deckinfo.primer:
First go around with a Mist Midrange Interrogator build!


Love the value this avatar brings for both aggressive and controlling play styles.


Early Game Focus

  • Starting Hand will determine early threshold goals but generally will value water threshold priority
  • Set up artifacts if drawn into or drawn into starting hand
  • Push for early game board presence with early game control/value minions
  • Winter Nymph
  • Coy Nixie
  • Grim Reaper
  • Nelly Longarms
  • Lugbog Cat
  • Jack the Ripper
  • Aino
  • Early game Browse Targets
  • Aquamarine Core
  • Silver Bullet/Toolbox
  • The Green Knight
  • Jack the Ripper
  • Aino
  • Summoning Sphere

Mid Game Focus

  • Board State and opponents choices on early trades will determine our strategy heading into midgame
  • In early/mid game we want to leverage Interrogator ability and your early turns determine whether you will push the opponent into a defensive strategy if they take the extra life loss, if they choose to give you card advantage however you will know they are setting up for a play so you can prepare a defensive counter strategy
  • If the opponent is playing aggro, fall back on the midrange minions or swing tempo with removal spells


  • Continue to build board control if unhindered with aggressive/sticky minions to get trade value with Interrogator ability
  • Phase Assassin
  • Gyre Hippogriffs
  • Sturmgeist
  • Ruler of Thul
  • Failed Mutation
  • Thing in the Ice
  • Daperyll Vampires
  • If behind or fighting or board control use forced movements on creatures or removal spells (Toolbox & Silver Bullet) to swing tempo back to your favor
  • Abaddon Succubus
  • Lacuna Entity
  • Nelly Longarms
  • Coy Nixie
  • Magic Removal
  • Cast into Exile
  • Lightning Bolt
  • Grapple Shot
  • Drown
  • Tempo Swings!
  • Browse
  • Mesmerism
  • Swap
  • Browse targets Mid Game/Closing Prep (matchup dependent)
  • The Green Knight
  • Ruler of Thul
  • Sphere of Annihilation
  • Summoning Sphere
  • Removal
  • Cast into Exile
  • Lightning Bolt
  • Grapple Shot
  • Drown

Late Game/Closing Out Focus

  • Interrogator can close games out very quickly with various set ups but more often than not we are going to be attempting to box the opponent in with smothering waves of damage from unlikely sources
  • Pushing in with your higher curve minions via site damage trades can push opponent to DD quickly depending on opponents choices
  • Claim the win with
  • Ruler of Thul
  • Summoning Sphere
  • Sphere of Animosity
  • Finish the opponent at DD via
  • Direct Minion strikes
  • Lightning Bolt
  • Murder of Crows
  • Grapple Shot
  • Counter defensive strategies
  • Summoning Sphere to get over wall strats
  • Sphere of Animosity to deny healing and wall off opponent from minion help
  • Clearing blockers/ threats with Forced movement minions/Tempo swing spells
  • Lacuna Entity
  • Abaddon Succubus
  • Coy Nixie
  • Nelly Longarms
  • Swap
  • Mesmerism


Hope you all enjoy this build as much as I am and would love to hear any thoughts on improvements!


Edit- v1


Cut the creatures down a bit to get to 32 creatures as I felt it needed more control aspects through straight removal


Also depending on local meta Return to Natures can be swapped for Magic Missles if graveyard hate isn't required


Edit v2


Cut River Sites from 5 to 2 to add 3 Thin Ice Sites after online testing

deckinfo.name: Inquisition
deckinfo.primer:
Core Game Plan: Pressure Early, Punish Relentlessly


This deck is built around The Interrogator as an aggressively slanted avatar that turns early combat damage into an impossible choice for your opponent:

lose life faster than they can stabilize, or give you card advantage.


The Interrogator’s ability is the engine that ties everything together. Whenever one of your allies strikes the enemy avatar, your opponent must either pay 3 life or let you draw a spell. Early in the game, most opponents will try to pay the life. The problem? This deck is designed to make that decision hurt immediately and repeatedly.

The goal is simple:

  • Deploy threats starting turn two
  • Bypass or invalidate blockers
  • Force early avatar strikes
  • End the game before opponents can fully develop their mana or board

This is not a grindy control deck. It’s a low-curve, high-pressure tempo deck that wants to end the game while your opponent is still setting up.


How the Deck Wins

1. Early Minions, Immediate Pressure

The deck runs an extremely high minion count (40 total), skewed heavily toward low-cost threats with:

  • Charge
  • Movement bonuses
  • Airborne or Voidwalk
  • Stealth on entry

These traits all serve the same purpose:

get to the enemy avatar as fast as possible.

Most games start with minions entering play on turn two, often already positioned dangerously close to the opponent’s back line. If a minion can strike the avatar even once, it’s already done its job.


2. Site-Based Positioning Is the Real “Combo”

This deck doesn’t rely on a single card combo—it relies on site placement and movement synergies to break normal board rules.

Key sites like Spore Sprouts and Wuthering Heights allow you to:

  • Summon low-power minions directly onto enemy sites
  • Skip front-line defenses entirely
  • Move minions an extra step the turn they enter play

This means creatures that normally need multiple turns to reach the avatar can:

  • Appear adjacent to it
  • Strike immediately or on the same turn cycle
  • Force Interrogator triggers before blockers exist

Against slower decks, this pressure can feel overwhelming very quickly.


3. Auras and Artifacts Remove the “Fair Game”

Your minions are intentionally small and efficient—so the deck compensates by removing your opponent’s ability to interact cleanly.

  • Summoning Sphere accelerates deployment and positioning
  • Sphere of Animosity prevents avatars from being defended or healed, which is critical when your creatures would otherwise trade down
  • The Rack will punish the enemy avatar by adding additional life loss for every time it gets hit while at the same time making them a easier target to hit as they would be in multiple locations.
  • Small power boosts from trinkets push damage just high enough to:
  • Avoid unfavorable trades
  • Increase the punishment when opponents choose to pay life

Once Sphere of Animosity is online, your opponent’s avatar becomes isolated, making every successful strike far more dangerous.


4. Life Total vs Card Advantage: The Interrogator Trap

Early on, opponents often choose to pay the 3 life to avoid giving you cards. That sounds reasonable—until the math starts stacking up.

A single strike can represent:

  • 2–3 base damage
  • +3 life paid to Interrogator
  • Often repeated multiple times per turn

Very quickly, opponents find themselves at a life total where they can’t keep paying. At that point, the deck pivots naturally into card advantage—refueling while still attacking.

Either choice they make pushes the game closer to your win.


5. Punishing Interaction and Blockers

If your opponent tries to stabilize by killing your early threats, the deck is ready:

  • Avenging Angel turns dead minions into lethal counter-pressure
  • Stealth, airborne, and voidwalk creatures bypass traditional blockers
  • Movement spells reposition attackers mid-turn to open new attack lines

Even defensive plays often create openings instead of safety.


6. Just Enough Top-End to Close

While the deck stays mostly under the four- to five-mana range, it includes a small number of higher-impact threats:

  • Cards that dominate mirrors
  • Minions like Lions and Blood Demons that outclass opposing boards
  • Finishers that turn pressure into inevitability

These aren’t the plan—they’re the insurance when the game goes a turn longer than expected.


Matchup Philosophy

  • Against slower decks:
  • You are the aggressor. End the game before they stabilize.
  • Against creature-heavy decks:
  • Bypass, reposition, or punish blockers rather than trading evenly.
  • Against mirrors:
  • Your selective top-end and removal give you an edge without diluting the main plan.


Final Thoughts

This deck doesn’t use Collections and doesn’t rely on long setup turns. It wins by breaking spatial expectations, forcing early avatar contact, and turning every strike into a meaningful decision.

If you enjoy:

  • Fast games
  • Aggressive positioning
  • Making your opponent feel like they’re always one step behind

Then Rico Char delivers exactly that experience.

deckinfo.name: The Rock, the Roll. [Gothic]
deckinfo.primer:
This primer is very out of date (two years out of date!) but most of what I go over is still relevant. I'll be updating this soon with relevant info once I've thoroughly stress tested this build. Thanks!


"Jund 'em out!"


This deck seeks to recreate the gameplan of The Rock archetype, a.k.a. Junk, Jund, or GBx Midrange, from Magic: the Gathering — Disrupt, Remove, Overwhelm. In Sorcery's current cardpool, there are several cards that can push a positive trade in resources — or, in other words, answer two-or-more of the opponent's cards for the price of one of ours. With this deck, we intend to push those cards to their fullest, and with that core, fight a long-term attrition battle, forcing them to answer threats inefficiently while playing efficient removal of our own. In this primer, I seek to explain fully my thinking with the deck, but please let me know in the comments if you try this deck, what your experiences are, and what your thoughts are. Thanks in advance.


{{https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wMsazR6Tnf8}}


Why Sorcerer?

Compared to other Avatars.


Several Avatars can lead this deck well. [[Battlemage]] can remove several minions in a turn, goes fantastically well with [[Cerberus in Chains]], and has the capability to develop the same sort of card advantage [[Sorcerer]] aims to. [[Avatar of Earth]] can potentially represent a "free" win condition, and punishes opposing [[Men of Leng]] and [[Spectral Stalker]]s. [[Pathfinder]] is able to develop your sites without the cost of ever having to draw from your Atlas. However, these avatars each lack two things: linear reliability, and preservation. In other words, they do not consistently show results during the turns they need to for this deck, and they actively encourage strategies that are jeopardizing at low life totals.


Sorcerer, on the other hand, does not need to move to be effective, which is relevant for our defensive sites ([[Free City]], [[Gnome Hollows]], [[Bedrock]]), and its second ability is paramount to the deck's gameplan of always playing 2+ spells per turn in the mid-to-late game.


The Deathspeaker Problem

A.k.a. the "Boogeyman" Problem.


[[Deathspeaker]] Combo-Control can easily become very difficult to keep pace with in the late game. The deck has access to [[Grandmaster Wizard]] and [[The Geistwood]], presenting a very powerful card advantage combo in the late game, and Deathspeaker's ability to replay GWM and [[Wraetannis Titan]] in the late game for their Genesis abilities presents easy 3+ spell turns, meaning they can answer threats and develop their own win condition very rapidly.


This deck aims to answer the Deathspeaker match-up by becoming the proactive deck, developing discard engines in the early game to force Deathspeaker into a non-optimal mid-game, where we can capitalize and gain both tempo and card advantage. Additionally, a considerable portion of the sideboard aims to keep pace with Deathspeaker and similar decks in the late game when the traditional Men of Leng strategy cannot be executed (see Sideboard Guide).


Core Cards

These cards are currently considered core to the deck's strategy.


[[Men of Leng]] - Anyone who has experienced a turn one or turn two Men of Leng followed by a [[Grapple Shot]] the following turn knows full well the potential of this card. It is effectively a kill-on-sight card, demanding an answer quickly, before it can begin to cause issues. For clarity, Men of Leng combos with Grapple Shot (on a following turn) by having Men of Leng grapple onto the opposing Avatar, striking them once, and then striking them again as an action. Even in situations where this might kill the Men of Leng, ie. against a Battlemage, Avatar of Earth, or another equipped Avatar, this is worth it. Note: The number of copies of Grapple Shot change a lot with what minions I am currently testing, and this number will continue to change as I continue to experiment. The current number simply feels optimal to me at the time of the last update.


[[Adept Illusionist]] - This card is worded in such a specific way that allows it to truly shine, especially, I believe, in this deck. For two mana, it is near perpetually a four-power minion that is often impossible to remove completely and still feel good about it. It forces non-optimal decisions from your opponent, and is deceptively threatening. Consider this: in the situation where one is played early, ie. turn two or three, and removed on your opponent's following turn, their removal is essentially wasted the moment you can play and activate the second one, and in the scenario that both are answered, you have forced your opponent to use most likely some combination of [[Firebolts]], [[Vile Imp]], or [[Lightning Bolt]] to remove just two power each. It's a damned if you do, damned if you don't threat.


[[Atlantean Fate]] and [[Earthquake]] - Core to many archetypes, both of these cards are capable of answering several cards for our one. They can be used to kill several minions, and to gain considerable mana advantage when they take out opposing mana-accelerants. Atlantean Fate also has the capability of shutting off the opponent from their ideal elemental threshold, acting as a pseudo extra-turn spell when played into an optimal situation.[[Atlantean Fate]] and [[Earthquake]] - Core to many archetypes, both of these cards are capable of answering several cards for our one. They can be used to kill several minions, and to gain considerable mana advantage when they take out opposing mana-accelerants. Atlantean Fate also has the capability of shutting off the opponent from their ideal elemental threshold, acting as a pseudo extra-turn spell when played into an optimal situation.


[[Frontier Settlers]] - This card is pretty common, inocuous, and often overshadowed by [[Land Surveyor]]'s instantaneous value, but its ability to ramp us quickly to our desired 5-6 mana goal puts it above Surveyors for me in this deck, despite the advantage of Surveyors (reducing the number of for-turn draws spent on sites/increasing the number of spells drawn overall), which is quickly mitigated by the Sorcerer's second ability anyway.


Notable Inclusions

These cards are currently played, but not currently considered core, and have potential to be cut.


[[Royal Bodyguard]] - This card was a difficult card to assess, but has so far been often game changing. It is pretty often difficult for most decks to remove cleanly, its a headache for Voidwalk-centric aggro decks, and complicates multiple combos, like [[Summoning Sphere]] + [[Nimbus Jinn]]/[[Wraetannis Titan]] and [[Orb of Baal Berith]] + [[Craterize]]. It has the advantages over [[Divine Healing]] of accounting for wasted overhealing, preserving your Avatar at Death's Door, and for doubling as a damage dealer.


[[Captain Baldassare]] - It may be easy to mistake this for the deck's win condition (more on that below), but I would classify it more as a card advantage engine, one which simultaneously threatens the opponent's life total. It cannot be understated how much more powerful casting your opponent's discarded [[Bury]] is than the Bury in your hand. He is yet another must-answer threat that can quickly develop a huge swing in card advantage.


Questionable Inclusions?

These cards are more likely to be cut, with specific reasons given for each.


[[Highland Princess]] - The value of this card comes largely in the ability to at best draw [[Philosopher's Stone]], and at worst draw a Core, and that's nothing new to anyone. However, I would argue that not all decks want Highland Princess. In this current build, I believe the deck does want her, not only because of the power of Stone in a three/four element deck, but because we play so many double-threshold cards. However, with only a few changes to the deck, that becomes considerably less relevant, and the deck's mana curve was specifically tailored to cast an average of two spells per turn in the mid-to-late game, making Stone less must-have.


Wincon? What Wincon?

And why they're overrated.


Eagle-eyed deck sharks might have noticed that this deck does not represent any particular win condition. No [[Wraetannis Titan]], no [[Nimbus Jinn]], no [[Craterize]], and no [[Panorama Manticore]]. Not even a [[Bosk Troll]] or [[Autumn Unicorn]]! This deck is looking to close games out slowly, with chip damage, and dealing the death blow with board presence, or a tutored [[Firebolts]] or [[Vile Imp]]. My closest consideration that resembles a late-game beater so far has been [[Hounds of Ondaros]], because it's so reliably difficult to kill. [[Amazon Warriors]] is also worth considering, as it's tutorable with [[Common Sense]]. I also think [[Withering Hero]] is a pretty solid rate, but too weak to site-based removal. But against most match-ups, I haven't had the need for a traditional top-end finisher.


The deck typically wins by two methods. Designed to go long, the primary gameplan is to get ahead on resources, remove or disable threats, and amass an overwhelming boardstate. The other gameplan is the "gank" method, in which a tempo [[Pudge Butcher]] can hook the opposing Avatar, strike it for 5, and enable a scenario where you can strike the Avatar in your own site with several small threats, ideally [[Men of Leng]]. If curved out correctly, this forces the opponent to make horribly nonoptimal plays, and represents a very fast clock.


Chaos Twister

The Dexterity Dilemma.


For the time being, I will be testing this card again, and I'm willing to reassess my prior position. That said, I still believe the design of the card is fundamentally bad for the game.


I'm choosing to not play [[Chaos Twister]], because I don't believe the card is good for the game, and because it's impractical to play on Tabletop Simulator in a way that feels authentic to the card. That said, the card has a good probability of getting at least a 2-for-1, and is a very strong option, viable to replace one or two copies of [[Bury]].


Thanks for reading, I appreciate all feedback. More updates are to come. Enjoy!

deckinfo.name: Interrogator River Snag
deckinfo.primer:
Your goal: Get your opponent's avatar closer using various hook / drag effects and go to town.

If that turns out to be tricky, just bring the fight to them by connecting the opposite edges of the realm or taking advantage of extra movement.

If you got a trigger or two off your Avatar and the board state allows for it, draw & play a site next turn. You'll quickly push to 6 or even more mana, allowing you to double spell consistently. Drawing many spells early on is nice, but keep in mind that you are drawing for card selection in that case. If you don't need it, go for sites and push ahead on curve.


If you see one of the hard counters, such as [[Garden of Eden]], [[Root Spider]], [[Bottomless Pit]], [[The Void]], [[Gnome Hollows]], ... shift your game plan to a standard Steam aggro-y midrange plan. If they spend their defensive tech on their home site, just go for regular site damage.


Hear me out on [[Mirage]]: Worst case, just play it as a vanilla fire site. But it's wonderful with [[Heirloom Lost]], because you return a site you OWN. Additional targets include shifting a [[River Rapids]] out of a silence effect or another chance at [[Darkest Dungeon]].

Update: Out again for now to include Tri-sites and include [[Mesmerism]]. Still a valid choice I think, will keep testing.


[[Aino]] is generally busted and combos very well with [[Polar Explorers]] or [[Ruler of Thul]].

[[Sir Agravaine]] plus [[Plague of Frogs]] is a devastating all time classic, especially with our [[Interrogator]] ability. Note: They need to have 3 life to prevent you from drawing. So put them to death's door and draw some more cards for your efforts!

Speaking of [[Plague of Frogs]], it's very juicy with [[Kiss of Judas]]. Thoughts: It's too "win-more" but the fantasy is great. I've chosen to replace it with more removal.

[[Coy Nixie]] combos very well with [[Thin Ice]], which is further enhanced by our [[River Rapids]] package.

Speaking of [[River Rapids]], the main idea is to push your minions with Charge one step forward off the River so they can directly attack their avatar. Pushing into [[Thin Ice]] feels great, too.


Considerations:

* I reaaally want to play [[Mimic]], but it's a dead card if they don't have an artifact. I feel like in the long run, people will not just play out artifacts unless they immediately gain value from them. Considered a [[Silver Bullet]] package but that makes the collection much weaker I think.

* Currently testing the exclusion of [[Joyous Garde]] etc. [[Earthquake]] seems very strong due to many new strong sites with Gothic. It also helps against the Omphalos.

Update: Decided to include the tri-sites to be a little greedier with threshold.


Notes on Collection

[[Lure]] can pull up [[Root Spider]]s - keep it for that, because a Spider under their avatar ruins our whole plan.

[[Extinguish]] - Keep it for [[Jihad]] and [[Great Famine]]

[[Minor Explosion]] - Our main finisher. Also great if they play [[Lilith]] or [[Morgana]].

[[Hamlet's Ablaze]] - Main targets are [[Gnome Hollows]] and [[Thin Ice]]

Check out my video deck tech for Ironclad here! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5GIB4AyE2kw



Using Ironclads ability to reduce the cost on self-damaging spells Searing Truth and Pnakotic Manuscript for very efficient card draw. Sugarplum Pixies untaps us at the end of turn and we can use our Avatar to block attacks and reduce damage taken (My Body As A Shield) The Inquisitions free summon trigger applies when revealing through our card draw spells and that is a really powerful tempo swing!

We have a lock on strike damage with Golden Harp allowing us to order the modifiers in a way that we take no damage from strikes. The Poisonous Dagger lets us kill anything when we block.

deckinfo.name: What doesnt kill you makes you stronger!
deckinfo.primer:
So its time for the Primer.


So i thought how can i get the most value out of this guy. I just didnt want to build him as a Voltron Avatar so tried something different. After along time of testing i figured, ironclads game really starts on deaths door in the late game.


So in the end what doesnt kill you makes you stronger.


You want to slow the game as good as it gets meaning taking controll with your wicked witch, your harp, the saint, poison nova. Heal back up, with divine healing, the vampires and sir galahad. Make yourself harder to kill with the pain in the ass maidens, you want them as fast and as much as possible on your hand, thats why i also run call to war. Searing truth is in my oppinion one of the most broken spell in ironclad going plus 1 for usually 0-2 damage is completly nuts.


Blade of thorns, poison dagger and the plate are also very important cause it gives you way more pressure in the late game and more removel.


I run the goat aswell, dont underrestimate this guy. He can be a gamechanger for you but you need to use him wisely. Specially when your maidens are nearby him.


You rely on chip damage on the early-mid game and smack your opponents in the late game with your big beaters.




So i reworked the list alot cause the midgame wasnt good enough. And gave it more consistency.


Also ist added betrayal i will try them. Other spots are, blaze of glory and warp spasm or whirling blades. Well now in he end i run them both. Im not 100% satisfied with Betrayal yet but i will keep it so far. I will try instead 2 iron shackles, 3 mana to disable a minion and themed based, ye lets give it a try. So far i run with 2 lava flow as finisher and removel, cause betrayal was not good enough as impact.

So i will consider to play wiccan tools, my treshhold is pretty high and it fixes the early/midgame card draw and more consistency as they count also as spellcaster for the devils pact. Im not sure yet what i will cut for them. I really consider to cut the blade of thorns and the plate of whale.


I recommend also instead of the amethyst core, the onyx core. I dont own it so i cant includ it. Also when you got cards like ring of morrigan or morgana play them instead of sir percival and 1 of the cores. Unfortunatly i dont own them yet.


Finally i got my Glastonbury Tor and can replace it with colour out of space.


And another epic hit for me, pulled a key to the city in foil. I replace it with a grapple shot.


And also i finally got my prescious ring ^^


I hope you like the list, i will maybe adjust small things here and there but in general this will be the final version of it.





Reminder:


I only includ cards that i own.

deckinfo.name: Ironclad Fury Road
deckinfo.primer:
UPDATE MAY 31, '26: Leaning more into the Fury Road aspects while keeping the protection for Ironclad. Now the game plan is to sit back with Ironclad and build up protection around it. Ironclad ideally needs a Gnome Hollows under it, and then a Harp in hand. If that happens, you are in a great spot. Beat down quickly, and then you can end the game in many ways with Toolbox, Powerwish, or the various bomb minions you have in play.


UPDATE FEB 25: Post Sorcery Con, the deck did not perform well, but I learned a lot and realized something interesting about Ironclad. Ironclad is best as a blocker, not an attacker. I played a lot of different decks, and I think the new motivation is to have charge minions who can get in for quick damage. Get the opponent to Death's Door and then make it near impossible to deal a death blow to their avatar. Late game, getting Ironclad to hold a Golden Harp on Gnom Hollows seals the game as you poke away at their life.


UPDATE JAN 14. I do not think that Wolves are viable. They are simply too slow. Splashing air allows a lot more card draw with pieces like "blink." Movement, striking, and card draw are what make Ironclad work well. Saving Harp for the late game is smart, as that reduces Ironclad's damage output as well. Having more movement in the deck makes this feel easier to play. However, I think I may need more ways to buff up Ironclad.


UPDATE DEC 16. In a Voltron mirror, this deck needs more card draw. I think having ways to cheat out spells is good too. I dropped Tutor for Cerberus, and I am experimenting with the wolves still. On games when I see a lot of wolves, it works okay. But I think I may need to go all in on Wolves because late game, seeing a wolf is a dead draw.


UPDATE DEC 15. I am leaning even more into the Voltron vibe here. Once Ironclad gets to 6 power or so, you have essentially won the game if your opponent cannot take away artifacts. I think having minions is still important to serve as blockers, but I am not worried about getting to DD much with this list.


I am toying with the idea of having a pack of wolves defend Ironclad. I like the idea and flavor of having a pack of Grey Wolves buff each other and defend each other on the board while Ironclad stays safe moving around the board state.


Ironclad Voltron Midrange: You’re trying to stick one or two really annoying creatures and turn them into monsters with weapons while Ironclad shrugs off a ton of chip damage. This isn’t a race deck; it’s a grind deck. Your equipment pile (Sword & Shield, Blade of Thorns, Rhongomyniad, Spear of Destiny, etc.) turns any decent body into a threat, and Ironclad lets that unit survive a lot more than it should. The magic suite gives you enough burn and board control to clear the way and punish opponents who try to swarm you, while your main goal is to stack weapons and armor on your best threat and drag the game to a point where you’re almost impossible to kill.


In my experience, you don’t actually care about sitting at death’s door that much, because if you can get Ironclad and your board to the point where your main beater is swinging for 6, 7, 8+ power, you’re not really worried about a death blow anymore. Lord of Greed helps you claw back the artifacts opponents inevitably steal from you and keeps your engine online in grindy games.


Your best bet is to stick to arming Ironclad. Good minions to clear some board space are usually Profane Revenant, Fallen Angel, Lesser Blood Demon, and sometimes Royal Bodyguard if you need a tank sitting near your avatar. Fallen Angel + equipment is nasty, and Revenant is great because it’s good value with the demon package. The big thing to remember: Ironclad prevents damage, not life loss, so your avatar helps against burn and combat, but not your own stuff like Demonic Contract or other “lose life” effects. Treat Contract / Pact / Powerwish as late-game power plays once you’re stable, not something you jam early.

deckinfo.name: Joven's London Dungeon [Ironclad Control]
deckinfo.primer:
"I don't want to be here in your London Dungeon

I don't want to be here in your British hell

Ain't no mystery why I'm in misery in Hell"


It's Rainy, It's Muddy, It's Miserable, It's....LONDON DUNGEON! This is a brutally slow and methodic control deck, where your only goal is Survival, you can eventually "Win" the game, but your REAL goal is to not lose forever.


Avatar

  • Ironclad - Preventing 2 damage seems fine, but with the right support, it can be game winning.

Aura

  • Summoning Sphere - Part of your finishing combo, lets you win the game............eventually.


Artifacts

  • Scarecrow / Bailey combo - Put one of each of these on your home site and your avatar can no longer be attacked by minions.
  • Makeshift Barricade, Golden Harp - Work well together, and help you prevent TONS of damage.
  • Angel's Egg - Life gain is great for survival.
  • Toolbox - Find what you need, when you need it! Helps win the game, and can help you never deck (See: Return to Nature)!
  • Amulet of Niniane - Protects you from magic.

Minions

  • Land Surveyor - Draws a land, blocks.
  • Apprentice Wizard - Draws a car, , blocks, can be used for a finishing blow Arcane Barrage if necessary.
  • Root Spider - Disables enemies, protects you well.
  • Pudge Butcher - A solid body used like a century tower with its projectile.
  • Daperyll Vampire / Renatus True blood - Beefy flyers, gain life, block.
  • Lord of Greed - Snatch away annoying artifacts, can protect you from maddening bells, blocks.
  • Draco Corvus - A mobile removal unit, blocks.
  • Rhitta Gawr - Slows the game WAY down, blocks.
  • Grandmaster Wizard - Draws 3 cards, blocks, helps you with your game-ending combo...
  • Nimbus Jinn - Your primary win condition - Teleport him to your enemies site with a summoning sphere (or a tool boxed teleport) and FINISH THEM by dumping your hand, blocks. (He's kind of your Psychatog, IYKYK)

Spells

  • Arcane Barrage - Clear a line of small minions, or use it as a finishing blow with either Ironclad or a well placed Apprentice mage.
  • Browse - EXCELLENT card draw.
  • Tithe - Draw three!
  • Common Sense - Find what you need!
  • Lightning Bolt - SOLID removal, can finish off a doored opponent...eventually.
  • Disenchant - Get of pesky auras and artifacts.
  • Chaos twister - Solid removal, sometimes a multiple-for 1, can finish off a doored opponent...eventually.
  • Earthquake - Clear the way!

Sites

  • Most of these are just to get your threshold but a few have other purposes:
  • Great Wall - Make your opponent's life HARD, basically Bailey #4.
  • Bottomless pits - Another defensive site
  • Briar patch - Great against necromancer
  • Pillar of Zeiros - Lifegain!


Collections **IMPORTANT!**

  • Zap - How to win the game when an opponent is at death's door. (3 because Legion of Gall exists, and if they want to use it on ZAP!, they have to FULLY commit.)
  • Common Sense - Toolbox for sense is just good!
  • Dispel - Remove artifacts, auras, etc.
  • Teleport - For when you don't draw your summoning spheres!
  • Murder of Crows - Slow down Necromancer.
  • Makeshift Barricade - #4
  • Return to Nature - *THIS IS IMPORTANT* You can win the game by decking your opponent out with these! Toolbox for the first one, and use it to shuffle your toolbox back into your deck, then do the same with the next toolbox you draw, but also shuffle the first Return to Nature into your deck, and there you go! You can't deck out anymore!


Enjoy!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Your opponent won't.

deckinfo.name: If you wanna finish me, you're gonna work for it
deckinfo.primer:
As of 1/3/26 I am at 16 wins and 16 losses with this deck.

I personally am not a fan of getting killed by magic and this is my deck to prevent that. So far it has succeeded pretty well with at least making the opponent have to think outside the box to finish me.


Amulet, harp and barricade, white hart, bodyguard and shield maidens are all there for the obvious prevention/reduction of damage. Barricade and harp are the most essential I feel like. Harp reduces all incoming strikes or life loss 2 which then is reduced to 0 because of Ironclad. That means that they then need to get rid of the harp or kill you with a lightning bolt or higher to finish you off when at deaths door. Barricade prevents all damage up to 5 because of Ironclad. That means that they need to deal 5+ damage in a go or remove the barricade to finish you which isn't super difficult to manage but if you have other reductions or prevention's in effect, which is fairly likely, they're gonna have a difficult time removing the barricade via damage.


Next up for the protection of your avatar are the sites. Gnome hollows puts in some serious work in this regard, keeping out any 3+ power minions. This means that even if you don't have any other damage prevention/reduction means, you still have that to fall back on. Next up we have free city with its ability to protect you in the event your units get taken out. I think bottomless pit is the strongest after free city since they specifically need airborne to come in and finish you off. Impenetrable copse would is in here to prevent any ranged shenanigans and I think is the weakest form of protection out of these 4 sites. Personally if I didn't have a hollows, pit or a free city in the opening hand i would mulligan all 3 sites for a chance at pulling one of em.


As far as magics and minions are concerned, I think these come down to preference. As of 12/26, everything in the list has been useful when i've had it so i feel comfortable with whats there as well as the amounts. I
