deckinfo.name: Trench Warfare
deckinfo.primer:
Feel free to comment or ask if you want any clarifications.


Spells

[[Golden Harp]]

Most (if not all) water decks deal only strike damage. So if you can manage to get this on an ordinary site nearby and keep it there, they will be unable to kill you at all. Just try to play it AFTER they use a spell that burrows artifacts if you're playing against earth.

[[Blasted Oak]]

MVP in any game you can draw it, but you'll only have a 33% chance of getting it on a good day. This artifact messes up any spell that targets an artifact, site, or minion. Just make sure to keep a minion on the site if you can for [[swap]], so the opponent is forced to target the blasted oak and your minion. No one I've played against has figured out that you can swap my makeshift barricade and my blasted oak yet, but you don't want to bet on your opponent being ignorant in a tournament setting.

[[Makeshift Barricade]]

The damage replacement for this card happens AFTER the damage reduction for [[Ironclad]], which means that anyone dealing you damage directly needs to do at least 5 damage to break the barricade. [[Lord of Lies]], [[Gnarled Wendigo]], and [[Dormant Monstrosity]] are usually the only cards that are run in water that can break through this, so this will keep you safe in most cases if you already dealt with those threats. Again, wait to play this until after Atlantean Fate is played if you can help it. Try to place an ordinary site as your home site to help with this.

[[Root Spider]]

This has way more opportunities to die than against other matchups, but there is one very important use-case. If you have an ordinary site as your home site, you will be untouchable if you play a root spider beneath you. As long as there are no voids next to you. [[Lacuna Entity]] is the real killer for root spider, in addition to fate.


Sites

[[Common Village]] / [[Humble Village]]

This should almost always be your home site. Because it's ordinary, it's not vulnerable to [[atlantean fate]]. And atlantean fate WILL be played in 100% of the games you play somehow.

[[Gnome Hollows]]

This is a great potential home site if your biggest concern in [[Ruler of Thul]] or [[Aino]]. Prevents him from coming into your back row in most cases. Unfortunately, it's susceptible to [[atlantean fate]]. It's best to not rely on this for protection on death's door, unless they've already used their atlantean fate or you've dispelled it.


Site Placement

You generally want to make a " T " formation to start. By turn 3/4/5, you should know if you have enough ramp to start encroaching on their side of the board or not. If you can confidently take at least 2 of their sites away, that will be enough to be worth it. If you keep their sites limited to 8, then they can't cast [[Lord of Lies]] + [[Swap]], or [[Ruler of Thul]] + [[Atlantean Fate]] on the same turn anymore. Then you can hopefully deal with the threats one at a time.


If you don't have the ramp to start encroaching in their space, you probably want to retreat into the " M " formation. Keeping only 1 entry point to your site is very helpful in controlling the flow of movement and can ward off a lot of threats. That being said, fill in the voids if your opponent is playing minions with voidwalk or hasn't played their [[Lacuna Entity]]s.


If you face water, you want the hollows as your home site, with an ordinary site somewhere nearby. This is to prevent a surprise [[Ruler of Thul]] attack. This does leave you vulnerable to [[Atlantean Fate]], but you can just move to a nearby ordinary site or something. For every other matchup, you can make your home site whatever you want. Gnome hollows is usually best played on the front lines, though.


Opening Hand

For your opening hand, it's generally a good idea to have some kind of ramp spell and some kind of turn 3+ play. You'll also want to keep any card draw you get. For ramp, you ideally want [[Landmass]], but [[Kettletop Leprechaun]] is a good consolation card. [[Common Sense]] is good as a third best option to search for a landmass or to keep for the later game when you need a [[Makeshift Barricade]] or [[Border Militia]]. You'll generally want to mulligan any card that costs more than 5 just so it's not sitting in your hand for 6 turns if you don't get the best ramp. For card draw, [[Morgana le Fay]] and [[Searing Truth]] are great keeps. [[Queen of Midland]] is a card you will not want to keep. You want to draw into that.


No matter what you mulligan, though, you shouldn't feel bad. As soon as you use a [[common sense]], you will shuffle your deck, so it won't be on the bottom anymore.


For sites, you want to try to hit an ordinary site and/or a [[Gnome Hollows]] in your opening hand. Any of the Villages will also go a long way for preventing yourself from getting fate'd. Mulligan or keep the rest depending on your threshold requirements.


Other good cards in your opening hand you can keep:

[[Blasted Oak]], [[Root spider]], [[Torrid Omphalos]], [[Toolbox]], [[Golden Harp]], [[Morgana le Fay]], [[Gargantula]], [[Archangel Michael]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], [[Gigantism]], [[Earthquake]], [[Death Dealer]] (maybe), and [[Poison Nova]].


﻿Cards you do NOT want to keep in your opening hand:

[[Arjaro Exorcist]] (situational, good against water, air, and [[Enchantress]]), [[Border Militia]], [[Onslaught]] (Unless you have minions you know will stick around), [[Boudicca]], [[King of the Realm]], and [[Balor of the Evil Eye]].


Tells

Usually players will set up their plays before they happen. If your opponent has 1 or more minions on their back row and are not moving up, expect a [[Ruler of Thul]] next turn.


[[Atlantean Fate]] is hard to predict, but if you see something like a [[Ruler of Thul]] come down and not attack, then they are most likely waiting until next turn to play their fate and disable your home site [[Gnome Hollows]]. Also, if they attack onto your sites with important minions that have submerge, that might be a tell.


If there is a minion with 4+ power on the board, it's pretty safe to just always assume that the player has [[Whirling Blades]] in hand. So make sure you play accordingly.


MATCHUPS

🌊WATER🌊

Main Threats - [[Atlantean Fate]] | [[Ruler of Thul]] | [[Swap]] | [[Lord of Lies]] | [[Coy Nixie]] | [[Lacuna Entity]] | [[Scatter]]

Secondary Threats - [[Whirling Blades]] | [[Grapple Shot]] | [[Call of the Sea]] | [[Acid Rain]] | [[Aino]]


🪨EARTH🪨

Main - [[Landmass]] | [[Archangel Raphael]] | [[Gargantula]] | [[Root Spider]] | [[Earthquake]] | [[Dispel]]

Secondary - [[Cave-In]] / [[Bury]] | [[Paladins of Bazia]] | [[Border Militia]] / [[Guards!]] | [[Garden of Eden]]


🌪️AIR🌪️

Main - [[Whirling Blades]] | [[Sphere of Animosity]] | [[Daperyll Vampire]] | [[Disenchant]]

Secondary - [[Sturmgeist]] | [[Grapple Shot]] | [[Feast for Crows]]


🔥FIRE🔥

Main - [[Courtesan Thais]] | [[Scorched Earth]] (with [[Roots of Yggdrasil]]) | [[Balor of the Evil Eye]]

Secondary - [[Morgana le Fay]] | [[Poison Nova]] | [[Shatter Strike]]

deckinfo.name: The Lich King
deckinfo.primer:
Max Skeleton start:


Turn 1 play Boulevard of Bones. Summon 1 skeleton.


Turn 2 play Open Grave/Mausoleum forward. Summon 3 skeletons.


Turn 3 play Mirror Realm right of Boulevard copying it and cast Novice Necromancer. Summon 3 skeletons.

You can Panpipes turn 3 for 6 damage and try to force opponet to Dispel/Disenchant to protect your +1 buffs turn 4+.


Turn 4 if no +1 buff play Forsaken Crypt right of Mirror Realm. Summon 2 skeletons.


Turn 5 play Den of Evil forward of Mirror Realm and cast Returned King. Summon 2 skeletons.

Or play non-Open Grave/Masoleum/Forsaken Crypt forward of Mirror Realm, cast Landmass, and play Open Grave/Mausoleum. Summon 3 skeletons.


Turn 6 don't play site left of Boulevard and cast Master Necromancer. Summon 5 skeletons.

Or play Open Grave/Masoleum left of Boulevard and cast 2x Novice Necromancer. Summon 5 skeletons.


End of turn 6: 17x skeletons

--------

Use Bone Spear for game win. Spore Spouts/Tactical Move/Landmass will help position a skeleton for the projectile.


Pile of Skulls can banish from the enemy cemetery, do this to save your cemetery for Book of the Dead.

Dark Depths is a Midrange water deck. I’ve opted Mono water vs air splash. Mono water allows me to run island Leviathan, sinkholes, and bureau. In addition, double omphalos has more outs.


Dark Depths leverages a monsters sub-theme. Usually abyssal assault would be a lackluster spell, but this deck leverages it to full effect. deckinfo.name: And I thought aggro was easy wins..... NECROMONSTER
deckinfo.primer:
Make skellies, play water, win.

Control board, disable things and move them around.


Built this deck without much thought right out the gate with Gothic and at first it felt just broken strong. Now that we are a little over a month into Gothic I think Water has come out as the strongest element in constructed (though maybe best when paired with something else), and I'm sure this shell could be tweaked and used for different avatars. It's nice in necro since necro is kinda like an arhci-druid, where you get tons of value in skellies on the board but they are more game stallers than damage pushers/spellcasters like tawny was. This means the longer the game goes and the more you can use the skellies that lets the overall power of the water cards grind out a win. Also, the site value in water has reached a critical point where water sites are just broken strong compared to the sites in every other element. There are a lot of incredible sties that could be swapped into this deck, but I decided to lean away from scrying and focus on movement and transformation. Sinister Pond with Adept Illusionist can kinda feel like a waste but also just some wild ramping. I will probably cut sinister pond for other sites soon (like maybe The Void or Mismanaged Mortuary).


With Necromonster you are playing a deck that is kind of like a Minion based Archimago - so the longer the game goes the more likely you are to win (except against other similar late game control decks).


How to Play It:

You want to mulligan big bomb minions from your starting hand to get your early game control pieces. Ideally get a site combo that can move skeletons to the front line (like a river rapids on the starting spot is ideal) and/or a prime defensive site with Nixie. This deck requires an annoying amount of thought to get maximum value out of it, since you are looking at lots of motion abilities and you usually have too many options for great plays. The floor though is just make skeleton when you can and play control pieces. Usually the easiest way to guarantee a door is going for a polar explorers or ruler of thuul around the world strike with something big or a just a bunch of stuff. The best cards to see in your opening hand are Coy Nixie, Gnarled Wendigo and Shapeshift. Turn 3 Wendigo can sometimes win the game on its own.


It's hard to describe all the different play lines - but it is surprisingly easy to see them once you start playing this deck. You will feel too powerful most of the time. Only times it struggles so far have been against other similar decks (Water is strong right now and there are lots of ways to build the control/ramp water lists including this, and things like Seer/Spellslinger or even Interrogator/Sorcerer). Definitely the Mist shell plays very similar lines with better tools (but less reliability), so that is one to watch out for.


Random other Tips on Playing this Deck:

I am slowly coming around to leaning on skeletons more. Prioritizing playing a skeleton every turn has become a lot like trying to draw a spell for turn every turn. The only time I won't is when I need to not do it to answer a threat. Like if they have a big threat that I can't answer and play a skellie, then I will just answer it, but for building board state I lean toward getting a skeleton every turn if I can.


Lessons Learned from Playtesting

I have lost games because I made the mistake of attacking with the Skeletons on many occasions. Even though they can't move to defend they are defensive pieces in this deck (and utility) so it's best to just get them to the various frontiers so they can chump block and keep you in the drivers seat.


Updates over Time:

Jan 10 took out the Silver Bullets finally (had been trying to see if I could make them work, but at the end of the day toolbox seems like the way to go).

Jan 12 switched in Mismanaged Mortuary for Sinister Ponds so as to eat my vegetables and ideally mess up any cemetery stuff my opponent might try :D

Jan 19 went down to 2 Horrible Hybrids in collection to add a Return to Nature so as to eat my vegetables (aka cemetery hate for stopping archi and deathspeaker). also went to 2 mariners curses so i could run both oompaloompas

Jan 20 decided to pull 2 winternymphs for sacred stag

Early Feb finally added Aino (wasn't convinced on her until I realized her power against imposter). Made some other changes that I forgot to record (like I think I added in the archange)



Things I am Considering (as of Jan 19, 2026):

  • Should I be doing the 4 kill spell collection? Basically, with Legion of Gall wreaking havoc on collections and Mist being (in my opinion) the strongest shell, I think in water it really makes sense to have 4 kill spells in your collection. Maybe it should even just be 4 ice lances. But also, I am not getting max value out of Gilman House and Toolbox by running 4 spells for the same job.
  • How can I fit Failed Mutation and Sacred Stag? List as of the writing of this doesn't include either - but they are soooooooo strong and auto-includes. They don't make the list because I prioritize 3 and 2 drops to be able to survive aggro decks, and then for my higher end creatures I just run the super overpowered uniques and elites. I'm already wishing I could run more Magics as well, but the creature count should really be 38ish (not the current 35). Mariners Curse is high on the list of potential cuts, but getting to re-use it multiple times makes it such good removal and has lots of other uses around shutting down other water decks.


Suggested Variants:

If you are looking for ways to modify this deck here are my main suggestions:

  • Mist Suite: basically pull things that don't gain value the turn you play them and trade out some snowballs and a riptide for grappleshots and whirling blades (maybe drop the into the abyss or a swap or riptide as well). Then you add in the small handful of really good air minions (basically just Sturmgeist and Daperyl Vampires, maybe consider Hounds and Grandmaster Wizard)
  • Go Harder on the Big Boys fast approach. One of the popular cards to run in Water Necro is Dormant Monstrosity. I personally prefer minions that control the board for this deck because it is more about control. Sneaking out a Monstrosity in the corner is nice for big bodies early, but piling a bunch of big bodies on the board early just makes sweeping your board with good board clearing spells too easy (think Poison nova, atlantean fate, etc). That said, leaning in on big boi's fast can be really strong (also popular with Seer and Spellslinger builds that are similar). You can pull some of the control and early game stuff to add Dormant Monstrosity and more of the high end water minions to make your Shapeshifts hit harder (things like Hydra, Mester Worm and Diluvian are options). Even the other Kraken can work for that approach, and you drop the Mariner's curses and a couple of the 3 drops like Lugbog and Order.

deckinfo.name: Every Villain Is Lemons
deckinfo.primer:
MYAH! Hello! It is I! Alino!


Mephistopheles is my favorite card, and Air is my favorite element, so this deck was created because of my desire to make a Mono-Air deck that uses Mephistopheles effectively.


With that said, let me go over the list!


The Avatar

Version One of this deck was initially designed this deck without an Avatar in mind. I planned to use whichever Avatar fit the deck best, and was going to use a generically good one like Sorcerer or Savior if none came to mind. But fortunately one did.


Necromancer ended up being the perfect fit for this deck. His ability to generate 1/1 Skeletons is great for smoothing out our curve. It's a bonus that the tokens are Undead/Evil, since the deck has many payoffs for both taglines.


The Spellbook

Auras

1x Eclipse - Serves as an anthem for most of our minions AND acts as a Summoning Sphere.

2x Sphere of Animosity - Shuts down healing entirely for the Avatar inside. Also great for shutting down Avatars like Realm Eater and Battlemage.

1x The Black Plague - This is good removal & area denial. Synergizes well with Necromancer, since we can send tokens in to die for the cause to keep the plague going if need be.


Artifacts

1x Amethyst Core - I just think it's neat. And we have a lot of top end, which this helps get out.

2x Mix Aer - I like this a lot. It can be really nice to open with this since it gives us the mana to do something like a turn 2 Daperyll Vampire.

2x Torshammar Trinket - A repeatable method of buffing our goobers is nice. It's doubly nice in a Necromancer deck, since we pop out Skeletons like a pez dispenser.

1x Pnakotic Manuscript - Repeatable card draw that is super cheap. We make a lot of expendable bodies for this.

2x Toolbox - Just an amazing staple. Lets us grab a variety of answers from the Collection.

1x Char Omphalos - Fantastic card advantage engine.

1x Dank Omphalos - Fantastic card advantage engine.


Minions

4x Pith Imp - Low-cost Evil disruption. Can ruin an opponent's entire game if it hits something juicy.

2x Earl of the Ivory Towers - Solid low-cost Spellcaster who happens to be Evil.

3x Gibbous Nightgaunts - A 3 Power Demon with Airborne and Voidwalk is just a nice statblock for this list.

1x Jack the Ripper - Extremely good removal.

4x Screamer - Really useful ability. Good for aggro and defense.

2x Sturmgeist - Amazing. Able to deal tons of damage if left unanswered.

3x Stygian Archers - Amazing. Great Ranged minion with a strong ability.

1x Bane of Aventis - Fantastic answer to Ward.

1x Archangel Gabriel - Strong minion that replaces itself.

3x Daperyll Vampire - Staple. Able to heal you for tons, and is a great body.

2x Legion of Gall - Absolutely shreds your opponent's Collection.

2x Renatus Trueblood - Two extra copies of Daperyll Vampire is nice.

2x Grandmaster Wizard - Refills your hand. Never unhappy to see it.

1x Mephistopheles - I just think he's neat.

1x Nosferatu - Absolutely annoying for an opponent to permanently get rid of.

1x Draconian Bonekite - Massive Airborne goober. Ability is great for closing out games.

1x The Doom of Dilmun - This card is phenomenal. The fact we can get it out for free with Mephistopheles is nuts, but this card is fantastic even if we're hard-casting it. Near impossible for an opponent to remove.


Magic

1x Browse - This is just a staple in every mono-air deck. It's such a good way of finding whatever it is we need at any given time.

2x Blink - Solid movement card that replaces itself.

3x Desecrate - Letting something like your Daperyll Vampire or Legion of Gall get a second strike in can be game-winning. Also great for answering any super pesky sites.

3x Kiss of Death - Over half our goofballs can cast. We even make tokens that can cast this. And this happens to be fantastic removal.

1x Black Mass - Great way of refilling the hand.

2x Whirling Blades - This card is devastating. Functions like a one-sided board wipe a lot of the time.


The Atlas

Sites

1x Cloud City - Amazing ability.

1x Dark Tower - Temporary ramp is good.

1x Defiler Spire - Nice card to play when we're on the offensive since it can drain health fast.

4x Den of Evil - This is like 4 extra copies of the Towers in our deck.

3x Fields of Phyxis - This + Desecrate gives us plenty of ways of dealing with annoying sites. Also, being blunt, I got the Dust Promo for this and wanted to use it.

2x Forsaken Crypt - I like being able to generate a body without spending a card to do so. I only run 2 of these so that I can have more flexibility in the Collection.

1x Gothic Tower - Temporary ramp is good.

1x Lone Tower - Temporary ramp is good.

1x Merlin's Tower - Temporary super-ramp is great.

2x Observatory - Topdeck manipulation is good.

4x Open Mausoleum - Extra bodies without spending cards to make them is great. Playing this turn 2 is nice with Necromancer since we can turn 1 make a token into turn 2 two more tokens.

2x Sold-out Cemetery - We have a lot of Undead, as well as the ability to pump out Undead tokens. This is nice free-movement with them.

1x The Manor at Daperyll Hill - Very nice defensive card.

2x Watchtower - Completely shutting down Stealth is great.

2x Wizard's Den - I don't care about the downside. Card draw is card draw.

2x Wuthering Heights - Great card. Using this to move an enemy onto Bottomless Pit is hilarious.


The Collection

Cards

3x Desecrated Ground - Needed for Desecrate.

1x Zap! - 3 mana to kill an Avatar on Death's Door is amazing.

1x Disenchant - 4 mana to blow up, ideally, 2+ things is amazing.

1x Tactical Move - The ability to reposition our entire board for 4 mana can come in handy in a pinch.

2x Ghoul - Needed for Forsaken Crypt.

1x Grapple Shot - Nice bit of positioning and removal when needed. Also just a great card.

1x Murder of Crows - Mass Ward removal or token removal is great.


Additional Comments

  • Play Style wise, this deck goes for the long game. We aim to outvalue the opponent over the course of the game. Cards like Mephistopheles, Char Omphalos, and Dank Omphalos are great when out because they generate so much value.

deckinfo.name: Queens of Moloch
deckinfo.primer:
👸 Queens united ! 👸 (work in progress)


Aino, Morgana, The Lady of the lake, Boudicca, Courtesan Thais, Lilith, Maiden, Mother and Crone join forces in the name of Moloch, god of Sacrifice !

An unlikely alliance to bring water and fire power together 🔥🌊.


Welcome to this Necro steam deck


Type of gameplay : Midrange power with a lot of synergies and abilities to turn tables around in your favor when needed


💀 Skellies uses in this deck 💀 :

-Equip a trinket on one of them for 2 power minions removal or dmg or just send them with another minion to add that +1 power that is sometimes needed ⚔️

-use them with Pnakoptic Manuscript to draw cards (they will die but heh that's what they're here for)

-Great at tapping to activate a silver bullet so you dont waste a meaningfull minion's turn by tapping it to activate the bullet

-infinite bodies to bring back Rasputin as they are evil (so if Rasputin is in your graveyard, summon a skellies and banish it to have a 3/3 rasputin-skelly back)

-Works very well with sir agravaine as any attack from a skelly if Agravaine is adjacent is now followed by a 3 power attack from the Sir (so your skellies can remove 4 power minions)

-obviously great with boudicca as every body counts with her

-Same goes for ruler of thul, send your skellies from bottom of the Realm to cross for 2 power strikes/skelly

-Can be target for blaze if you need to remove something in the way or wards and you don't have anything better

-Great targets for swap as sometimes you don't wanna send your big guy far , you want him close to strike that lilith you're swapping from your opponent to bring it to your side with your skelly. Or swappin a skelly on thin ice with their 5 power minion to kill it

-Sacrifice them on elder ruins to summon a shoggoth from your collection (2)

-Sacrifice them on the temple of Moloch to be blessed by the god of Sacrifice with a +2 mana in your turn which is cool stuff




Single cards discussion :


Aura :

-Atlantean fate : hmm super card, not gonna waste time justifyng that :D


Artifacts :

-Torshammar trinket : great to remove stuff without loosing yours and with skellies you always have a target for this

-Pnakoptic manuscrit : draw engine with skellies and frogs , also don't hesitate to use it with rasputin and bring him back after with a skelly

-Silver Bullet : acces to collection (see collection part of the primer)


Minions :

-Grigori Rasputin : absolutly amazing unique, cast him, use him, let him die, and bring him back with your vile imp to deal another 2 dmg, with a succubus to double its power in a turn for 4 dmg / 4 life, lacuna entity for another free removal, Balor for a second heat ray in a turn etc. And ofc with skellies, you always have a target to bring him back

-Pied piper of Hamelin : against other necro, also prevent Wizards from beeing played by your opponent as you control 1 power and less minions. and still a 2/2 for 2

-Aino : regulard damage that is hard to get rid off, can act as a finisher too as stealthed minion cant be defened against

-Lugbog cat : great curve advantage card, turn 2 with a pond (4 in the deck), or summon it in opponent side if he plays water sites

-Mazuj ifrit : great curve advantage card, the airborne on a 4 power minion is nothing to laugh at, it's a very mobile and hard to remove threat

-Morgana Le Fay : Sorcery power nine . That gurl is on fire 🔥🔥🔥

-Sir agravaine : amazing striking power, if you have several tokens (frogs, skellies) close to enemy's avatar, its power will activate each time for a 3 power strike for each ally's strike. And with him close to even a skelly, it will help remove almost any minion

-Lady of the lake : nice 3/3 spellcaster submerge for 3, but she can bring back a saracen raider, agravaine, Ruler of Thul, Morgana, Boudicca or Courtesan from the graveyard if needed and also an artifact like a silver bullet ;).

-Colicky dragonette : Works really well with skellies, gift of the serpent , good 3/3 minions that can act as a trinket to add a ping somewhere ! and remove ward, can be a finisher

-Abaddon Sucubbus : Great 4 cost minion, her ability pairs well with skellies to deal 3 dmg + its board control , try her if you haven't you' ll love her !

-Boudicca : Obvious choice in a deck with a lot of tokens, but works well with Saracen raiders also

-Failed mutation : (currently trying without them)so, 4/4 for 4 ain't super sexy, but don't underestimate its protection ability. beeing immune to bury, poison nova, infiltrate, bolts, explosions etc make it really tough to remove and a key piece when you're facing archimago (earthquake will remove it :P). If you have this match-up , keep one in your opening hand.

-Ruler of Thul : great way to bypass fortress sites and deal a surprise strike, send him with a few skellies or one of your many 4+ power minion for a nice 8/10+ dmg

-Sacred stag: Great value, especially if you are lucky enough to get a pond to cast it for 3. The ward forces your enemy to spend more ressources to deal with that 4 power minion. Also , few chances that it happens but if you ward one of your site when it dies , it can be a great site to cast your pnakoptic manuscript or silver bullet in the hand of one of your minions as ward prevent Dispel/disenchant on the site ;)

-Saracen raiders : charge minion that may surprise the ennemy as this is not a charge deck, but it's just too strong not to get them, the ability to cast them in enemy side is amazing (helps remove a lilith, a maiden morther and crone and other back row annoying stuff)

- Courtesan Thais : just here to turn table around, can be use as a finisher, a great disruptor, can be brought back with lady of the lake, a very fun card with lot of possibilities but can be a bit tricky to play, so feel free to replace it with like an inquisition etc

-Lacuna entity : awesome removal that ignore regions on a 4 power body . Nice to get that annoying coy nixie under thin ice in the void hihihii

-Lilith : She is queen of Evilness you may wanna stack a skelly with her to protect her a bit against lightning bolt

-Maiden, Mother and Crone : (currently trying without her as she still 8 mana to draw the 1st card)Great value card and draw engine, just value nothing else to say, protect it !

-Panorama manticore, cost4 with pond, airborne on a 5/5 is super strong, lethal can be useful versus lord of lies or against multiple defenders, untap is a nice bonus

-Questing beast : (currently trying without it) So this is a bit of a swappable spot here, it's obviously a great minion, but it's just a fat fightning body that is nice to cast for 4 with a pond. It doesn't have a wow effect the moment it arrives on board tough, but the stealth and free movement with that 5 power is just a "can't be wrong" card

-Balor of the Evil eye : amazing minion, his heat ray affect subsurface, so great to remove nixies and spiders , work as an amazing finisher, is a 6/6 yep good stuff , also, you can Rasputin him to shoot 2 heat rays, pew pew

-Infernal legion : (currently trying without them) Great threat that the enemy will need to remove fast, its effect plays the turn it arrives, like Balor, which means you'll probably always get some value from this card, which we like when we spend 6 mana. it can hit several things, be used as a finisher, a great staple

-Lord of lies : this thing should be unique. Strongest of the 4 lords, can be use as a removal as it can make an enemy fight him or can deal an insane amount of damage if not taked care of

-Sir Mordred : 2 removals for 6 on a 4/4 stick, not bad. Bring him back with LAdy for more one shot effects :)

deckinfo.name: TOO BIG TO FAIL (aka too big, too frail)
deckinfo.primer:
From the Diaries of the Apprentice Wizard


Volume II: Follies and Foibles - Entry #37: How One Minor Miscalculation Led to a Major Monster Mash - A Primer on “Too Big to Fail (aka Too Big, Too Frail)”



Dear diary,

It happened again.


I was only trying to study basic auras (you know, the glowing kind that don’t explode), and somehow I ended up summoning a 10-power horror from beyond the veil by turn 4. Not that I’m complaining - it crushed my opponent... and that old Inn down the road.


Anyway! While the Grandmaster insists I “relearn the basics of restraint,” I say: if the spells are there, why not cast big?


Which brings me to the deck I’ve been accidentally PERFECTING:


Too Big to Fail

(aka Too Big, Too Frail)


If you love:

  • Huge, stompy minions
  • Clever card filtering
  • Baiting your opponent into doing something foolish...


Then congratulations, this is your kind of chaos.


The Master Plan (Well... Apprentice Plan)

You take a massive minion - the type of creature that usually costs a fortune in mana and morals ...and you toss it into the cemetery.


Yes. On purpose.


Then, you bring it back to life early with cards like Raise Dead or Boneyard.

Your opponent won't know what hit them. (Spoiler: it's a giant sea monster. With tentacles)


The only trick is surviving the early game, filtering through your deck to the right cards, and looking completely harmless until suddenly... WHAM! The Doom of Dilmun has arrived and he brought an extra serving of DOOM!


Key Spells and Shenanigans

* Wizard's Den - My favorite Atlas card in the deck. Set it early. Opponent think's your clueless? Let them attack it. BOOM. Discard your biggie and set up for next turn's reanimation.

* Sisters of Avalon - Card filtering AND an excuse to act mysterious and tragic? Win-win. Being able to drop your biggies into the cemetery is key!

* Browse, Rivers, Observatory - You've got to dig through your deck to find your combo pieces, and these all help!

* Raise Dead & Boneyard - Your MVPs. The cemetery isn't the end, it's the launchpad!

* Chaoswish & Kythera Mechanism - Feeling lucky? Chaoswish lets you cast a random spell for free, and with Kythera Mechanism, you decide the outcome. So give yourself something devastating, and if your opponent tries to cast it, use your Kythera Mechanism to give them something deeply underwhelming. (Like a Battering Ram with an apology letter pinned to the side).

* Clairvoyant - Once on your turn, you may banish a dead minion to look at your top spell. Thin out your opponents cemetery and stack the odds in your favor for when you need to Raise Dead and don't have the Kythera Mechanism just yet.

* Sir Tom Thumb & The Black Plague - As long as you control a site afflicted by the Black Plague, Sir Tom Thumb can scamper in again and again to keep the contagion merrily spreading. Some say it’s the mouse he rides that’s carrying the disease; others say it’s because I refused to wash my hands after handling cursed artifacts. The Grandmaster insists it’s “a grotesque misuse of epidemiological magic.” He keeps repeating it with increasing volume, which I assume means I’m doing something right.

* Temple of Moloch + Skeletons/Frogs -

You know that side door in the cellar? I finally looked inside. It’s just.sone strange statues and an indoor sky that’s always red. Terrible reading light.

But whenever I send a delegation of frogs, or the Necromancer’s skeletons, through the door and close it behind them… they disappear, and my spellcasting gets noticeably better.

I’m not asking questions. The mana is lovely, and some theological complications are simply worth it.

* Gnarled Wendigo - The ancient scrolls say to speak not its name. I wrote it in large letters on my notes anyway. The Grandmaster confiscated them immediately, which I think proves my point about overreaction. Use any Skeletons laying around to get “it” cast early. The Grandmaster says patience is a virtue. But when asked “Wendigo?” the answer is always: go now.

* Pnakotic Manuscript - I learned long ago that having someone else do the assigned reading is the true mark of a scholar. Giving a Skeleton the Pnakotic Manuscript is ideal! They read it, they perish, I get the spell. I can see how addicting Doom Scrolling could get.


Lessons in Grave Mismanagement

The hardest part? Getting your minions into the cemetery.

That's why positioning matters, especially with Wizard's Den. You want to plop it down very casually (read: completely obliviously) and act like you have no idea what you are doing.


"Oh no! I put my Wizard’s Den right in front of your minion! I sure hope you don't attack it!"


They fall for it almost every time.

Which is actually kind weird, because honestly...it's really not that subtle.

But hey, if it works, it works.


Survive the Setup

Your non-monster minions are all tutors, discarders, and blockers. Their job is to buy time while you assemble your masterpiece.

Your sites and auras are defensive. Use them to stall, clog the board, or make your opponent think you're flailing (you might be flailing, but in a cool, strategic way).


Final Thoughts (Before I'm Grounded Again)

The Grandmaster keeps saying, "Magic isn't about shortcuts - it's about discipline!"


But what's more disciplined than carefully orchestrating a turn 4 resurrection of a nightmarish Monster?


That's right.


It's not "Too big and too frail." Clearly, the Grandmaster Wizard doesn't fully appreciate my genius here. It's TOO BIG TO FAIL!


Until next time, may your hand be full, your cemetery fuller, and your Den unguarded.

-- The Apprentice Wizard

(still not banned from the library yet!)

deckinfo.name: Steam Necro
deckinfo.primer:
Change Log / Updates:


1/13/2026

  • I've come down on [[Gift of the Serpent]] just a little bit. While it's a great cantrip to include in aggressive fire decks, there seem to be a lot of airborne or ward minions right now and it doesn't help a lot with those unless you have exactly [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] or [[Colicky Dragonettes]] in addition to the Gift. Similarly, I am considering [[Màzuj Ifrit]] as a way above cost aggressive beater that also provides some more airborne.
  • I'm also seriously considering cutting [[Ring of Morrigan]]. I lose the healing with my own [[River of Blood]] and with 3 copies of [[Toolbox]] and [[Searing Truth]] we're not exactly hurting for Death's Door finishers here. It is nice at popping wards, but still that usually requires moving my avatar forward when I don't always want to. There has also been an increase in copies of [[Swap]] and [[Toolbox]] gives every deck ways to answer the Ring. Obviously it's still an objectively powerful card, and the presence of answers for it is not a good reason not to play it, but I feel like it's a slot that could be better used for my strategy.
  • Added back the 3rd copy of [[River of Blood]] after learning that they do stack.


1/9/2026

  • Cut [[Firebreathing]] for [[Sir Mordred]]. I feel like having removal to kill individual big minions matters more right now. Firebreathing was bad against ward minions, bad against a lot of the new larger threats, and bad against random cards like having a [[Sturmgeist]] near your avatar.


1/6/2026

  • Cut 1 [[River of Blood]] for an [[Accursed Desert]]. I figure that River of Blood isn't necessarily something you want to draw in multiples anyway, and ward is quickly proving to be one of the most important things in the game. This could be better as a copy of [[Vast Desert]] with the ability to pick off small bodies or help stack damage to kill a minion, but I want to test Accursed Desert for that potential upside to pop multiple wards.
  • I am also considering cutting [[War Horse]] entirely. The card sometimes feels very weak, but it's also overall very important to the structure / goal of the deck so I am keeping it for now.


1/5/2026

  • Cut [[Doctor Demetrius]]. Overall I think this card is great still, I just think not being able to ward skeletons makes Doctor Demetrius a bit too poor in this list in simplified game states.
  • Cut one [[Gift of the Serpent]]. I felt like I was drawing too many cantrips and felt okay with being at 3 overall including the collection copy.
  • Cut the [[Infernal Legion]]. Obviously this card is great but I decided I wanted the 3rd [[Searing Truth]] and wanted to make the deck more lean overall.
  • Added an old favorite [[Polar Explorers]] to help keep pressure up against decks that play cards like [[Pebbled Paths]] and [[Gnome Hollows]]. This also helps lower the overall mana curve.
  • Trimmed one [[Firebreathing]] for [[Into the Abyss]]. Firebreathing felt poor in many situations as there are a lot of big dudes being played right now many of which have ward. I wanted something to serve as a 3rd hard removal spell alongside [[Infiltrate]].
  • Made several changes to the atlas. [[Altar of Malachai]] is a super powerful card and I can see myself adding it back, but ultimately I wanted to sure up my mana base and felt that card was cuttable due to the overall aggressive tilt of the deck. Added more copies of [[Active Volcano]]. Between [[Floodplain]] and [[Active Volcano]], the idea is to have more opening hands with my threshold requirements met without needing to top deck the right one or draw sites at awkward times. Also cut [[Valley of Delight]] as I feel this card is no longer necessary with the addition of the double threshold sites.
  • A few collection changes: Cut [[Just a Rock]] because it doesn't deal with the Omphalos and really only covers what [[Swap]] already does. Cut [[Instigator Imp]] because it's just not good enough for constructed I think. Added [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]] as an out to cards like [[Pebbled Paths]] and [[Gnome Hollows]] and added [[Sand Worm]] as an out to [[Root Spiders]] but considering [[Sea Serpent]] instead to combat the [[Coy Nixie]] + [[Thin Ice]] stuff and we already have answers to the spider in [[Geyser]] and [[Floodplain]].



1/2/2026

  • -1 [[The Great Famine]], -1 [[Redmane Hyena]], +1 [[Doctor Demetrius]], +1 [[The Inquisition]]
  • Cut [[The Great Famine]] because it is poor against warded minions, which is something I want to be able to deal with. [[The Inquisition]] serves as somewhat of a removal spell, and I think is just a great card overall in more aggressive fire decks. It also has a mini combo with [[Searing Truth]] if you reveal it you can play it for free. Also trimmed a [[Redmane Hyena]] to make room for [[Doctor Demetrius]]. This is a card I've been wanting to play for awhile to help protect my board from spells like [[Earthquake]] and [[Poison Nova]]. I still like [[Redmane Hyena]] but think overall it's one of the weaker cards in the list. I am contemplating cutting the second one for [[Aino]]. Still also considering [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] over [[Pendragon Banner]].



Overview


The idea of this list is to refresh my favorite, and very first Sorcery deck - Steam Druid. In playing constructed MTG for years, I learned that as new sets are released and people begin brewing decks, a good starting place is to evaluate which archetypes from the previous season may carry over into the new one, and what new tools they might have gained. Given that metagames are highly contextual, this doesn't always work out. However, Fire and Water still have the most efficiently costed Charge minions, and busted Uniques.


One of the biggest differences between this deck and the Steam Druid decks of old is that we don't have reliable access to a spellcaster every turn with the [[Druid]] / [[Tawny]] nerf, which means we cannot reliably cast cards like [[Disintegrate]], [[Pollimorph]], and perhaps most importantly, [[Lava Flow]]. While this is a significant change, I think this archetype of busted Steam cards will do just fine going forward. I won't go through every single card here. By now, it's no secret how strong cards like [[Plague of Frogs]] are in combination with other powerful cards such as [[Sir Agravaine]], [[Boudicca]], and [[Ruler of Thul]]. We also all know by now that Charge minions like [[Redcap Powries]] and [[Monstrous Lion]] are really strong. Instead, I will talk about what is new here, and how our new Avatar, [[Necromancer]] fits into the picture.


I will offer a hot take - Necromancer is at least as good as Druid ever was. There, got that out of the way. Being able to generate a body every single turn while also developing your sites is incredibly powerful. The questions that need answered are: How can we take advantage of the resources that Necromancer generates? And, how do the existing Steam cards help us do that? Gothic gave us many build-around-skeletons cards in Earth and Air, so why Fire and Water? For one, all of the previously mentioned busted Steam uniques that combo well with Plague of Frogs also combo well with skeleton tokens. Additionally, creating an army of skeletons is inherently aggressive, which is a game plan that Fire and Water support perfectly. Lastly, there are some new cards from Gothic that help fill some of the gaps left by the Druid nerf.


New additions from Gothic


We've briefly covered Necromancer, but there are a few other new cards from Gothic that I'd like to cover.


[[Toolbox]] is incredible. It provides access to [[Minor Explosion]] which is absolutely critical, and half of the reason to play this card. Additionally, it provides access to more removal with cards like [[Just a Rock]], [[Angry Mob]], [[Instigator Imp]], [[Boil]], and [[Extinguish]]. Or, perhaps we need graveyard interaction in [[Return to Nature]], or want to play around an opposing [[Poison Nova]] and cast [[Baptize]] to protect a minion or two. Or, perhaps we simply want a Charge minion in [[Petrosian Cavalry]] to apply pressure in a simplified game state. Toolbox does all of this while allowing us to keep the mainboard lean.


[[Redmane Hyena]] is here for a few reasons. For one, it is a beast that fits in well with our [[Pond]] package. More importantly, it offers some additional graveyard hate against the [[Archimago]] decks of the world, and the many other new graveyard shenanigans from Gothic such as [[Grigori Rasputin]]. Even if our opponent isn't planning on playing out of their graveyard, the Hyena helps clear out minions from the opponents grave to make [[Boneyard]] one sided.


[[Sacred Stag]] is one of my favorite cards from Gothic. On rate it's a very solid minion. It's also yet another beast that we can play ahead of curve with [[Pond]]. However the real reason for including the Stag is the Ward it comes with, providing us a minion that is resilient to an opposing [[Poison Nova]] or can simply represent card advantage in combat.


I almost created an entire section in this primer for [[Gift of the Serpent]]. The floor here is turning our skeletons into removal spells that cantrip. The ceiling is turning [[Infernal Legion]] into a one sided board wipe that cantrips. Additionally, it combos well with some of the usual suspects such as [[Collicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], and [[Sir Agravaine]]. As I mentioned, we lost access to several powerful removal spells with the Druid nerf - Gift of the Serpent helps fill that gap while maintaining some of the card advantage element of the previous Steam Druid decks. It's worth mentioning that while this is a very effective way of dealing with ground minions, it means that large Airborne minions can still be a challenge. This is the primary reason for playing double [[Panorama Manticore]] over [[Askelon Phoenix]], and also means we still need [[Infiltrate]] as a hard removal option. All of that said, Gift of the Serpent may look strange on the surface, but I promise that it will impress you. There's a reason the fourth copy is in the Collection.


[[Searing Truth]] is one that I think most people recognized as powerful when it was previewed, and it certainly is that. It's card draw and a Death's Door finisher all in one card. However, after playing with this card, I learned a few things. First off, this card is not always good in game states where you are behind, which is why I play 2 copies instead of 3. The self damage can be too much leaving it stuck in your hand in many situations. With that said, if your deck is built aggressively, and has at least somewhat of a lean, low to the ground mana curve, this card is an excellent inclusion. This deck has a few painful cards to reveal such as [[Infernal Legion]], but ultimately we are designed here to keep the opponent on the back foot, which means that Searing Truth should help us more than hurt us.


[[Swap]] isn't really a new card. Hopefully this isn't as much of a hot take as my earlier statement, but it's one of the most powerful Water spells in the game. That being said, Necromancer some how pushes this card further over the top by giving us a guaranteed body every turn to Swap around with our opponents minions, or even more fun - stealing an opposing [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Key to the City]].


[[Altar of Malachai]] is extremely powerful. Changing the math on "who dies first?" when both players are at Death's Door is a one of a kind effect in Sorcery, and Necromancer ensures that we can set aside a disposable minion to sacrifice for it. Similarly, [[Temple of Moloch]] gives us a Phyrexian Tower to convert skeletons into more expensive spells ahead of curve. You can even use it to sacrifice opposing minions that you [[Infiltrate]]. We want to position both of these sites further back if we can, especially Temple of Moloch, since it's a symmetrical effect.


There isn't much that needs to be said about [[River of Blood]]. Since this is an aggressive deck, we want to ensure our opponents can't use [[Divine Healing]] to undo the work we've done. There could be metagames where you don't need this card, but for now I am including it to cover my bases.


A few honorable mentions for old cards:

  • [[Torshammar Trinket]], [[Pendragon Banner]], and [[Drums of Doom]] all serve to make our skeletons and other cheaper bodies more threatening. With Banner and Drums, you will want to carry these on a Stealth minion such as [[Sir Agravaine]], or carry them on your Avatar and take a step forward.
  • [[Firebreathing]] is doing some work to fill the gap left behind by [[Lava Flow]]. We no longer have [[Tawny]] to reliably cast Lava Flow deep in enemy territory, but we do have a significant number of Beasts and Dragons which allow us a similar effect.


A few cards that I wanted to play, but couldn't find room:

  • [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] clearly combos very well with Necromancer. Ultimately, I decided to go with [[Pendragon Banner]] to lean more aggressively, but I could see working this card in one day.
  • [[Aino]] is just an all around very strong card. I simply could not find room for her but is one that's still up for consideration.
  • Similar to Aino, [[Doctor Demetrius]] I think is just a generally strong card. Ward is an incredibly powerful ability and very important in minion heavy strategies to protect your board from [[Poison Nova]]. This is the card I want to make room for the most.


Wrapping up


I'll just quickly cover some strengths and weakness of this deck.


Strengths:

  • Aggressive and proactive. Sets the tempo of the game and asks your opponent if they have the proper answers.
  • Mana efficient - Necromancer helps ensure that we are using our mana each turn.
  • Effective at generating card advantage. Some games we will just make an army of skeletons, which often requires our opponent to use resources from their hand without us having to do the same to create pressure. We also play cards like [[Gift of the Serpent]], [[Vile Imp]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] which create card positive exchanges.
  • No clear / direct counter. While our plan A is to be aggressive, it can play any kind of game well enough. [[Toolbox]] also gives us access to sure up match ups that might be unfavorable.
  • Sometimes you just win with those busted Steam uniques like [[Plague of Frogs]], [[Sir Agravaine]], [[Boudicca]] and [[Ruler of Thul]].

Weaknesses:

  • Hard control decks. A deck that can consistently deal with our threats using cards like [[Poison Nova]] or [[Earthquake]] can be problematic. With that said, it's equally important that those decks have pressure of their own to follow up with, otherwise Necromancer will continue to apply pressure.
  • Bigger midrange decks. Decks that play a mix of removal and bigger minions, especially Airborne minions, I can see being a problem for this deck. Still, I think this deck has the tools to win match ups like that even if it's not favorable.


If you made it this far, thank you very much for reading. If you enjoyed this primer, please consider giving it a like and following for future decks. Feel free to comment below and let me know what you think.


Thank you! - Quinn

deckinfo.name: Ghost's Fire Pathfinder 3.0 - 7th/43 at SCG Atlanta (4-2)
deckinfo.primer:
I played this deck like 3 times before the constructed tournament in Atlanta. I'm not a brewer but wanted something mono color that I was already familiar with.


Bureau of Occult Control is coming out. Locked myself out of my collection on my final match but I played a very poor opening anyways against a water necro with a perfect open so I doubt it would have helped.


I had mask of mayhem in for the first game instead of trinket since I didn't realize it was also errata'd. I may put it back in though. Making a Coy Nixie have to attack at the beginning of a turn and get it off the troll bridge would be absolute money.


Sinterfee was my MVP. And Searing Truth. It sealed the deal on three of my four wins and was a good dice roll on the stallout when opponent had 5 life vs my 20. I've lost many games after that point.


Choosing to go second for the second-player seer saved me from once again leading out with a mirror realm, but I lost that game while door to door and if he didn't kill me I had him, so...?


Btw, I'm high on Key to the City but out of 9 total games it's never come out once.


I think next iteration I want to do silver bullet for the truth and put one Gift of the Serpent in the collection.

deckinfo.name: 1st Place Cornerstone w/Gothic (6-0) The Red Comet
deckinfo.primer:
I registered for my LGS’s Cornerstone (we put in a lot of effort to get that status - should out to Battlegrounds in Richmond, VA!) but hadn’t played for five months. Going into the tournament, I needed 1) an Avatar I had at least some experience with 2) a deck that was pretty easy to pilot 3) something that could hopefully win or not make me look entirely foolish ;)


After looking at my old pre-Gothic decks, I landed on the “red deck wins” Pathfinder in a dusty deck box. I figured, “there have to be some cool new toys and more fire sites,” and I was pleasantly surprised. There’s a fair amount of Gothic in this deck as a result! I would add a Horns of Behemoth for the Wasteland if I had pulled one and I totally overlooked Vindictive Nation, which is also an easy add in lieu of one of the duals.


The Avatar pilots no differently than before, you have to attempt the optimal pattern to enable a path to at least six sites, but either via Giant, Warhorse, or just walking over a few sites, you can easily get to 10+ simply because of the tempo you have.


The deck archetype is classic sligh/red deck wins. You simply want to be as aggressive as possible. Gift of the Serpent, especially with Dragonettes, is AWESOME for taking out problematic minions. Searing Truth is an MVP as it gets you even more cards if you need them, but can also kill an Avatar instantly on DD. I’d definitely figure out a way to cut some things (I.e. Minor Explosion) to get up to max for each of those. I didn’t bother with any of the collection artifacts as they are simply too slow. The only collection card is a Hounds in case you elect to cast it from Molten Maar.


If you’re looking for something than can simply

blitz out a win, particularly before folks figure out deck efficiency and the meta, this may be a good choice for you. I’d you’re looking for something with some neat combos and cool interactions, there are a few, but really this is all about the burn. Enjoy the heat!

deckinfo.name: Waterfinder

Deck made for Sorcerer Summit Elo League January 2026.


Deck is a mix of all the best water cards , combined with Pathfinder and Omphalos card advantage and a lot of good minions on curve with high power or broken abilities. Sprinkle in some acceleration and Silver Bullets for the kill.


Winrate in January league: 75%+! with around 100 games and counting. Got second spot in regular season, Made it to finals in January26, where I lost to Avatar of Air.


Good results against most decks and avatars.

Weaknesses are Enchantress (Drought!) and Archimago (little hate).


Mulligan for curve and accelaration. Must keep cards are Athlantean Fate and Mesmerism.

deckinfo.name: Hate
deckinfo.primer:
Check out the video for HATE on my channel Lord of Itza!


The premise of this deck is to utilize discard effects to limit your opponent's options to eliminate the numerous small threats in the deck. As a bonus, many of the effects in this deck Banish cards, which prevent Deathrite abilities from resolving and also inhibits decks that utilize the cemetery, particularly Archimago and Deathspeaker.


February 24, 2026


Removed

  • 2 Drought
  • 2 Sphere of Animosity
  • 1 Char Omphalos
  • 4 Men of Leng
  • 3 Quarrelsome Kobolds
  • 2 Askelon Phoenix
  • 4 Blink
  • 1 Peasant Revolt
  • 3 Dark Alley
  • 2 Plague Pits
  • 2 Treetop Hideout

Collection

  • 1 Displace
  • 2 Grapple Shot


Added

  • 4 Wiccan Tools
  • 2 Peacemaker Arbalest
  • 1 Grigori Rasputin
  • 3 Swiven Scout
  • 1 Corruptor Freak
  • 2 Sturmgiest
  • 1 Bane of Aventis
  • 2 Legion of Gall
  • 3 Grapple Shot
  • 4 Den of Evil
  • 2 Funeral Pyre
  • 1 Merlin's Tower

Collection

  • 1 Detonate
  • 1 Gift of the Serpent
  • 1 Flayer


After a number of games at my local store, on TTS, and at SorceryCon, the deck has reached this composition. I removed Sphere of Animosity as I have found that the Persecutor needs to be able to move and be aggressive, so the Sphere could actually backfire onto me. Quarrelsome Kobolds was also a difficult choice to remove, but I wanted to try out Swiven Scouts. Between the Scouts, Accusation, Feast, etc., I have found that I am aware of my opponent's complete hand throughout most of the game. I also opted to add Wiccan Tools so that the Pith Imps could cast their stolen spell, and also to replace the draw from Blink's removal. Grapple Shot was added to make the deck more aggressive. Askelon Phoenix was removed in favor of Legion of Gall, which feels much more in theme with the deck since it banishes so many cards. I also refined the Collection to a broader option of spells.

deckinfo.name: Judge, Jury, & Persecutioner
deckinfo.primer:
We are running this deck to be as utility-based as possible with a heavy emphasis on the collection to have the answer you need to a wide range of scenarios. This deck is fine with going either first or second and it's definitely conducive to a mid-range strategy that can extend/scale itself to the late game if necessary.


**Update (2/18/26):

  • Traded out 2x Searing Truth (not as reliable as I expected) and Added x2 Drought to combat a water-heavy meta
  • Traded out 1x Bind Evil to maximize the amount of Banish Evils in the deck, having the ability to target any region has proven way too beneficial in more cases than not
  • Traded out 1x Intrepid Hero to maximize the amount of Redmane Hyenas in the deck which doubles as additional GY hate
  • Shifted lands around for additional threshold consistency (tracked in deck history). Specifically of Note: Removed City of Souls as it exposed me to guaranteed death blows more than once
  • Traded out 2x Betrayal for 2x Infiltrate to be able to hold onto the minion for the right time is generally more advantageous in this deck. Infiltrate being 1 less mana and 2 less fire threshold are also exceptionally important for tempo
  • Traded out 1x Peacemaker Arbalest for 1x Torshammar Trinket to enable creature alphas and versatility**


The ideal opening hand for spells - One or a mix of the following:

  • Vile Imps or Lesser Blood Demons - for early removal/value and to turn on later Redmane Hyenas
  • Kettletop Leprechaun - So you can continue to draw spells at the beginning of turn
  • Toolbox - Consistency and additional ways to draw key cards, most of which are in the deck
  • Landmass - while more expensive then artifact ramp, it helps build out the board for greater hits with Border Militia and Guards as the game progresses and is less vulnerable to removal/being destroyed.


The ideal opening hand for sites - One or a mix of the following:

  • Pebbled Paths - for defense against more aggressive decks
  • Active Volcano, Fertile Earth, Steppe - make sure not to neglect threshold
  • Silent Hills - Works multiple angles in this deck. It can work as an auxiliary to Pebbled Paths to nullify enemy charge, it will pop early minion wards nearby, and it will silence detrimental Genesis effects from your above-rate minions (Lesser Blood Demon, Corruptor Freak, Greater Blood Demon, Shackled Demon), and will temporarily silence minions like Pudge Butcher to allow for repositioning.


The deck's goal is to continually put out more valuable minions than your opponent, while keeping the board clear (via Bind Evil, Begone, Betrayal) with the Persecutor's fantastic range that can accrue free movement from your own minions.


As the game progresses though, so does the strategy a bit. I've included 2x Border Militias (+1 in the collection) as wells as 2x Guards! to either help put the final nail in the coffin, or conversely work as a way to provide the deck more time if you're behind and need to rebuild. The additional free movement Persecutor takes can make spells like Guards! hit at the maximum or near maximum amount of units produced (7-9). I've enabled flex support for this plan as well with 3x House Arn Bannerman, and Boudicca (both good w or w/o foot soldiers), as well as 1x Torch and Pitchfork in the collection.


The mana curve was designed to stick mid-range as the Persecutor can also act as a flex to inflict damage if necessary, hence the inclusion of the 2x Peacemaker Arbalests which scale the avatar's damage nicely, but will also work fantastically on a minion like Intrepid Hero in tandem with the Persecutor turning anything evil for additional easy one-hit removals.


**Cards I'm Experimenting With**


Sites:

  • Wizard's Den - Additional card draw, but worried about more non-threshold producing sites


Artifacts:

  • Amulet of Niniane - Being so mobile makes you way more vulnerable to taking magic to the face. This may be valuable.


Magic:

  • Lash - Double value from larger minions as positioning isn't an issue

deckinfo.name: The Wild Bunch
deckinfo.primer:
Howdy,


This is my exceptional mono fire deck! The goal of this list is to put early pressure on the opponent with efficient minions, eke out card advantage where we can, and hopefully land a killing blow with a lucky burn spell.


Since [[Druid]] got nerfed I'm going with the next best thing to [[Tawny]], our friend the [[Persecutor]]!

  1. He is wearing a cowboy hat! I love a good Western!
  2. Free movements allow us to still run burn spells effectively, and his other ability gives us the best removal in the game [[Begone!]]. [[Begone!]] is absolutely insane it can take out ward minions, stealth minions, and [[Root spider]] since it does not target! 
  3. Two power is not nothing, he gets the beats in and carries a [[Torshammar Trinket]] with the best of them.


We are aiming for a consistent and efficient early game. That is why the curve is low and does not include a lot of big finishers like [[Panorama Manticore]]. That is also why we are sticking with one element. A big benefit of being mono fire is we get to run fun utility lands for extra value! 

  • [[Town]]: early ramp, a lot of the minions are exceptional and town will smooth out your early game.
  • [[Ersatz Platz]] is our 3rd and 4th [[Town]]. It's a little awkward but as long as you are netting two mana off it in a turn I think it's worth it. Also allows us to play a bunch of utility lands out of our collection.
  • [[Sinkhole]]: Removes problems like [[Pebbled Paths]] or [[Perilous Bridge]]. 
  • [[Wizards Den]]: Free card advantage-ish!!
  • [[Rift Valley]]: Sometimes deals with problematic sites, sometimes a free movement spell.

7 to 8 colorless sites seems to be the sweet spot if you consistently want to get (F)(F) early. We are running 9, because [[Active Volcano]] is now a thing and [[Ersatz Platz]] could be (F).


Okay, So we are mono fire [[Persecutor]] and trying to abuse [[Town]]! We need to jam in every (3)(F) cost exceptional minion we can find! 

  • [[Corruptor Freak]] & [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] can easily be cast turn 2 off [[Town]] and any (F)site. Both benefit from free movement with [[War Horse]], but if you have to take some damage off of them no big deal! It’s better to get out early pressure.
  • If you are braver than me you could definitely run [[Slobbermaw]], but 4 damage is a big setback in aggro mirrors where you are trying to be a little more controlling! I often found [[Slobbermaw]] stuck in my hand.
  • Rounding it out with [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Barging Barghest]], and [[Redcap Powries]]. All solid 3 drops that can be cast turn 2 if you have [[Active Volcano]] + [[Town]].
  • If your meta is heavy earth and you're expecting a lot of [[Pebbled Paths]] and [[Root Spider]] I could see swapping out [[Redcap Powries]] for [[Khamaseen Mummy]].

We end our minion curve @(4) which is nice because If we draw a [[Town]] we never have to use [[Persecutor]] to draw a site and can start getting beats in!

  • [[Hotwheels]] was such a disappointment 2 power is just too low impact. I still have 1 in because he is good at landing a killing blow.
  • [[Clamor of Harpies]] is insane with [[Jihad]], an evil minion to help move [[Persecutor]], and airborne is just nice. A solid include. 
  • [[Hillock Basilisk]] is absolutely insane and no I will not elaborate lol


The rest of the deck is a variety of burn spells, feel free to adjust for whatever is best for you and your meta. Don't be afraid to throw burn at an avatar's face if you have nothing better to do. A few notes.

  • I hate [[Toolbox]] in an aggro deck it's just a (2) mana tax that slows down your tempo!. I looked at a lot of mono fire list collections and the main inclusions where artifact and land hate [[Raze]] does both of these things!
  • [[Peasant Revolt]] is our only (5) drop. It's not needed but it does answer a lot of questions and is my favorite safety blanket.
  • [[Searing Truth]] best killing blow in the game, but don't be afraid to draw cards if you can find time to cast it.


Thoughts:

  • Trying out [[Holy water]] over [[Disintegrate]], deals with ward and is cheaper. I don't know if tapping a minion is worth it though.
  • [[Hand of Glory]] has been pretty good as just another [[Torshammar Trinket]], and allows for some surprise spellcaster thangs.
  • -1 [[Saracen Raiders]] +1 [[Redmane Hyena]], lowers curve, lots of upside with hyena could cast [[firebreathing]]??
  • Trying [[Accusation]] out, and as much as it pains me I am seriously considering [[Toolbox]]. [[Raze]] has been.... okay
  • I also REALLY wanna fit [[Pith Imp]] in, but a 2nd threshold is a big change

deckinfo.name: EAT THE REALM
deckinfo.primer:
"CURIOSITY IS GLUTTONY. TO SEE IS TO DEVOUR." –Victor Hugo


This is a straightforward deck that seeks to apply pressure with [[Realm-Eater]] equipped with [[Flaming Sword]], [[Key to the City]], [[Flame of the First Ones]], [[Ring of Morrigan]], and [[Torshammar Trinket]]. By increasing the power of our avatar, we make it hard for enemy minions to take advantage of an advanced avatar in their own territory, while simultaneously increasing our clock.


Utilizing [[Fine Courser]], [[War Horse]], [[Blink]], and [[Teleport]], we can move [[Realm-Eater]] around after eating a site, meaning we can ideally get away with never having to actually digest any of them. If needed to, it's important to note that if you tap [[Realm-Eater]] to digest a site, you'll remove Immobile from it, no matter how many undigested sites remain.


This deck utilizes [[Frontier Settlers]], [[Landmass]], and [[Sow the Earth]] to allow mana development on turns 3-5 without having to tap [[Realm-Eater]] to play sites, freeing it up to advance and eat sites.


[[Darkest Dungeon]] can act as a win condition, but its primary purpose is as a secondary [[Mount Ussar Sanctuary]].


[[Plate of the Whale]] can be good if [[Realm-Eater]] can reach the power requirement, but I found that it's too dead of a card otherwise that it's not great here.


A fuller deck tech will come after I manage to test the deck more extensively.


To Test:


I've found from my games so far that getting an early [[Landmass]] is more important than getting an early Castle or [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]], so I want to experiment with leaning more into fast ramp starts. Since the deck runs so few minions, [[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]] should be a powerhouse, even at the cost of turning off our own horses.


-2 [[Mix Ignis]]

-2 [[Angel's Egg]]

+2 [[Mix Terra]]

+1 [[Landmass]]

+1 [[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]]

deckinfo.name: Consume the Realm and Everything Within
Snapple
deckinfo.primer:
Here is my attempt at a competitive mid-range deck made from the best stuff in Earth! I like this deck enough that I took the time to update the primer to be much more thorough and cover every one of my card choices. Let's burrow in:


Artifacts:


Onyx Core remains an inclusion that is welcome more often than not. The benefits of drawing it early are obvious, but even late game it essentially provides an extra ward for some positive tempo plays.


Toolbox/SilverBullet replaces Common Sense and frees up a lot of slots in the main deck so you don't have situational ordinaries/exceptionals like Dispel and Divine Healing taking up space there.


Holy Water (collection) is another ward for anything that needs it, particularly something that has lost its initial ward and is crucial for maintaining your board presence. Also useful for getting rid of large evil threats that are unaffected by Bury/Cave-In.


Pnakotic Manuscript plays well enough with warded minions immune to the damage or supported by Lady Iseult, Crown Prince if you have another mortal, or Kettletop to trigger its ability.


Auras and Magic:


Crusade is an automatic inclusion for any mono-Earth deck. Ideally you want it early and placed on your opponent's side of the board for maximum aggression.


Tithe can potentially extend the time you have to keep drawing spells instead of sites for each of your turns. Casting it early also gives you greater selection of which sites you get to place in a deck that doesn't play Crossroads.


Dispel (collection) is most often a Toolbox target for when you need to get rid of a particularly troublesome aura or artifact, or to stop an Enchantress or Battlemage from running you over.



Border Militia is a versatile little ordinary that can provide you with some cheap fodder for slowing down enemy aggression, or overwhelm the board later when combined with King of the Realm. Just be careful if you choose to use it against Battlemage because they can easily turn it into a lot of card advantage if they manage to find a timely Screaming Skull. Be careful about using this when Order of the White Wing is on the board!


Bury (collection) is a cheap, staple removal spell that only tends to be bad against Water decks. Don't forget that it can be used to burrow artifacts and potentially deprive your opponent of their benefits if they don't have a burrowing minion to retrieve them.


Call to War has a lot of worthy targets in this deck and acts kind of like Rescue if your aim is to replace a dead exceptional mortal and you need your Toolbox for something else. Take Shield Maidens first as they are generally your best exceptional mortals.


Rescue (collection) has a lot of situational usefulness. Lady Iseult and King of the Realm are excellent minions that are sadly easy to kill, so being able to fetch Rescue on demand can help maintain a favorable board state with them.


Cave-in is similar in utility to Bury, but has more potential to punish over-committed opponents at the cost of one more mana and not being a Toolbox target.


Gigantism is an infrequent but always welcome spell with its ability to turn even a lowly foot soldier into a serious threat for a single turn. Use it wisely!


Earthquake is a game-changer more often than not for its ability to kill multiple minions at a reasonable cost and switch sites around to make them more vulnerable to attack in the absence of Crusade. It's naturally less effective against decks with a lot of water sites, but you can still move things around to open them up to more advantageous angles of attack, potentially breaking up bodies of water to strand dangerous enemies like Mester Stoor Worm and Giant Shark.


Guards! gives you some serviceable cannon fodder in a pinch and can help close out games in tandem with King of the Realm, Bannerman and/or Shield Maidens. Be careful it doesn't overlap with Order of the White Wing!


Landmass helps you ramp into the mid game as a mini Tithe to ensure you can afford to ward important minions on curve.


Pendragon Legacy can get back all your VIPs and even unique sites that may have been destroyed, giving this deck an edge in especially grindy games.


Minions:


Carrion Beetles (collection) is here to counter Archimago for the most part.


Revered Revenant is a cheap and effective minion that only works in a Savior deck. You will usually play this with a ward on turn 2, but can sometimes get away with it on turn 1 if your starting site is a Blessed Village or Pilgrim's Shrine.


Angel Ascendant is another cheap minion that really wants a ward, worth holding for a turn if your opponent is off to a slow start..


Holy Warrior comes pre-warded, so he serves as a good companion to a Revenant and is a solid defender against early aggression.


Kettletop Leprechaun having deathrite means you want to be aggressive with it to draw a site, and only give it a ward if you really need it to defend for a turn.


Lady Iseult is the classiest dame on your side of the board and does a fine job of maintaining your board presence in most situations. She can allow you to be a bit more aggressive even with your smaller minions given that they come right back to your hand if they die. She is unfortunately rather easy to kill due to being low-power and needing to be nearby the front lines, so try holding a Toolbox for a Rescue in order to keep her around longer. She can also benefit from the protection of sites like Gnome Hollows and Dome of Osiros depending on the situation, so placing those sites forward is ideal in an Iseult game.


Crown Prince is another early minion that holds the line and synergizes well with some of the other cards. He performs well early on under a Crusade and even later with King of the Realm sitting somewhere relatively safe.


Root Spider is another high-utility minion with a lot of value for its low cost. It can single-handedly shut off avenues of attack from non-burrowing minions and save you from an early onslaught when used correctly with other defensive cards. It can also be used aggressively, pushing forward and disabling defenders while you gain more ground towards overwhelming your opponent's side of the board.


Order of the White Wing is an all around solid minion that punishes reanimator decks and cards like Necromancer and sites that produce tokens.


House Arn Bannerman acts like a mini King of the Realm that can also buff your non-mortal minions. Definitely worth a ward, and a great target for Call to War if you already have Shield Maidens on the board.


Royal Bodyguard makes you and your royal VIPs even harder to kill. Very good ward target.


Archangel Michael is a lot of value for a mere 5 mana. Getting a free step and strike makes him invaluable in ward mirrors.


Shield Maidens are utterly busted in a Savior deck and your main target for Call to War because of this. Ideally you want multiples nearby each other because their abilities stack and you hate the idea of your opponent having anything resembling fun.


Scent Hounds (collection) is a cheap solution to annoying cards like Morgana and Infiltrate. Can and probably should also be warded against decks using such cards, as they tend to pack a lot of removal.


Vivien the Enchantress can be game-changing against avatars with high-value abilities like Necromancer and Animist. She can always be used to play or draw an additional site per turn and is almost always worth warding.


King of the Realm makes all mortals yours to command and strong enough to close out games with the help of Border Militia, Shield Maidens and/or Crusade. He only gets thwarted by King Arthur or another King of the Realm played after, so keep removal handy if you anticipate your opponent playing these cards. He is generally more valuable staying safely in the back row or ideally nearby wherever Lady Iseult happens to be.


Tragedy Worrywart (collection) can be a lifesaver against any deck packing a lot of damaging spells thereby negating your ward strategy.


Sites:


City of Souls provides an excellent source of free mana for your avatar to keep pumping wards. Best placed in your back row to reduce the chance of your opponent exploiting its drawback.


Dome of Osiros is a great defensive site for one of your MVPs to hang out in, like Vivien or King of the Realm. Also acts as a massive speed bump if your opponent can't muster removal for whatever you have parked here.


Haystack is somewhat of a flex slot, but well worth it when it gets to punish combo decks running fetch cards. Also neutralizes Murder of Crows quite effectively.


Kingdom of Agartha is another flex slot that tends to be more useful against decks running a lot of minion removal. It also allows you to be more selective with how you use Savior's ward ability because burrowing minions are generally difficult targets for spells.


Gnome Hollows is a life-saver against any minion big enough to be a true threat to your avatar, making it an ideal first turn play to serve as an effective hideout in most games.


Mirror Realm does just about whatever you need it to. It can copy useful enemy sites if need be, or can serve as an extra copy of your more important sites like City of Souls for even more ramp.


Mount Ussar Sanctuary is rather self-explanatory. It's probably best placed in the back row alongside another defensive site like Gnome Hollows.


Pebbled Paths stops charge minions so they don't get free attacks to break your wards.


Pilgrim's Shrine is another power source for your Revenants and a free ward for anything.


Pillar of Zeiros might actually be the only site you'd rather not draw early, as its utility is generally greater the longer the game goes on. It can save your life against burn strategies with massive life gain and makes for a great potential hoser against dedicated cemetery strategies. Remember that this affects both cemeteries, so you might want to Rescue something before playing it.


Rift Valley is best used early and aggressively as a means of opening up another avenue of attack against the opponent's side of the board. It's not quite as powerful as Crusade, but it can serve well enough if played correctly.

deckinfo.name: God of Wards

Hey there! Thanks for checking this deck out. Main focus is to pump minions out with ward and attacking sites. Then to finishing with holy nova or kiss of Judas or earthquakes to clear a path for the finish.


now warding minions with stealth is pretty fun. I do need to find a way to ad aino in here. I also may test playing with magic bullet and or toolbox in the future. I just don’t feel like paying extra mana to cast a card though.


bless is for those situations where you try and trade with a minion and you can re ward it to make it even harder to kill.
