BASIC OVERVIEW

Start with automatic hand advantage, +1 card going first on the play and gain an even better +2.5 card advantage going second on the DRAW turn 1. (.5 when you consider the second player scry) Going second is almost always the best option unless matched against an extremely aggressive list.

Really trying to dig through the deck as much as possible using constant spellbook draws, rivers, and all the minions / spells that help look for early big combos to put an opponent on their heels with hopefully something they cant come back from. Really take advantage of any opportunity to draw from spellbook and apply pressure. Water is so strong and filled with top tier uniques just find em try not to overextend and enjoy beating good decks with [[Spellslinger]]!






OPENING HAND



Spells

Draw 4 spells and pretty much always mulligan 3 of them unless you already have a ramp card in hand such as [[Mix Aqua]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]], or [[Aquamarine Core]].

You are also looking for any of the game changers / bombs mono water lets you use. Cards to look for are [[Atlantean Fate]], [[Ruler of Thul]], [[Mesmerism]], [[Plague of Frogs]], [[Ring of Morrigan]], depending on the avatar youre up against any of these can be a very strong keep.

If no ramp or game changer in opening hand mulligan 3 spells and the extra 4th card you keep should be something you can play early on curve 1 - 3 mana cost if possible

If you start the game with any ramp card and none of the prime game changers you can keep the ramp card and any big boss spells like [[Lord of Lies]], [[The Green Knight]] or [[Questing Beast]] any of the 5 and 6 cost spells can be trouble for an opponent early.

Also you can grab any of the strong 4 mana minions if you know the deck youre facing is very aggressive.




Sites

Pretty much always keeping sites opening hand and digging for spells cause we are not threshold stressed but if you already have ramp + a big minion or a game changer in the opening draw you can ditch regular rivers really hoping for movement sites [[Innsmouth Dock]] [[River Rapids]] or [[Maelstrom]]. I also like good defense in [[Troll Bridge]] or even a [[Wizard's Den]] for more draw. Big fan of [[Undertow]] turn 2 and pulling [[Spellslinger]] to the side against air and fire decks makes him a little safer and harder to hit with projectiles.


Sites are mainly Rivers (ex. [[Winter River]]) and on every search youre looking for ramp cards just like the mulligan. Unless you have one already then if you do start looking for something big to play with it instead.

Of course if you see the perfect card for whatever situation youre in at that moment you can keep that on top too.


Really always hoping for at least 1 River (ex. [[Spring River]]) opening hand. If your hand is already perfect and you want to mulligan sites, keep 1 river at least or dig 3 deep for a river. Early scry means more info especially with a [[Fenvale Muse]]. It is a real pain having muse and no rivers. The muse/river combo early can be very strong even works late game when looking for a Deaths Door finisher








TIPS/TRICKS?




(Similar list to my deck Cruel Waters, I did build Slinger first but Cruel has Waveshaper and a few different cards with a lower ceiling. Waveshaper is such a nice mix of strength and control but this is a faster very strong fun list! Beating good decks with the Slinger is always a good time. Very decent win rate when I pilot)


Deck very consistently cast out huge minions and spells.


Going second feels insane with so many cards in hand early. 5 cards turn 1 is nuts especially with a [[Wizards Den]] in hand.



Gaining the full effect of [[Spellslinger]] mono water really comes with knowing your threshold is always good to go in a mono water list. Allowing you to keep drawing from the spell book. Having to dig for the right threshold will slow down things dramatically. Constantly drawing spells every turn is what really gives [[Spellslinger]] extra benefit.

Splashing even one threshold is to tough, having double threshold requirements in a second thresh is impossible if you want to keep a decent hand size.


Now with the full benefit of the draw I love water having every river to constantly cycle the deck only searching for bombs mixes etc. ([[Mix Aqua]] [[Four Waters of Paradise]] [[Mesmerism]] [[Atlantean Fate]] [[Ruler of Thul]] or all the big minions once you have a mix or combo). Constant drawing + the 4th card out the gate hopefully going second for 5 cards turn 1, make the mixes so much more powerful and can push combos out that can be tough to recover from especially with the game changers full water has


[[Mesmerism]] is just so good will win the game most of the time! Use it wisely!


SWAP MAKES PLAYING MIXES ALOT TRICKIER IF YOURE PLAYING AGAINST WATER BE CAUTIOUS PLAY THEM MORE STRATEGIC


WATER IS STRONG, going to be a lot of tough mirror type games. Slinger can punch faster then most still, just need to be careful with enemy [[Mesmerism]]s taking the big Minions. Use movement like [[Riptide]], [[Maelstrom]], [[River Rapids]], [[Nelly Long Arms]], maybe even [[Swap]] to play things in safer places and move into attack-able sites.



Deck feels very strong still, might be even better w/ Gothic since everyones decks got bigger and we get all the Scry action with the rivers (ex. [[Winter River]])





EVERY CARD AND WHAT I THINK




AVATAR:


[[Spellslinger]] is a very basic avatar his main + is the extra card out the gate making the mix combos less detrimental to thinning out our own hand. Whats really helpful is the mono water sites so threshold is always okay and you can keep drawing spells. Making [[Spellslinger]] tap to draw sites the main way we collect sites. Only draw a site at the start of turn if a combo in hand requires it if not keep digging spells. I will say after turn 3-4 sometimes drawing a site is necessary so you dont fall to far behind in mana but even so if you have strong 3 drops (ex. [[Lugbog Cat]]) or a [[Mix Aqua]] combo you might not need to draw a site and can keep drawing spells for advantage.



SPELLBOOK:




• AURA


[[Atlantean Fate]] (x1)

Can be a game winner one of the best cards in the game! Setting an opponents threshold to water only can hurt bad, especially if they don't run water spells. Just be careful ordinary sites not being affected can be tricky to play around at times.

Will submerge still on ordinary water sites or any flooded ordinary site





• ARTIFACTS


[[Aquamarine Core]] (x1)

Always nice to see early. Helps get the deck running a little faster. Simple and effective +1 mana.


[[Mix Aqua]] (x2)

RAMP O’CLOCK! Everything is a water spell and can always use a mix. Really hoping to see some ramp early for some big plays to apply pressure whenever possible. Usually a good idea to wait to crack a mix until there is a 5-6 cost water spell needing to be cast but in an emergency these can come in handy to combo out whatever is needed.


CLUTCH MIX COMBOS

Turn 1

[[Ludbog Cat]] or [[Aino]] right out the gate can be very strong for early pressure. Can be very risky if they have a turn 2 answer (ex. [[Polymorph]]). Even stronger play with [[Polar Explorers]] turn 2. Safer for the cat, constant stealth attacks for [[Aino]].

[[Nelly Longarms]] has been an emergency turn 1 or 2 play if they cast something crazy out the gate or play a tricky home site. Risky but definitely an option.


Turn 2

[[Questing Beast]] crazy turn 2 for a hard to dodge stealth 5 power next turn.

[[Atlantean Fate]] is an option here depends if an opponent over extends and how much sites can be effected but definitely an option here.


IF against an aggro matchup (ex. [[Interrogator]] or [[Sorcerer]]) playing any of the strong 4 drops in the list can be very strong defense on turn 2


Turn 3

Biiiiig minions can be activated here (ex. [[Lord of Lies]] [[Mester Stoor Worm]] or [[The Green Knight]]). Can win a game early if theres no answer for the early pressure.


Turn 4

A lot of good options here. Be very careful not to overextend. Stay spread out if possible.


Turn 5

With a mix already in play prior.. this turn can be huge playing 2 god tier 4 mana water spells in one turn can just turn a game on its head.

[[Mesmerism]] + anything else

[[Ruler of Thul]] + [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] avatar is a 3 power with 2 [[Ruler of Thul]]s

Crazy options here.



[[Ring of Morrigan]] (x1)

Such a win more card. Can gain just enough life to outlast opponent and helps with trades or removal in general. Great to see for a Deaths Door final avatar hit.


[[Torshammar Trinket]] (x1)

Seems to be a card that can really swing a match with favorable minion trades and +1 damage whenever possible. Can be combo’d with [[Plague of Frogs]] if every frog is at a single location each frog can swing with +1 power. The first trinketed frog hitting the Unit to die dropping trinket and letting more frogs pick it up and attack. Can be a sneaky 7 power attack for 1 Mana.

Combo w/ [[Sea Raider]]s to be able to survive or trade up and get an opponents spell for only 1 mana


[[Four Waters of Paradise]] (x1)

RAMP! Try to save for bigger costing/threshold spells. Always on the hunt for this card to cast heavier combos. Great combos in the double 4 drop range. (ex [[Ruler of Thul]] x [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] HUGE damage out put with a board already in play. 11 possible damage alone with Thul x2 and [[Spellslinger]] at 3 power) Great combo piece


Turn 2

On cast can immediately play a 4 mana spell most likely for defense against agro stuff (ex. [[Pirate Ship]], [[Sacred Stag]], or even [[Mesmerism]] if needed)

For a more aggressive offensive option [[Captain Baldassare]] can be a solid play early if he has good options for attacking next turn.





[[Toolbox]] (x2)

Really a [[Common Sense]] for all. Can be insanely clutch just reach into the collection and get what you need!



COLLECTION


[[Just a Rock]] (x1)

One I forget about might be worth something else in slot but can get rid of [[Ring of Morrigan]] or any pesky artifact enemies can carry


[[Led Astray]] (x1)

CLUUUUUTCH forced movement. Great card for game to get someone in range for attack or pings. Can send an entire battalion into a [[Bottomless Pit]] or just away for a turn. One of my favorite tools.


[[Old Salt Anchorman]] (x1)

Mainly here for a minion summon for 2 mana if its absolutely necessary to play a minion to block or something but mana is low he comes in handy.

Can also be very strong against enemy forced movement (ex. [[Avatar of Air]] or forced movement mud list) and can save a squad from [[Bury]] / [[Submerge]] actions! Very tech


[[Riptide]] (x1)

Feels great similar to [[Led Astray]] but with a draw. Great value card in here.


[[Drown]] (x1)

Simple removal. Best saved for real problem minions, pretty much anything strong or has a crazy ability.


[[Horrible Hybrids]] (x3)

Here to help keep a healthy hand size with [[Peculiar Port]] can be used as a decent minion summon in an emergency.


[[Ice Lance]] (x1)

Mainly a Deaths Door snipe. Can be emergency removal for airborn or just extra damage to finish something off.


[[Pirate Ship]] (x1)

Great for defense and if enemy plays water or we have flood action can apply a lot of pressure.




[[Truesight Crossbow]] (x1)

Mainly for when an opponent is at deaths door, can be a sneaky way to avoid blockers with a snipe. Gives some extra range to waterbound creatures! Seeing this late game is preferred but if you see it early play it on your avatar and wait it out. Avatars gain some range and can target stealth minions with spells!!! (can be big for kill spells or [[Mesmerism]]). My favorite tech has been strategically placing either [[Plague of Frogs]] or my minions on board, in a way so that I can run a [[Truesight Crossbow]] from my avatar to whatever minion can tap in range for game.


[[Dank Omphalos]] [[Algor Omphalos]]

Extremely helpful card draw and necessary value to keep up if the game goes late with any real value avatars (ex. [[Sorcerer]], [[Pathfinder]], [[Necromancer]]) Trying to play with movement sites in mind like [[River Rapids]], [[Innsmouth Dock]], or [[Malestrom]] to keep the Omphalos safe and Minions cast there with more options to attack.

Really just insane value here. Even if you draw an artifact it thins the deck and gets you closer to the bombs. If out early can really make a game.







• MINIONS


[[Fenvale Muse]] (x1)

With all the rivers this extends the dig for any of the bombs or ramp cards [[Mix Aqua]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]] or [[Aquamarine Core]]. Helps just sift through the deck even better. Especially turn 1 which is the main reason you should always keep 1 river opening hand.

Combo this with [[Mesmerism]] since she is a Spellcaster youre able to tap [[Spellslinger]] to play or draw a site and move up with [[Fenvale Muse]] to take an enemy minion.


[[Adept Illusionist]] (x2)

A staple in any water deck for me. Just feels like so much value, constant chump blocks or [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] draw. He is also a spellcaster so he can bring out his buddy ol’ pal and start casting [[Ice Lance]] or [[Mesmerism]] from farther for game.


[[Pied Piper of Hamlin]] (x1)

Insanely clutch card and is a must keep against certain matchups. [[Necromancer]] forsure takes all their skelly boys or any deck that wants to use 1 power / token rush / stall stuff. [[Deathspeaker]] and [[Archimago]] come to mind forsure. Try to keep him safely tucked away normally and swing only when needed.


[[Polar Explorers]] (x2)

For attacking with hopefully unseen damage, or finding a new angle to help whatever the agenda is at the moment. Here for tech. Could be anything really. Combo with [[Geyser]] for even crazier back door angles


[[Aino]] (x1)

I can see why this card is a staple surprised it is so expensive but for 3 mana + stealth + movement it can be a very strong card opponents have to get rid of asap.

For me I think id rather see this card late game as a finisher or like a 6 mana [[Ludbog Cat]] + [[Aino]] play. Seeing this early is still nice for early pressure but really combos for a strong start with [[Polar Explorers]] or [[Ruler of Thul]] for constant stealth attacks.


[[Fey Changeling]] (x1)

Helpful for blocker removal and can set an opponent back a turn if they play some huge minion. Just send it back to the hand and continue on about your business. Sending certain genesis cards back to hand can be tricky so watch out for those.


[[Lugbog Cat]] (x3)

It’s extremely hard not to put 3 of these in every water deck. Just value. 3 cost 4 power can cast to any water site. Cast to an enemy back row water site if possible or even better back row on a [[Pristine Paradise]] and just attack.


[[Nelly Longarms]] (x1)

Can be easy removal especially against bigger minions. Normally just a deterrent threat defending her range of sites.

Love to combo with [[Riptide]] or any movement and just pull her into the right angle and drown something big. Playing her with future forced movements in mind can really put opponents on their heels.


[[Sea Raider]] (x3)

Here for much needed card draw. Ability still works even if he dies attacking and is usually worth the sacrifice to help with hand advantage. I really like this card it seems just okay but he always makes opponents sweat and has blessed me with insane top decks.


[[The Lady of the Lake]] (x1)

Cycle any mortal you need! Mainly [[Pirate Ship]], [[Ruler of Thul]] for charge sneak attacks or [[The Green Knight]] feel the best.

Can also grab ARTIFACTS! Which I forget but can be useful for tech or grab a [[Ring of Morrigan]] for door


[[Captain Baldassare]] (x1)

Here for extra draw similar to [[Sea Raider]]. Pure water list just need more draw and this gives some hand advantage, use enemy spells whenever possible. Decent cycle option for [[The Lady of the Lake]].

For best play options he needs some type of site movement (ex. [[Malestrom]], [[Innsmouth Dock]], [[River Rapids]], [[Undertow]]) for free movement into attack range even if he dies casting enemy spells for a turn is just value.

Another good way to keep him around is play him on the heels of other big ally threats and spread them out so they have to choose what to deal with.

Drawing sites on the turn you know he will get an attack off is usually best to be able to cast more opponent spells.


[[Lord of Unland]] (x1)

Usually feels best played submerged at first for a few turns or even the whole game moving under toward enemy avatar for a door blow or back to our [[Spellslinger]] for defense. The +1 in his body of water always feels strong great for trades and huge damage. Was doubting this cards worth and then he came in clutch a ton of times. Combos well with [[Ruler of Thul]] giving a bunch of bonus’. Can be [[Selfsame Simulacrum]]’d for more buffs!

A little tougher to keep him safe these days mainly because of [[Lacuna Entity]] so if possibly play him with no adjacent voids



[[Pirate Ship]] (x3)

Just a strong 4 cost 5x5 BEATER. At worst hes a huge defender and maybe a [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] sacrifice but if on a [[Floodplain]] or connected to enemy water site is such a beast and must be dealt with.


[[Ruler of Thul]] (x1)

Top tier card giving +1 power to allies on the TOP and BOTTOM of the realm + unexpected movement. Very good for sneak attacks for door especially with [[Plague of Frogs]].

Can be cycled with [[The Lady of the Lake]].


[[Sacred Stag]] (x2)

So much value. Can be worth keeping early against agro list like [[Interrogator]] or really any of those fire charge list can be strong defensive value all around. Other than that I think id rather see this mid - late game and would probably bottom this early looking for bombs. Super strong 4 drop.


[[Selfsame Simulacrum]] (x2)

Tech card! Love to copy pretty much any unique / big minion card in this list but pretty much if something is good on board copy it!


[[Lacuna Entity]] (x1)

Useful for removing pesky smaller minions. Ive heard some good opinions on running more then 1 to make sure you remove whatever problem card trying to hide but I dont like having 2 in hand with nothing to use the ability on so only 1 for now.


[[Questing Beast]] (x1)

Really great card all around, 5x5 power is always strong. I like to use this for a final stealth strike at Deaths Door especially with the movement at the end of turn. Just the pressure of a 5 power swing + the added movement feels great. When playing against Earth opponents the movement at the end of turn can be used to move back onto a water site for safety.


[[Lord of Lies]] (x2)

One of the best cards might even be to good to be Elite. Being able to swing for 12 using his ability attacking an enemy Avatar is insane. Can be really strong with [[Polar Explorers]] and [[Ruler of Thul]]. Really can change a game forcing an opponent to double trade their own minions in a fight then punching for 6.


[[Mester Stoor Worm]] (x1)

Waterbound and Submerge hard to kill giant 7 power. Just all value basically a constant smaller [[Poison Nova]] threat on top of that. Can be used to board wipe with the lethal ability and ping for a Deaths Door final blow! Decent combo for [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] for a draw engine it will always stay alive but not attacking for 7 or using ability is tough lol


[[The Green Knight]] (x1)

Can win you the game! Forcing the enemy movement and crushing smaller minons is so good I forget about the strike he does at deathrite! Feels best when played on a [[Troll Bridge]]. This turn 3 with a [[Mix Aqua]] can really set the tone for a game. Also great option for [[Pnakotic Manuscript]]








• MAGIC



[[Plague of Frogs]] (x1)

Great defensively mainly, can buy some time. Crazy draw when paired with [[Pnakotic Manuscript]]. [[Ruler of Thul]] and [[Lord of Unland]] can turn these boys up +1 power for a sneak attacks. Can be used to run artifacts around to different units!


[[Geyser]] (x3)

Important for attacking with waterbound creatures can be secret damage if opponent isnt ready. Hoping to use it for surprise attacks and possibly drowning pesky burrowed minions especially [[Root Spider]]. Can be used with [[Polar Explorer]] or [[Ruler of Thul]] for extremly hard to predict backrow attacks

Fun to attack a [[Bottomless Pit]] if an opponent uses it with no flying minions themselves! Especially with [[The Green Knight]].


[[Polymorph]] (x2)

Banish the original minion so it never sees the cemetery leaving only a little baby enemy frog. Pairs really well with [[Sea Raider]] and [[Captain Baldassare]]. Try to save for a big bomb of a threat.


[[Riptide]] (x3)

Helpful movement spell for your own minions but it can also target enemies. Moving them out the way or closer for whatever you need. Can help facilitate a final blow at Deaths Door. [[Floodplain]] can help with range when needed. CAN TARGET STEALTH

If I end up with a [[Riptide]] opening hand I like to play to the side and [[Riptide]] my avatar over to get out of the way of [[Grapple Shot]] or any pesky projectile right away turn 2 make it a little harder to line up shots

Keeping a spare in the [[Toolbox]] for clutch forced movement + adding draw feels good when it pops off


[[Drown]] (x1)

With so many water sites and the flood ability this is very strong minion removal. Really helps remove pesky artifacts especially ring with an enemy avatar on the move for door or any crazy artifact really.


[[Ice Lance]] (x1)

Not my favorite Deaths Door spell but water doesnt have a ton of options. Usually best to hold until late game if found early, only to be used in emergencies to get rid of some flying or huge minion threat. Being able to pierce and choose any target per space is very good but damage starts at casters location 3, adjacent site 2, next adjacent site 1. Range is a little weaker than I thought but still usually does the job. [[Adept illusionist]] work well with this being a spellcaster the 1st copy can bring out the 2nd and should be in range for a final blow.

Extra in the [[Toolbox]] for a game winner!


[[Kiss of Judas]] (x1)

I see this card mainly as a finisher an unblock-able attack at Deaths Door is hard to beat. Can really help get someone to door if multiple units are surrounding an Avatar. The draw effect really is a nice bonus, can combo with pretty much anything close to an avatar especially [[Plague of Frogs]] and maybe a [[Torshammer Trinket]] to dive bomb some damage and draw 7! Might be as good as it gets


[[Swap]] (x1)

Pretty useful forced movement insane amount of options. Any artifact can be taken or minion moved out of the way to create attacking lanes. Use wisely. Can be used against enemy Omphalos’ forcing them on to sites they can not cast minions on but bringing them closer is tricky if they have good damage magic.


[[Mesmerism]] (x1)

Might be one of the best cards in the deck. Taking someone’s untapped minion and swinging especially if theyre huge feels very good. Can swing the momentum greatly.

Cards to good and is now everywhere. Be careful casting minions to close to Spellcasters but it is hard to avoid.







• SITES


[[Autumn River]], [[Spring River]], [[Winter River]], and [[Summer River]]

Searching hard for ramp cards such as [[Mix Aqua]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]], or [[Aquamarine Core]] pretty much always. Once found start looking for the BOMBS (ex. [[Mesmerism]], [[Atlantean Fate]] [[Ruler of Thul]] [[Plague of Frogs]]) or something big to play (ex. [[The Green Knight]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], or [[Questing Beast]]). Repeat this until you get close to the end game where it’s best to start looking for Deaths Door spells. Late game [[Ring of Morrigan]] [[Toolbox]] or [[Ice Lance]] are probably the best options but you can also look for [[Questing Beast]], [[Mesmerize]], [[Truesight Crossbow]], or maybe [[Riptides]] / whatever is needed at the time.


[[Floodplain]] (x2)

Really helps for attacking with any of the waterbound minions. [[Riptide]] combos similarly, you can flood for more reach and hit some forced movement when needed.

Can help add water threshold to a non water site to play something with higher water threshold requirements.

Will drown unsuspecting burrowed minions!



[[Innsmouth Dock]] (x1)

Strong movement tech. Can pull ally minions from back row forward for safer attacks, can shift a defense and can even target Stealth enemies with the pull ability. Simple and very useful.


[[Maelstrom]] (x1)

Should of had this in here the entire time!!! Can play minions back or to the side pulling them next start of turn to then be in attack range feels very strong. Doesn't always have to be used either but in a full body of water pulling everything in can come in handy


[[Mirror Realm]] (x1)

Here mainly to be a river and scry but can copy something big maybe [[Troll Bridge]] for defense, [[Undertow]] for free movement, or enemy towers for ramp a nice maybe option.

DOUBLE [[Maelstrom]] or [[River Rapids]]!!! insane movement options at all times very good idea to be sneaky with attacks


[[Peculiar Port]] (x2)

Here to assist with keeping a positive hand size. Not always worth a minion play sometimes its better to get off a crazier combo but when cast it can be a very strong extra minion. Opponents may have to waste a spell to get rid of the lil guy and also we get to keep our current hand. Combos well using [[Polar Explorers]] or [[Ruler of Thul]] to help attack backline if the site is placed correctly.


[[River Rapids]] (x2)

WOW! This card in this deck.. just wow! Can be used to push a minion off ITSELF! Having a body of rivers for sneaky movement is just so clutch. Put rivers back row (normal turn 1 river stuff) then it activates with Rapids giving our minions safer spawns and more options to attack.


[[Tadpole Pool]] (x1)

x3 little tadpoles can be used as chump blockers mainly, but if you're lucky you can combo with [[Ruler of Thul]] for a +1 power sneak attack style

Works really well with [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] if that ever makes it back in the deck


[[Troll Bridge]] (x3)

Staple for any water deck. Helps with defense and provides threshold. [[Riptide]]-ing someone into here feels great.


[[Undertow]] (x2)

Super helpful for attacking or adjusting the board in an unseen way. Nice bonus that it is free and adds mana.

Turn 2 moving [[Spellslinger]] to the side for free can be very helpful to avoid Fire and Air projectiles early.


[[Wizard's Den]] (x2)

Draw and hand advantage is top tier. Even if you have to discard later in the game the draw was a card you didn't have before and sometimes people arent even able to attack the site and its just a free draw. Very underrated I believe it should be in pretty much any deck that isn't to threshold stressed.

I dont play this first site most games it tends to be my turn 3 site right or left backline. If possibly trying to play this backline corner for less chance of losing the extra card.













MAYBE CARDS


[[Observatory]] (x2)

Provides some useful information giving a little advantage to the next few turns. I was always skeptical of this site might be better to have towers and push but if used correctly can feel like it extends your hand size. Might be worth a pen/paper or pad.


[[Tide Naiads]] (x1)

Tech card. Can help waterbound minions move around easier. Best used with [[Floodplain]] to keep sites flooded. Good target for [[Shapeshift]]


[[Grim Guisarme]] (x1)

Might need to be x2 so good! Can hit for door out of nowhere with all these big minions. Better saved for door can be brutal used against you. [[Grim Guisarme]] + [[Seirawan Hydra]] is NUTS btw


[[Pnakotic Manuscript]] (x1)

Simple draw support can be used on smaller minions mainly especially a twin [[Adept Illusionist]] but with all the river abilities (such as [[Winter River]]) it can be easy to know what will survive the draw or if youll only take a small amount of damage to the avatar. [[The Green Knight]] with so much defense can be a strong option

+ FROGS LOVE TO READ TURNS OUT! [[Plague of Frogs]] or [[Tadpole Pool]] combo so well for easy draw engine


[[Shapeshift]] (x1)

Looking to shift into something big preferably [[The Green Knight]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], [[Seirawan

Hydra]], or [[Questing Beast]] for a sneak attack.


[[Kelp Cavern]] (x2)

I think of this as a better [[Observatory]], searching the bottom of the deck instead, giving you more card selection and much appreciated water threshold

deckinfo.name: Frogimago's Cube
deckinfo.primer:
Frogimago's YouTube Channel

Join Weekly Drafts Wednesdays @ 7:30pm ET by joining the Sorcerers Summit Discord!

How to Draft on TTS Video Tutorial


Welcome to my cube! I intend for this to be the most powerful singleton cube possible. But if specific cards emerge that are un-fun I will consider cutting them. It grew from its original 360 cards to its current 450-card form with the addition of cards from Gothic! I value a diverse draft experience and would prefer this cube grow to 540 cards once the card pool supports it, likely upon the release of the next set.


HOUSE RULES

  1. SECOND PLAYER SEER – After mulligans, the player going second looks at the top card of their Spellbook or Atlas and may put it on the bottom. 
  2. If you draft [[ADEPT ILLUSIONIST]] you get an additional copy to put in your deck.
  3. If you draft [[DRAGONLORD]], you may choose ANY Unique Dragon in Sorcery as your "Champion". You DO NOT need to draft the chosen Dragon. You may change your Champion between rounds prior to seeing your opponent’s avatar (load it in from your collection for reference).
  4. [[PATHFINDER]] can have duplicates in its atlas. Treat it as if the first line in its text box doesn't exist.
  5. [[IMPOSTER]] - Select 10 different avatars to keep in your collection from outside the game before seeing opponent's avatar. You DO NOT need to draft these collection Avatars.
  6. [[ERIK’S CURIOSA]] instead of being “ripped to pieces” is banished. You take any card from your Collection and put it into your hand. (Does not tutor for any card in Sorcery like it originally did).


STRATEGY GUIDE:

Cores and Mixes are great. There are many expensive bombs, getting them out before your opponent develops their board is an easy way to win. With the addition of cards from Gothic, the curve is much better and aggressive decks have come to together more often. Premium removal is needed to stop the many bombs. Keep an eye out for an Avatar that fits with your gameplan, or the generically great ones like [[Elementalist]], [[Necromancer]], or [[Pathfinder]]. Some of the best cards in the cube are the Cores/[[Philosopher's Stone]], [[Four Waters of Paradise]], [[The Green Knight]], [[Lilith]], [[Ring Of Morrigan]].


PICK ORDER SUGGESTION

Avatars

Artifact Ramp

Premium 2-4 Mana Minions

Threshold Fixing

Removal

Game-ending 5+ Mana stuff


COMBOS

[[Necromancer]] + [[Gilman House]]

[[The Green Knight]] + [[The Lady of the Lake]]

[[13 Treasures of Britain]] + [[Kythera Mechanism]]

[[Pnakotic Manuscript]] + [[Plague of Frogs]]

[[Roots of Yggdrasil]] + [[Sinkhole]] ([[Salt the Earth]], [[Asmodeus]], or [[Raze]]) Watch Me Pull It Off!

[[Kythera Mechanism]] + [[Chaoswish]] + [[Ring of Morrigan]]

[[Drums of Doom]] + [[Druid]]


ELEMENT RANKING

(E) Earth

(W) Water

(F) Fire

(A) Air


ARCHETYPES

MIDRANGE

Everything is some form of midrange. Your average curve will be something like:

2 spell that costs 1

5 spells that cost 2

6 spells that cost 3

5 spells that cost 4

3 spells that cost 5

3 spells that cost 6+

The hardest part is getting the one and two mana spells so be sure to prioritize those. Only prioritize 5 and 6 mana cards that are either great removal or legitimate game enders.


AGGRO

Aggro's in a much better place. I've found success with Fire Air decks with lots of Airborne minions. But be wary if you don't get enough 2 and 3 mana minions you'll end up with a sub-par midrange deck. [[Pathfinder]], [[Sorcerer]], [[Dragonlord]], [[Avatar of Air]] are my picks for this archetype.


CONTROL

By control I really mean a midrange deck with a higher than average curve or a deck that has a larger than normal suite of premium removal. Ideally both. I think [[Archimago]] has a real shot at being a competitive control Avatar if you amass 10+ good magics to control the game with. [[Sorcerer]] is also uniquely suited for a long game.


WATER CONTROL

Mono-Water has emerged as a powerful control option. Flooding abilities include [[Floodplain]], [[Atlantean Fate]], [[Great Old One]], but most powerful is [[Waveshaper]]. The ability to flood your opponents' sites is important for a few key cards, most importantly, [[Mariner's Curse]]. This has been extremely impressive as a repeatable removal spell. And you can force it to trigger using [[Coy Nixie]], [[Nelly Longarms]], and other forced movement options. The powerful game delaying control option in Water pair extremely well with the powerful and difficult to deal with minions such as [[Mester Stoor Worm]]. [[Shapeshift]] is very good in this deck, especially if you have ways to generate free Frog tokens. Most of your opponents' decks are midrange with 6+ expensive minions, making [[Waveshaper]]'s tap ability busted, especially if you can use forced movement to bring their threats together.


RAMP

You can watch me draft Earth ramp in this video or this video

You want 5+ sources of ramp and 5+ expensive cards to cast. This is the only deck that can use [[Black Obelisk]] effectively. I don't think this deck necessarily needs to be Earth but there are some sources of ramp in Earth that help a lot and some of the best things to ramp into are in Earth so it's pretty likely that's where you want to be. [[Geomancer]] is the preferred Avatar.


COMBO

you can watch me try to draft Combo in this video

There's not a ton of combos yet but some of the ones that exist are quite potent. The two combos that draw cards are what I think of when I think of a combo deck (see list of combos above). [[Seer]] is the best Avatar to assemble these. If you pick up one half of the 13 Treasures combo, other players are unlikely to draft the other half so you're pretty likely to get it assembled. Be wary drawing a bunch of cards will not automatically win you the game. You need to control the board at the same time to buy the time to use those cards.


CUBE DETAILS

Sites:

There are 3 sites in every pack. I broke singleton for 2 of each of the dual- and double-element sites. You will also find the tri-element castle sites, [[Colour out of Space]], and [[Valley of Delight]]. I still think the most powerful decks are the ones that stick to 2 elements with good threshold fixing. There are many triple and quadruple threshold cards that are very difficult to play if you're in 3 elements. There are 13 utility sites of each element. There are 10 colorless sites for extra utility if you can take the hit to your fixing as well as for players to assemble [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] + [[Sinkhole]]


AVATARS


[[Imposter]]: See House Rule at the top. [[Imposter]] has been super fun and powerful. This is one of my favorite additions from Gothic. Often you want to become [[Pathfinder]] on turn 4 and then turn into [[Sorcerer]] or something else later on to get additional value. Generically great in any deck, except maybe aggressive decks that can't afford to take a turn off.


[[Archimago]]: Very difficult to draft. You want 10+ powerful Magics. Hoping we get a more generically powerful control Avatar in a future set.


[[Avatar of Air]]: It's been somewhat underwhelming but is most suited for an aggressive deck with lots of Airborne minions. Likely you don't want to be just mono-Air.


[[Avatar of Earth]]: Testing


[[Battlemage]]: Hard to draft but when it comes together and you get some equipment on this guy he really performs.


[[Dragonlord]]: Flexible and powerful. [[Draco Corvus]] is borderline oppressive. [[Ignis Rex]] trivializes the death blow. [[Adtonitum]] is reasonable.


[[Druid]]: I considered cutting due to the nerf but I'm willing to keep it in for now to test. [[Drums of Doom]] + [[Druid]] is still a pretty effective combo even if it doesn't work on opponent's sites anymore.


[[Elementalist]]: S-Tier forever. Goodstuff.deck


[[Flamecaller]]: Mono-fire has been drafted plenty of times, this is a good option for that deck.


[[Geomancer]]: This is my pet avatar. Always better than [[Spellslinger]], mana acceleration is important in cube, it's busted with [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] + [[Sinkhole]].


[[Necromancer]]: Super powerful and generically great in any deck. On the short list of best Avatars in Cube. There are some combos with it, things that use your tokens well, [[Zombie Bruiser]], [[Shapeshift]], pump effects, etc. [[Gilman House]] is extremely powerful here since there is no limit to how many [[Horrible Hybrids]] you can get from your collection in Limited.


[[Pathfinder]]: See house rule at the top. This is a generically very powerful Avatar. Stick to 2 elements and avoid the tri-sites. Big mana decks are very good. But really every deck would love to draw a spell every single turn.


[[Savior]]: Has been underwhelming so far. It's hard to take a turn off in Cube when the curve can be a little unforgiving. But if you can manage to play off curve and stabilize you're going to snowball into a late win.


[[Seer]]: Specifically good for assembling combos but I think it's always better than [[Spellslinger]]. You'll get a lot of value out of drawing what you need when you need it.


[[Sorcerer]]: Has performed better with the lower curve since Gothic's release. Including some ramp spells seems strong so far. If you're up against a [[Sorcerer]] with 7+ mana you'd better be closing the game out fast. But Aggro decks with less mana can also take advantage of this powerful draw engine.


[[Waveshaper]]: A powerful control deck. See "Water Control" archetype above.


Minions:

The general advice I've heard is you want about 17 minions, 7 non-minions in your Spellbook. That's 70% minions. I applied this benchmark to the entire cube. Currently 65% of spells (non-site, non-avatar cards) are minions. There has been a wonderful infusion of 2-4 mana minions from Gothic which hopefully will shake things up and breed a faster format as a result.


Stats for nerds:

70 spells of each element

29 multicolor spells

15 sites of each element

20 multi-element sites

10 colorless sites

3.0 sites/pack

Average Mana Cost of Minions in Each Element:

Earth: 3.7

Fire: 3.6

Water: 3.9

Air: 3.7

Average Minion Cost: 3.75


NOTES TO SELF:

Combos currently cut:

[[Excalibur]]


CHANGE LOG:

6/4/2026: I mostly wanted to remove Harbinger since I've found it to be a trap for newer players (win rate of 22%), but made additional tweaks. I've felt for a while I wanted slightly more answers to threats if possible. I was able to bring in a few more removal spells and cut some junky minions. There were a few holdovers that were supporting the previously removed reanimation and evil archetypes. I decided to remove Gnarled Wendigo not because it's bad but because the deck that uses it most effectively, Necromancer, is already the most winning avatar and doesn't need the support. Island Leviathan was a hard cut but Mono Water is the highest winning elemental archetype and doesn't need the Leviathan. No one else can use it. And Stinging Kelp is good against Necromancer, especially since Necromancer decks tend to be water decks themselves. I've had the 1 power lethal minions for a while but they have failed to be an important answer to large beefy minions.

deckinfo.name: Bar Cube
deckinfo.primer:
Welcome to the Bar Cube 4-8 players. Players are dealt 3 packs of 17 with 12 spells and 5 sites.


The design goals for this cube are to be convenient to fire off and play, and to have few unplayable and overpowered cards (low power band).


288 spells/avatars and 120 sites intended to build draft decks with up to 24 spells and 12 sites.


This cube does not need extra game pieces like tokens, counters, modifications or collections. This cube can be played without a land station as there are plenty of sites to draft.

deckinfo.name: Relic Templar
deckinfo.primer:
The best option to start with this deck, is to have some of the exceptional Knights in your starting hand.


They march ahead and makes the way free for the harder units, waiting behind them, ready for the real battle.


Artifacts can be equipped, depending on the situation. It's all up to the moment!


If you manage to equip King Arthur with Escalibur, and the Amulet of Niniane, well..., you gonna give a hard time to your opponents.


Niniane can be also very useful for the Templar itself, especially on death's door.


You can use the Round Table and the Ruler of Thul as a nice combo to send units in the back of your opponents and still draw cards.



If you have the Archimago against you, I strongly recommend to input 3 Funeral Pyres in the Deck.


Good pull at the beginning of the game can be also a root Spider. Helps you to control the field in the early stages of the game.


Advanced Tips.


1. Let Sir Bedevere takes one of your fallen lances, so you can draw additional card every turn.


2. If you play against Sorcerer, you can equip your Queen of Midland with Niniane and draw a lot of cards until the opposite site finds a way to get her out of the game.


3. Save your Dame Britomart for a turn, where you can use your already placed Horn of Corleon, to have secure hit on a site. Than you can bring back some of your fallen knights on the battlefield for more benefits.


4. The Deck has been updated to Gothic. Now it plays like a Commander Deck from MTG, with a lot of single and strong unique Minions! More interactions and more madness on the board!

deckinfo.name: Here Comes the Bride
deckinfo.primer:
GOTHIC UPDATE (08/12/2025):


______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


Everything below this line is outdated but will remain for posterity.

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


The [[Elementalist]] update: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmayjtz1c00p9js045psulfgp


This deck got more and more greedy as time passed by that it became clear that a switch to Elementalist was probably the safe and smart decision. Other than a small flavor loss of no longer having a Knight as our avatar and abandoning the Wedding Hall plan (since we no longer have the cost reduction from the Templar, we cannot afford to have sites that do no provide mana) the deck's essence remains in tact. It is simply more consistent and arguably better with the Elementalist after all the changes that have been made.


The [[Wedding Hall]] Update:


Due to the shift of the deck to Elementalist, I absolutely wanted to maintain this deck with Templar because it is just so sweet and full of flavor. Sticking to this thought process, and because we now have the greedy version piloted by a new avatar, I wanted to refocus this deck towards the [[Wedding Hall]] combo and try to make that marriage happen. In case you wish to play the deck as it was before the Elementalist addition or the new laser focus on the Marriage Combo, I have listed all the cards that I have changed. Feel free to revert those changes and enjoy the primer below. Most of the primer still remains relevant to this new list however with our deeper focus on the Bride and Groom some cards it references may no longer be applicable. For example, all Water cards (except for [[Sir Mordred]] have been cut (also, I could not bring myself to cut [[ruler of thul]] since he is just too good in this deck and also our sites still allow for water splashing). I needed a deeper focus on Earth cards that can draw me sites so I could not justify as greedy a site base. Water took the hit because: 1) Earth has [[Land surveyor]] and [[kettletop leprechaun]] and [[tithe]] which also fuels [[knighthood]] and allows for the Village sites that generate 1 power tokens (perfect for the curve) and 2) Air and Fire present the strongest knights the game has to offer as well as the spells included.

(to be continued..)


[[SEE BELOW THIS LINE FOR PRIMER AS IT PERTAINS TO ORIGINAL LIST WITH TEMPLAR:]]

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


[[Wedding Hall]] is a cool card, there is no doubt and as much as we are secretly always trying to win that way, we need to be honest and realize that the likelihood is extremely low. Finding three specific Uniques and having them all live for a full turn cycle is extremely hard. The following breakdown keeps the proper beatdown plan as the main focus, but never forgets where it truly wants to live. Let me take you on a journey....


We are of course utilizing the [[Templar]] avatar ability to play over stat'd Minions faster and cheaper than our opponent in an attempt to dominate the Realm. Our collection of minions is primarily Knight, Sir and Dame based in order to effectively abuse the Templar's ability but we are not forced into only playing with these subtypes. You will notice that not all knights are being played and as much as it pained me to cut [[Sir Tristan]] he simply costs too much for his stats. After playtesting as much as I have with this deck, it is not only about good abilities, but mostly about the stats. The minions need to come down quick, be very hard to remove and in addition be good on their own. What inevitably occurs throughout the course of the games is that you end up in a 1 for 1 or sometimes 2 for 1 state as your opponent chops down your soldiers. This of course is bad, but the good news is that they often leave their mark before being dealt with. Because they usually do their thing, and then get killed, its crucial not to play cards whose text relies solely on other minions still being around. [[King's Council]] for instance will likely draw you 2 cards most of the time, but at any chance you get a third or more you are probably winning.


Every non-knight/sir/dame minion is the deck plays a vital role and after many changes and tweaks to the decks, the ones who remain have proved their worth. Their concepts are simple enough: If they cannot benefit from the Templar ability they must cantrip (with some exceptions). [[highland princess]] finds much needed mixes or a game ending [[Ring of Morrigan]]. [[Queen of Midland]] while seemingly over costed for her stats, has helped keep me in the game and is an absolute bomb of a minion. She is vital because you will definitely run low on cards playing everything you can each turn and she helps keep you in the game. [[Lady Iseult]] doesn't exactly cantrip but because she saves your minions and allows you to replay them, she fills a sort of virtual card advantage engine. They must kill her first, which is exactly what you want, so you can continue to beat face with your over stat'd minions. Here are the exceptions:


Exception 1: [[The lady of the lake]]

  • She can be replaced by a card that resummons from the graveyard but the fact that she allows you to pick the one you want and then gets reshuffled into the deck for future use is 100x more valuable. Recurring a [[Sir Pellinore]] is pure filth. She is still quite possibly the last minion on the chopping block but so far she deserves the slot. If a cut needed to absolutely be made, i would have to start by considering her though.


Exception 2: [[Vengeful Heir]]

  • similar to Lady of the lake, the recursion of your power houses puts immense pressure on the opponent to constantly have answers to high health minions that threaten to end the game.


Exception 3: [[Ruler of Thul]]

  • I like to jest that this is actually a Rule of Thul deck. At some point in the game, the gears shift from in your face pressure, to behind the scenes defense. Building your board in a safe way, staying back to protect your avatar loosens your opponents concerns and builds toward a surprise alpha strike. the fact that he both has charge and offers +1 power work hand in hand to crush your opponents soul in a moments notice. This guy brings the pain. [[Seven-League Boots]] is a cute addition to the deck but offers the same kind of "oopsies, gotcha" that we are aiming for with Thul. Not to mention what happens when you equip these things to [[Sir Balin]].


Opening Hand/Mulligan:

Its important to know what you are playing against to help determine what you should keep, what you should mulligan towards and how worried you should be if things do not go according to plan. For instance, keeping or mulligan'ing into a slow hand vs Fury Road likely means you're just dead. It is already a very difficult matchup but the fact that your minions are so heavily stat'd means you can put up a good fight against most of what they're doing. You just cant afford to be on the backdrop straight out of the gate.

  • Sites: Typically I mulligan sites a lot less than I do spells because for the most part your sites will take care of the thresh requirements in the first few turns and the diverse set of sites we are packing put in a lot of work towards this end. I will mostly mulligan sites of redundant threshold and duplicate sites as the diversity is more important. Other than this, try not to keep sites that don't provide mana early on, namely [[wedding hall]]. As much as we want to see this site at some point, we really (really) cant afford to be seeing it as one of your first 4-5 sites. [[Camelot]] is a powerhouse early game site, despite not providing threshold, especially if you can find [[Tournament Grounds]]. Putting Camelot at your starting location provides the highest chance of benefiting you without assisting your opponent as the card is symmetrical. [[Annual fair]] and [[Valley of delight]] are fixers which means they will round out what you are missing. You really don't want to playing these sites until you have established some amount of sites in the realm so you can round out the missing thresh. The best time to draw these sites is as site-draws #4-6.
  • Spells: This is pretty easy because we are an aggro/beatdown deck so really prioritize your Knights that cost 2-4. We can play them immediately and start the pressure right away. You should mulligan away all Magic in favor of Minions. Let the deck naturally draw you into your Magic to help clear space for already summoned minions or for ending the game post-pressure. An exception to this rule might be one of your [[King's Council]] but really only if the other two cards are both Uniques and can come out early and consecutively. You should feel good drawing 2 from your Council. I will generally always keep at least 1 Mix in my opening hand and when I do, will mulligan to a higher cost Dude to really terrify the opponent. Without a Mix, mulligan all high cost minions. Getting to 5 mana is rather easy with this deck so, its also not that crazy to keep a [[queen of midland]]. The card draw is just that important.


Notes:

  • The Mixes are 10,000% better than all cores in this deck. It is much better to be able to push out a 6 drop on turn 2 than it is to have the extra mana provided by the cores throughout the game especially since you will not need these tiny boosts as you get to 5-6 sites (which you will get to as you flesh out your thresh requirements)
  • [[The Round Table]] should be played in the same way that you play your minions/build you board: against water, prioritize land sites, against earth decks prioritize water sites. [[Earthquake]] is the bane of your existence. [[Feast for Crows]] will almost always name this card otherwise.
  • [[Grapple shot]], [[Leap Attack]] and [[Whirling blades]] are all extremely crucial parts of not only opening pathways to ensure you can safely attack with your big boys and girls but also provide the necessary conditions to end the game once you get your opponent to death's doors. I strongly recommend not playing around with these cards/quantities. Because of the difficulty this deck can experience ending the game, these all become much praised and prayed for cards throughout the game.
  • We have difficulty dealing with burrowed minions so [[Root Spider]] can become a problem (our forced movement cards will help with that specific card however). Build your board according to the implications of your opponents threshold.
  • [[Queen Guinevere]] is one of the top cards in the deck and provides a lot of surprise and potentially recurring damage. The minion she untaps can be anywhere in the realm which is especially powerful. She threatens to end the game quickly with the burst damage potential she provides. If unable to protect her, try to play her after you have 1-2 minions ready to attack already in the realm. She pairs especially well with [[Grapple Shot]].
  • Don't underestimate [[Sir Lancelot]]! With a [[grapple shot]] to the opponent avatars dome, he delivers a nice 13 damage swing. Not to mention an addition 4 if you also have [[queen Guinevere]] out. Fun times.


CONSIDERATIONS


Consideration #1 (08/04/2025): I have been wondering if [[Adept Illusionist]] truly deserves a spot here of if they're too slow/narrow. I am considering replacing them with another [[Blink]] or [[mad dash]] and possibly [[torshammar trinket]]. ~~see (17/04/2025) updates~~


Consideration #2 (18/05/2025): I might need to cut the Seven-League Boots. Which is sad times, but the explosive turns it can provide might not be worth the facts that a) usually your opponent ends up in possession of the boots after they kill your minion and b) they can be a dead draw as they are a conditional card ~~see (19/05/2025) update~~


UPDATES


Quick Update (28/03/2025): removed 1 Steppe for 1 Windmill. After playing a bit more, Air/Earth can be a bit taxing so I wanted an extra site that provided both.


Update #2 (02/04/2025): sad times have arrived but we must say Good night sweet princess to Lady of the Lake. After playing some more games, I am constantly reminded of how critical free movement is for this deck. The ideal card to me for this is [[Blink]] since it also draws you a card. My problem continues to be not being able to close the game once they're at death's door so this is why I'm not putting something like [[Fade]] or [[Vanishment]]. It is with heavy heart that Lady of the Lake gets the chop because she is not being chosen for being a bad card. In fact her ability is still heavily desired. If you have experienced [[Vengeful Heir]] then you know. She has been chosen because as a non knight minion, with 3 water threshold she simply holds the spot of "hardest requirement" to cast. I will be trying to find a way to get her back in. Until then, [[Blink]] joins the fight.


Update #3 (17/04/2025): I went ahead with consideration #1 above and swapped the Illusionists for the [[Trinket]] and a [[Mad Dash]] but I'm still wondering if [[Blink]] #2 is just better than Mad Dash.


Update #4 (28/04/2025): I have been craving Earth threshold lately. For this reason, 1 [[Mix Ignis]] is removed and replaced by 1x [[Mix Terra]]


Update #5 (05/05/2025): I have had too many games over the past three days of drawing that trinket and it doesn't do anything for me. Sadly it was the wrong inclusion. I have also been getting smoked by [[Blaze]] a lot so I decided to try it out as it is a perfect way to continue helping to solve the decks issue of closing the door. For this reason I have made the following changes -1 Trinket, -1 [[leap attack]], +2 [[Blaze]]


Update #6: (19/05/2025): [[Courtesan Thais]] replaces the [[seven-league boots]]. It occurred to me that this card provides a near guaranteed way to end the game when you get opponent to death's door. You are very likely to put the opponent to DD by attacking their avatar directly (or their avatar's site). Taking control of their next turn means you can just use their Avatar to attack into one of your dudes.

deckinfo.name: Relentless Knights
deckinfo.primer:
Deck Overview


***The main theme of the deck is high card draw and recursion from your cemetery to take advantage of the Templar discount and continuously deploy knights***


• Avatar: Templar (reduces the cost of your first Knight/Sir/Dame each turn by 1 — the core engine that makes your 3- and 4-drops play like 2- and 3-drops, enabling explosive early and mid-game curves).

• Playstyle: Wide knight swarm focused on cheap, efficient threats. Establish a board fast with low-cost knights, use card draw to fuel ongoing pressure, recur fallen knights for value, and close with amplified attacks via artifacts and positioning.

• Mana Base: Streamlined multi-color with minimized Water for easier threshold fixing (strong Earth/Fire focus with light Air splash). 30 sites prioritize knight-friendly locations like Tournament Grounds, Camelot, Avalon, and basic mana producers.

• Key Synergies: Cheap knights cluster for buffs; cheap artifacts that help you ramp. Artifacts like Round Table; card draw engines keep the gas flowing; cemetery recursion (via spells or effects like certain Arthurian pieces) brings back threats to maintain board presence without slowing down. 

Strengths: Overwhelming early-to-mid board pressure, high resilience through recursion and draw, deceptive mana curve thanks to Templar, strong into longer games via value engines.

Weaknesses: Needs a solid early knight drop; can struggle if completely shut out of the board before recursion kicks in. This deck will struggle with control decks.


Mulligan Strategy (Absolutely Critical)

Mulligan is the difference between a smooth knight flood and a clunky game.

• Always mull high-cost minions (5-6 mana) — they clog your early curve.

• Mull combat-enhancing magics to dig for artifacts, card draw, and recursion pieces.

• Keep hands with at least one low-cost knight + good mana fixing.

• Aim for a perfect spellbook mana curve (1-mana play on turn 1, 2-mana on turn 2, etc.) to maximize Templar’s discount.

• Mull sites aggressively for threshold redundancy or if your opening thresholds don’t cover your hand. Prioritize hands that support early cheap knight drops and draw engines. 

This build turns Templar’s discount into a relentless engine: cheap knights on curve, constant draw to refill, and cemetery recursion to keep coming back stronger.

deckinfo.name: Tempo Wave Lockdown
deckinfo.primer:
Core Strategy

  • Early Game (Turn 1-4): Focus on setting up Pirate Ship and Anui Undine
  • Mid-Game (Turn 4-5.5): Expand your board presence with synergistic plays, leveraging control cards like Riptide, Pollimorph, and Drown to maintain dominance. While SPAMMING Waveshaper ability to keep your control, most games, your wont play 6 sights, but you can if the board is completely controlled.
  • Late Game: Push for Deaths Door using combo plays with Selfsame Simulacrum, to overwhelm opponent with ships and Anui, You will be surprised how fast you can get people to deaths door.

Key Cards

Water Core Cards


  1. Pirate Ship: A critical card for early aggression; thrives with Floodplains and Waveshaper.
  2. Anui Undine: Game-changing aquatic minion; combine with Flood effects for massive damage.
  3. Selfsame Simulacrum: Copy your Ships or Anui to overwhelm.


Timeline of Updates

5/16/2024:

  • Replaced Sea Raiders with Sea Salt Anchormen for utility in disruption-heavy matchups.
  • Refined focus on Pirate Ship and Selfsame Simulacrum for consistent tempo.

6/13/2024:

  • Added Polar Explorers for defensive and burst-damage capabilities.
  • Streamlined the deck by removing Captain Baldassare and an additional Sea Salt Anchorman.

7/16/2024:

  • Added Mariner’s Curse to protect units and create synergy with Riptide for control.
  • Consolidated flood mechanics by replacing a Flood with Atlantean Fate.

9/18/2024 (50/30 Deck):

  • Added Common Sense (4 copies) for card search and flexibility.
  • Introduced Bosk Trolls and Belmotte Longbowmen to counter aggro.
  • Transitioned toward Earth-focused spells for additional board presence and utility.

10/5/2024:

  • Integrated stealth mechanics with Swindler Troupe to enhance Pirate Ship/Anui Undine damage output.
  • Added Guisarme + Ludbog Cat Combo for surprise burst damage (8+).

Strengths

  • Excels in mid-game tempo (4-6 mana), dominating the board with low-cost, high-value minions.
  • Adaptable to various metas through Water, Air, or Fire splashes.
  • Punishes core-heavy or mana-dependent decks with Stormy Seas and Waveshaper's ability.

Weaknesses

  • Vulnerable to disruptive cards like Infiltrate, Lethal, or heavy removal.
  • Aggro-heavy decks can overwhelm early game defenses without proper draws. Look for Troll Bridges, and smaller Minions such as Bosk Troll, Shellycoat, and Ludbog Cats to mitigate aggro burst


11/22/2024: Air or Fire Splashing (Currently Testing)

  • Currently Working of other Splash variants Water/Air and Water/Fire threshold variants for meta adaptability:
  • Water/Air: Emphasizes, card draw and mobility with Fade, Sir Pelleas, and Blink, Lightning Bolt - Grapple Shot
  • Water/Fire: Focuses on aggressive damage/ and Counter Midrange late game decks with Infiltrate and Sir Gaheris, Black Knights, Kobolds ETC
  • Water: Currently testing Helpful Hob, Geyser, Sea Serpent, and Green Knight in my base deck. Lastly, testing Grim Guisarme, thinking it will work really well with Ludbog Cat to swing at their avatar turn 3 or 4, or to buff ships.


3/12/2024: Won Local Tournament Using Air Instead of Earth

  • I took out Kettletop, Common Senses, and replaced them with Blinks and Sir Pelleas, and added some Deep-Sea Mermaids. Having Blink really adds a flex to your units and having that really made the Cats feel a lot more powerful, I also added a few Sea Serpents which did feel really well but im unsure if I want to keep them in the main deck. Having Sir Pelleas, feels op if your opponent also has water. Still play testing, and creating a more Aggro version called "Messmer".




TIPS:


Mariners Curse - You can play on top of your minions on opponents sites to protect them while hammering down with damage


Silence - Utility can use on your own ships to attack earth sites or disrupt enemy plays


Old Salt Anchorman - Prevents forced movements, BURYS and SUBMERGES are also forced movements so it adds a layer of proection, also protects against pudge, riptides ETC


Waveshaper Ability - USE THIS ABILITY, it can hit sites NEAR your body of water, and you can really F up your opponent if played correctly. By the time you have 5 sights you should be spamming this and not placing more sites. Unless you have full control in most cases.


Starting hand: Try to go for at least one lighthouse and Floodplain to help cast your spells and create a larger body of water. If you have your sites, Put any Blink/Riptide on the bottom of your deck you can fetch it later with a deep sea mermaid or a Kelp forest.


07/29/2025

Due to the recent rule changes I put in 2 Grim Guisarmes, now that they can do double damage to sites, it’s worth putting as you can lock down opponents minions with waveshapwe ability and hit extra hard with pirate ship, Anui etc

added some gothic cards and Toolbox, which is very important. Only thing in testing right now is Drowned, as it can be a good counter against direct aggro from interrogators. Also overflow, may be a good option as with Waveshaper, we can ramp and control

deckinfo.name: IDK (H2O shifty) street legal v3.0
deckinfo.primer:
IDK (H₂O Shifty) Street Legal v2.0

“We love water & movement.”



Deck Concept

This deck began as an Elementalist hybrid leaning toward Water, but it has evolved into a pure Water control-tempo build — with just a splash of Air. The idea is simple: use Water’s ability to reshape the map, submerge, and disable, while Air gives you just enough burst to keep opponents guessing.

You’re playing fluid tempo control — not full stall, not aggro, but that beautiful middle ground where your opponent always feels a half-step behind.

Mana cap sits at 6, which gives room for big bodies that can double dip with Grapple Shot or Helpful Hob for extra attacks.



Game Plan


Opening

Mulligan for at least one Air site (to support your spell suite), but otherwise lean heavily Water.

Your ideal opener:

  • Pond, Tower, Pirate Ship, Lugbog Cat, and ideally a Grapple Shot.


Classic curve:

  • Turn 2: Lugbog Cat (with Pond)
  • Turn 3: Pirate Ship (with Tower)
  • Turn 4: Flood an enemy site and swing with Ship
  • Turn 5: Flood their back site (disabling your Ship on Land), then Grapple into their Avatar for a direct strike.
  • If they already have Water sites, even better — the current is already flowing your way.


Core Tools


Hard Removal

  • Atlantean Fate, Iron Shackles, Drown, Stormy Seas


Card Draw & Cycling

  • Seelie Court, Blink, Riptide


Stalling & Tempo Tools

  • Tufted Turtles, Plague of Frogs, Adept Illusionist


Big Bodies for Grapple Combos

  • Pirate Ship, Questing Beast, Daperyll Vampire — boosted further by Lord of Unland



Play Patterns

  • Early: Establish control with Pond, Babbling Brook, and Floodplain sites while dropping small, resilient minions (Lugbog, Shellycoat, Turtles).
  • Midgame: Build tempo through Blink, Riptide, and Grapple — pivoting minions into key attacks or repositioning threats with Maelström.
  • Late: Transition into large, sticky finishers (The Green Knight, Daperyll Vampire, Lord of Unland, Ruler of Thul).



Evolution Notes


This deck has evolved through a ton of tuning — often in response to the shifting meta and the wisdom of fellow Sorcery players:

  • Removed Swindlers for Coy Nixie and Ribble to reduce mortals (due to Bower of Bliss and King of the Realm).
  • Added Poachers per Buamie’s suggestion — useful for peeking and sniping threats, though risky if it thins their deck favorably.
  • Brobdingnag Bullfrog now serves as the primary disable tool, giving a body plus lockdown. Previously tested Sleep and Shackles could return.
  • Shameless Squire offers artifact retrieval — great when paired with Disenchant or Atlantean Fate.
  • Best combo: Mester Stoor Worm + Riptide + Hob for double attacks, especially after flooding a site to access the opponent’s back line. Trinkets amplify this combo when available.
  • Trinkets / Ring of Morrigan once offered strong boosts but were cut for a leaner, submerge-focused build.
  • Card Draw Core: Tadpole Pool, Frogs, Manuscript — flexible enough for discard synergy or Turtle backup.
  • Site & Minion Core: heavy Water build now includes Tufted Turtles, Shellycoat, Tide Naiads, and fewer land-locked pieces. Naiads help conserve Waveshaper taps for midgame plays.
  • Caution: Babbling Brook can disable your own minions’ great abilities.
  • Mana curve: Leans toward 3–4 mana plays. Use early disables to survive, then deploy consistent threats each turn. 4 mana is the sweet spot — it enables both Waveshaper’s ability and flexible reactions.



Post–Gen Con Tuning (Aug 2025)

  • Removed: Hobs → Added: Grim Guisarme (enables 6-mana Grim + Grapple plays)
  • Reintroduced: Daperyll Vampires for life gain (Angel Eggs cut)
  • Swapped: Shameless Squire → Attack by Night → back to Squires (artifact pickup utility > burst)
  • Trimmed: Frogs → briefly replaced by Maelström for reposition testing, then re-added for reliable stalling
  • Removed: Lord of Unland and Trinkets → doubled down on submerge synergy
  • Removed: Unland Eels (dead draws) → replaced with Shellycoat, Tufted Turtles, Tide Naiads
  • Added: Drown, Stormy Seas for flexible artifact removal + submerge synergy
  • Latest advice from Sun God: reinforce card draw, early stalling, and hard removal for consistency while maintaining 6-mana ceiling
  • Removed: Manuscript to make room for Swap



Final Thoughts


“H₂O Shifty” thrives when you play like water — flow around obstacles, absorb pressure, and strike when the current turns. The best games feel less like combat and more like choreography — your minions glide, flood, and vanish, only to reappear for the finishing blow.


“The tide doesn’t turn in your favor — you become the tide.”

3/1/26
