Welcome to this deck that is so much fun and pretty violent. It takes its inspiration from the well known Furious Witch's road deck ( https://curiosa.io/decks/cmah6ebes002ll704cycrhe8o ) but I prefer dipping into Air instead of earth,it just fits my playstyle better and I love the keys we get with air as aggro deck to bypass a lot of the problems we usually face (fortress sites for instance) so here we go :


Deck goal : Putting enemy down to death door as fast as possible (no surprise here) by using our aggro stuff with the witch's drain (2 life loss/turn)

Deck strategy : As you see, we don't really need more than 4 sites in most games, so most of the time you'll draw a site only once during the game. The deck is almost mono fire, and the few air cards just need 1 air tresholds, so you won't have any treshold problem with the deck. The air part of the deck is mostly to get acces to the awesome air sites Gothic gave us to bypass fortress sites, they will be discussed next.

So basically, draw spell everytime, draw site once, get to 4 site, then use the witch drain (2 life) each turn to put opponent to death door , once he is at death door, and cannot loose life anymore use the witch tap ability to tax him (+1 mana cost of his spells) untill finisher. (wich ..will comme fast as almost your whole deck is filled with finishers)


Specific cards discussion :

Sites :


Field of Phixis : This site alone justify air. Silencing opponent's sites allow your minions to go through to deal damage and totally shut down fortress strategies, no more perilous bridge, gnome hollow , pebble paths limitations, this site is so amazing. If you draw one at start of game, keep it.

River of blood : Kinda obvious, it's an aggro deck you don't want your opponent to get life back as you heavily spend your ressources to lower his life's total

Spore Spouts : the deck has 17 2 power minions, and the site allows you to summon your 2 or less power minions anywhere in the realm. The strategic advantage of this site is awesome, you can cast Sinterfee anywhere to silence/remove treshold of the opponent's most important sites, you can cast Hotwheel from anywhere, you can cast vile imp turn 2 and deal 2 damage to opponent's face directly or summon Kobold next to his avatar to strike it (as kobold is a 2 power minion).

Vindictive Nation : This site is the protection we needed badly, an atlantean fate, year of the blaze and such would put us in a place we could hardly recover from, but now, if you have vindictive nation, well, doing so would be almost a suicide mission for the opponent.

Wuthering heights : Another amazing air site, giving you avatar of air's power on a site, help your throw your minions to the opponent's sites (for instance corruptor freak the turn it's summoned) or throw back enemy's minions to their side, using enemy's sites at your advantage (for instance if opponent has a Thin ice/bottomless pit nearby your Wuthering heights you could use the free minion's moove from Wuthering heights to your advantage this way to send back their minion there).

Deserts : great removals, even if Tawny is not around anymore, with the necro skellies, and the wards we now see, and the fact it's ordinary , deserts still stands as an awesome site.

Poisonned well : Free life loss, make opponent go to death's door faster.

Ruins : Treshold fixing.

Molten Maar : Card advantage, 3/3 minions for three mana cost, without using a card as its from your collection, it's great !

Ordinary Towers : mana accelerator,so cast saracen raiders, lion turn 3, can also be used as 4th site to reach 5 mana for Betrayal if you happen to have that in hand without having to draw a 5th site.

Dread Thicket : Another great site to have in the front row as it allows you to deliver damage with your charge minions even if opponent is playing token army or heavy stuff.


Minions :


Hemogoblins : As with river of blood, preventing your opponent to get life back is so important, hemogoblin does this on a 2 power body. Usually played at the end of turn, drain with witch, deal damage with minion on board or magic and then play hemogoblin to set new life maximums.

Sinterfee : Absolutly amazing minions, the power of disruption this has is incredible, its a 2/2 for 2 also. Totally shut down fortress sites to allow your other minions to pass, remove treshold from water sites so deactivate mariner's curse power, auto kill any minion that is submerged (porcupine 1/1 lethal minion for instance) and also, as it remove the treshold while alive, it slows opponent's strategy, and slowing the opponent even by one turn can be so deadly with this deck (as it's one more turn of 2 life drain and 3 average minion damage).

Vile imp : a total staple, so versatile, deal damage to remove an annoying minion or use Spore Spouts or summoning sphere/jihad to summon next to enemy avatar and deal the 2 dmg directly to its face

War horse : charge minion with added carry unit bonus if required

Barging bargheist : Awesome new card, doesnt have charge, but as it is summoned in the void it's hard for the opponent to remove it at first, and with the movement +1 it's easy to make sure you can attack an undefended site the following turn. Also with Blaze it's a total blast (4 steps total)

Colicky dragonette : Remove wards, skellies, on a 3/3 minions, can be a finisher, just a value good card

Corruptor freak : this will draw your opponent's removal as it cannot let it live. If you have wuthering heights or sphere/jihad it will be in opponent territory from the turn its summoned so will deal the 2 dmg directly, otherwise if this manage to live it is 5 damage per turn, so awesome, but of course the psychological effect of the 2 site damage in addition to the 3 power makes opponent heavily try to remove it :D.

Morgana Le fay : Not gonna insult you by trying to justify her.

Mazuj Ifrit : Awesome aggro minion, 4 power airborne (the downside is more thank ok) on turn 3, can go diagonal with airborne, curve advantage

Quarrelsome Kobold : auto strike is great, can be summon anywhere with Spore spouts to make sure they deal dmg to avatar"s face upon summoning or remove annoying minions, but work great with summoning sphere and jihad too of course, and awesome trinket target.

Recap powries : Hot charge minions.

Saracen raiders : hot charge minions.

Monstrous lion : Not the biggest fan to be honest as it can't attack a site, but it's great minion removal and as we have 2 summoning spheres + jihad + wuthering heights we have way to get it close to enemy avatar to give it more chance to strike it. Excellent target gor warp spasm and blaze of glory

Hotwheel : the 4 mana cost is annoying not gonna lie, but it's a finisher, it remove wards, it remove skellies and other tokens, it passes through gnome hollow, its auto strikes, it's blaze on a minion stick and versatile so it totally deserves its spot.

Wild fanatics : 2/2 charge minions that can be cast with spore spout anywhere in the ream


Magic :


Firebolts : remove skellies, remove ward efficiently (using just one of the 3 pings), finisher etc, just a great simple 2 mana cost magic

Lightning bolt : the randomness is annoying, and i generally prefer firebolts but with Gothic we more and more see very dangerous 3 power minions with huge advantage (Lilith, Maidern mother and Crone) and beeing able to just one shot this kind of powerhouse that stay in opponent's back row is too good

Blaze : if you have never played blaze, play it and you'll see. bonus movement so your minions can go strike wherever you like, cant be intercepted + damage on departed locations including removing token, wards etc, it kills stuff, it was used as finisher in more games than I can count.

Blaze of glory : uber cheated Gothic card, can easily remove 1 or 2 enemy minions while dealing damage to enemy avatar and clearing the way for a strike afterward, all for 3 mana

Minor explosion : different kind of 3 dmg magic, can remove several stuff, great finisher , jsut good (trying to just play with one in collection for a bit).

Warp spasm : I know at first glance you think loosing the minion at the end of turn sucks but this violent magic allow you do double your power (so let say your 3 power minion become 6 power), you can easily remove an enemy minion up to 5 power, then untap and deal 6 damage to a site (which i remind your with witch 2 life drain its 8 dmg in a turn) so the trade off of loosing a minion for a big minion removal + 6 ish damage, yeah it's good ! (and also can remove several tokens if needed with this).

Infiltrate : super tempo card, gain control of a defending minion to allow your to strike, then use the control minion to deal more damage or remove another one etc, the degree of control and impact this offer is awesome, only downside beeing, you have to wait a turn to use the controlled minion, but it still allows your minion to pass and strike as you just took over an annoying defender. also stealth minions are good finisher so you can take control of an enemy minion to use it to finish opponent that is at death's door.

Betrayal : Only 5 cost in the deck but direct impact, control a huge enemy minion to deal big damage, to attack another enemy minion and potentially remove 2 minions one shot, control defender to deal death blow etc etc, huge control/damage potential (in trial for now I'll update once tried enough to see if its a keep or remove card).


Artifacts :


Trinkets : just a good reusable +1 power , more damage, helps minion removal

Toolbox : Get easy finisher or specific answer like angry mob, blink etc.

Silver bullet : get drought. haha, amost not kidding, water is imo becoming super strong and beeing able to put that aura on their water site totally destroy them, a very good tool to have in hand , or get searing truth / hotwheel / trinket for finishers, or other situations where they are needed.


Auras :


Jihad / Summoning spheres : allow you to summon your stuff where you want, if you have one, opponent is gonna cry and try to remove it (and amazing against fortress decks of course).

Great famine : great removal, kills root spiders or anything if well placed, or as our minions may be less powerful than opponents, it keeps Famine on the realm killing opponent minions first.


Starting hand and Mulligan :


I'd say an ideal starting hand would look like this (not gonna include uniques) :

Sites : Blood river, vindictive nation and Field of phyxis (you have all the utility you need) - never keep more than 1 air site in starting hand (well, ruins doesnt count), remember your need only 1 air treshold and some cards need 3 fire so you're aiming for 3 F 1 A (all sites have tresholds in the list) ideally having 1 field of phyxis or 1 dread thicket or 1 sinterfee in starting hand really helps getting damage through , so try to hit that.

spells : if you draw betrayal in starting hand, mulligan it, rest is pretty dope, of course, try to have at least 2 minions if you can as you need to start dealing damage (a 2 cost and a 3 cost is cool). Also if you happen to have a spore spouts (site), pay attention to your minions powers, as it means you'd be able to summon 2 power minion anywhere.


Hope you will enjoy that deck as much as I do :) and a big thank to @Childe Roland for his Witch inspiration, never forget he revealed the power of the Witch to the world ! :D

Marco

deckinfo.name: Feast & Famine (Witch Tempo)
deckinfo.primer:
Disrupt and outvalue your opponent with curses! This deck aims to use the [[Witch]]'s tap ability as much as possible and as quickly as possible. Draining our opponent for 2 life per turn wonderfully supplements a fairly aggressive strategy. Generally, this deck works in three ways:


Hand Attack: One of the core packages of this list is looking at and interfering with your opponents' hand. In addition to removing cards from their hand directly, the knowledge of what they hold also gives you a distinct advantage and informs your plays.

  1. [[Pith Imp]]: A random but cheap hand attack, which can throw off your opponents' early game and open a window for your pressure to snowball into the midgame.
  2. [[Feast for Crows]]: Target cards specific to your opponent's strategy in their deck and hand.
  3. [[Swiven Scout]], [[Lookout]]: Play around your opponents' next moves and further enable Feast.


Disruption: A low mana curve that tops off at 4 allows for the inclusion of notable threats, all while lowering the number of sites needed for the deck to function. This means you can start using your [[Witch]]'s ability earlier to further interfere with your opponent's game plan by taxing their hand, shrinking their avatar, or, in most cases, steadily draining their life total while advancing your board strategy.

  1. [[The Great Famine]]: Pick off larger, harder-to-tackle threats while your typically-smaller minions push through.
  2. [[Sturmgeist]]: An incredible tempo minion, capable of taking steps and striking units on your opponent's turn in addition to your own. All but disables nearby spellcasters with less than 4 power.
  3. [[Sir Lamorak]]: Functions as an effective dissuasion from being too aggressive towards us, as he likely wipes out all nearby enemies on death. Notably, his ability can also kill an opponent on death's door with proper positioning.
  4. [[Gift of the Serpent]]: An all-star of a cantrip, this card gives another burst of value to any of our 1-power genesis minions, ([[Highland Falconer]], [[Highland Princess]], [[Apprentice Wizard]]) turning them into deadly removal pieces.
  5. [[Infiltrate]]: Outright steal our opponents' largest threat, simultaneously protecting ourselves while giving us an unblockable threat of our own. Only lasts for one hit, but that can be all that's needed.


Push: The aggro side of the deck, prioritizing fast damage that can slip through defences and occupy our opponent. As long as they are pressured to focus on our minion threats, our witch can continue to drain their life down.

  1. [[Summoning Sphere]], [[Spore Spouts]]: Playing directly to your opponents' back row is a strategy that this deck loves, as pushing our early threats as far from our side of the board as possible pressures our opponent to focus their attention there, buying us valuable time to set up our witch.
  2. [[Sphere of animosity]]: The main use for this sphere is ensuring that our attacks cannot be defended, pushing damage through no matter what. Additionally, a single sphere of animosity can completely break a [[Pathfinder]] deck, and it and our [[River of Blood]]s ensure lifegain will not work against us.
  3. [[Corruptor Freak]]: Likely the best option to follow a summoning sphere with, our corruptor freaks allow us to compound our witch's ability to drain our opponent for 2 life per turn consistently.
  4. [[Morgana le Fay]]: It's Morgana le Fay
  5. [[Redcap Powries]]: Fast burst damage that encourages us to play aggressively.
  6. [[Boudicca]]: Playing Boudicca at the right time can allow for a handful of smaller minions to burst your opponent down to death's door in a single turn.
  7. [[Shackled Demon]]: Often, skipping a turn of cursing our opponent to free a shackled demon is worth it, as a 5 power threat overpowers most other units. It's also likely that another spellcaster will be in play to free it, with the inclusions of [[Apprentice Wizard]]s and Morgana.
  8. [[Blaze]], [[Wuthering Heights]]: Movement abilities like this allow us to push our threats to the far side of the board, which is especially useful for our Corruptor Freaks. In a pinch, most of these also work to get our witch out of tricky situations.
  9. [[Searing Truth]]: The typical finisher of the deck, Searing Truth either allows us to draw two cards at the cost of- typically, 3 life, or it works as direct damage to finish off our opponent from anywhere on the board, with no way to counter it.

deckinfo.name: Dank Faeries
deckinfo.primer:
Theme

The theme of the Dank Faeries deck is tempo + max annoyance really. Control the speed of play, get out some heavy hitters, use things like stealth and tapping to your advantage.


Strengths

Great faerie and beast synergy, not too stretched on artifacts, magic and aura and really focused on minions and their boosting abilities ie; use your [[Shellycoat]] as blockers, making that a little bit harder for your opponent. Throw out [[Sugarplum Pixies]] and [[Tooth Faeries]] to impact the board state by tapping minions to suit your play.


Weaknesses

High power isn't the focus, and using things like [[Torshammar Trinket]], [[Fourberie Knot]] and [[The Faerie Queen]] can be essential in the late game to ensure your valuable minions aren't just chump blockers.


Strategy

Plan A:

  1. Play only (4) sites, ideally 2 (W) and 2 (A) threshold minimum
  2. Use the [[Witch]] to direct burn for 2 each turn from then
  3. Throw minions out each turn, ensuring you pay attention to start and end turn benefits from the likes of [[Aino]], [[Questing Beast]] (who you'll need a 5th site for if you play it)
  4. Spread out and control the field - [[Winter Nymph]] is a really strong card here, early game, maintain stealth and get it to the other side of the board.
  5. Use combinations of cards in the final stages, particular when your opponent is on DD, that can get you the win; [[Polar Explorers]], [[Ruler of Thuul]], [[Aino]], [[Stagecoach]], [[Sturmgeist]]

Plan B:

  1. If the opponents' deck is more defensive or more magic focused, look to make that a bit more challenging with minions like [[Sturmgeist]] or [[Tufted Turtles]] and ideal when you can give them movement that comes through the back row.
  2. Protect boosters where possible, like [[Faerie Queen]].
  3. Use [[Vanishment]] or [[Fade]] to prevent targeting
  4. Always save a magic for the wincon if your minions aren't making as much progress, such as a [[Toolbox]] into [[Lightning Bolt]] or one in hand

deckinfo.name: HEXE - Aggressive Cursing
deckinfo.primer:
An aggressive Witch variant with focus on artifacts and consistency. The low curve and threshold requirement allow her to start pinging damage starting turn 5 consistently. Artifacts replace popular last hit spells as most require positioning of a caster and this Witch hates moving.


  • In the first 4 turns you'll build out 2x2 sites with preferably either Free City, Troll Bridge, Dome of Osiris, or Great Wall directly bordering your opponent.
  • Mulligan sites carefully, if both Water and Fire threshold are achieved in the opening hand, its often better to keep it!
  • Bigger enemy threads are disabled with Iron Shackles and Sleep.
  • Last hit options include Rolling Boulder, Blaze, Rhongomyniad and Ruler of Thul.
  • Poison Nova is a board clear option if you should get overwhelmed too quickly e.g. Knight decks.

deckinfo.name: Faeries Tempo
deckinfo.primer:
Theme


This is a deck of distant legends and mysticism. The theme of the deck is clearly focused on Faeries, drawing heavily from the roots of the old Fish archetype in Magic: The Gathering. It’s a tempo-control deck: you annoy your opponents, deal small but consistent damage, and generate card advantage.


Strengths


  • Very good late game
  • Good card advantage and quality through toolboxes and Sylvan Splendor
  • High flexibility, you can switch to fast aggro o full control depending the draws
  • Quite good against slower control
  • Fast opponent's life burn once setted up
  • Very strong sites
  • Very strong card removal / control


Weaknesses


  • Low power minions, but some of them really impactful
  • Can be vulnerable to explosive early aggression
  • Witch can be tricky in this one
  • Misplays are heavily punished, often time you're gonna lose after 2 mistakes
  • Some combination of initial card draw can be punishing
  • Depends heavily on sites


Strategy


The deck kept me busy for quite a long time before I found the right build, and even longer before I learned how to use it properly. The main strategy, as I mentioned above, is to annoy the opponent, buy time early on through lands and control spells, and then burn down the opponent’s life total in a very short time.


  1. Play only 6 sites, you don't need more. Try to be defensive, you need time.
  2. Mulligan allways not impactful sites: you need to defend the Witch. You allways need one of these site: Bottomless Pit, Mountain Pass, Troll Bridge, Wuthering Weights. These help to keep enemy minions away.
  3. Try to keep sites on the first row as long as possible, unless they're control sites. Don't spread too much, you need to use your Sylvan Splendor and minion/sites abilities.
  4. Defend and kill everything the first turns. Then, when you're ready and the battlefield is stable, burn enemy life with Witch, minions in enemy sites with Spore Spouts or Summoning Spheres.
  5. If the enemy is slower than you, and he has fewer sites, play the other ability of the Witch "pay 1 more". You're gonna tempo him fast enough.
  6. If the enemy is an aggressive avatar like Battlemage, and he's chasing you, keep him at bay with the last Witch ability, -3 power: he will be turned off.
  7. Use your magic to control the battlefield: Plague of Frogs to protect you Witch from aggro, Chaos Twister, Pollimorph to remove big threats, and the others to remove small threats.


Nice combos:


  • Lookout + Hyter Sprites: lock and tempo your opponent for 1 turn, sometimes can really save you time.
  • Sling pixies + Poisonous dagger: great ranged removal, very obnoxious.
  • Wuthering Weigths or Abbadon Succubus + Bottomless Pit or Troll Bridge, or multiple combinations of those: just have fun, while the opponent doesn't. XD
  • Sir Tom Thumb + Sylvan Splendor: a good blocking creature, and each time it dies you can play it again within Sylvan Splendor, generating card advantage.
  • Fey Changeling + Sylvan Splendor: if i understood it right, you can draw 1 card every 3 mana, targeting Fey Changeling's ability on itself.
  • Any Faerie + Fae City: can really be annoying, but not so easy to get it right.

deckinfo.name: Deathspeaker Self Mill (cornerstone deck)
deckinfo.primer:
Yo! Welcome to the primer for my DS Self Mill Deck!

To start things off a quick history on me a tcgs and why im choosing this deck as my main passion project for the Sorcery tcg.


Basically for as long as ive been playing tcgs (started with Invasion block for mtg) ive loved using the graveyard as a resource. So naturally in mtg I was the reanimator guy and when I got a good collection I competed in legacy format events using a deck called Tin Fins and Dredge as a back up. I loved every minute of it too until mtg started doing things I heavily disagreed with and I dropped the game about 7ish years ago. When Sorcery was announced on KS it immediately gave me those mtg vibes I loved as a kid so I backed it. When I got my product I saw DS and knew this was the avatar for me and ive been working on making this deck as fun as I can so here we are haha.


So for the start behind this self mill deck is ever growing as I play more games against various avatars and opposing strats. The idea is pretty simple though, mill yourself to get that advantage asap. The advantage here is tons of card draw with those wizards and lots of minion generation with the necromancers. I also run a solid ordinary package that answers various problematic cards that exist in the game. The way I look at avatars is that each one offers the player a "cheat code" to help them win paired with piloting the deck correctly. DS "cheat code" is obviously using the graveyard as a second hand. When all this self mill stuff got printed in gothic my face lit right up and I felt at home haha. Something ive learned though is to not fill that yard up too fast, especially if the opponent is on fire, the bigger a yard you have the juicier a target it can become. Try to keep it minimal until you need new targets and go from there. In my maybe board I have a short stack of cards im considering and site hate is something ive added to it thanks to that unique fire site that kills my deck lol. Youll also notice I dont run ring, p stone, cores or other obvious "staple competitive cards" and I do that for a reason. I dont find those cards fun at all to play and im all about having fun here. If you want to run those no shame on you and feel free to edit the deck as you see fit to run the cards you want to run. Im choosing to run the token generating stuff to offer me good chump blockers or easy ping damage to opposing sites. Tokens in general are just annoying so it felt right to me and so far its been fun. Hotwheel has also been an all star for me. Killing random dudes or even putting in that finishing blow has been great. 3 might be overkill but I like running max copies of stuff when I can. I will say the mvp of the deck though is Skeleton Mage. I. Love. That. Card! Its so so good at everything this deck wants to do and casting Common Sense a million times in a game just feels criminal lol. But really it helps me always have an answer to my opponent with all the 1 of ordinary cards I run to be fetched with Common Sense. I also run some pet cards that happen to be very strong like good ol pudgy but besides that I tried making the deck with cards that function in my hand and graveyard to really abuse that "cheat code" I mentioned.


Hopefully this probably poorly written primer helps you all make your own sick DS decks and show my passion for the deck! So go out there and resurrect the realm in a fashion that fits you best!

deckinfo.name: 4th place CORNERSTONE SAO PAULO/BRAZIL 2025 - Maquinas Agricolas  🪨🔥🚜
Avatar of Air - 1st Place Cornerstone Championship
deckinfo.primer:
This is a Gothic mid-range Air/Earth deck with Avatar of Air for mobility. It's not too different from the typical air/earth mid range gameplay that encourages an aggressive early-mid game with late-game finishers. With the changes to Guisarm and other "Strike" effects, you're not going for the OTK and instead looking to constantly apply pressure.


---------- Artfiacts:

Onyx Core is to help ramp and fix Earth Threshold. Torshammer Trinkets are to help deal more damage and make trades more favorable. Toolbox is to provide answers when you need them but more often than not it is to pull Zap! out from the collection to kill your opponent at Death's Door. You could argue running a 3 of to add consistency to access to the cards.


Rolling Boulder is a typical card to have in an Avatar of Air deck, however with Gothic we have a brand new toy to play with in Lord of Greed. You can now roll the boulder and have Lord of Greed bring it back at the end of turn.


---------- Minions:

Most minions don't' need explanation as they are typical valuable creatures to fly into your opponent's board with AoA.


Men of Leng is a personal pet card of mine that if played at the right time can be very hard to deal with and can take a few cards from your opponent. Use your Blinks, Wuthering Heights, and AoA to fling them to the back row and force some discards.


Skeleton Mage is a fantastic new addition to the roster of air minions as it not only lets you recast your magic, but you can also cast opponent magics that you may need (specifically says "a cemetery" not "your cemetery").


All of the ranged units become extremely difficult to play around with air's mobility. Stygian Archers are one of my favorite new additions. Kill stuff, gain benefits. Doesn't get more satisfying than that.


Daperyll Vampires are probably the most questionable minion on the list. With the changes to how they work in that you no longer get health when striking a site, they lost a lot of luster. However, they are still an airborne minion that is hard to deal with sometimes. They are the most likely to be replaced for lower-cost aggressive targets. And they've also been outclassed by one of my new favorite Airborne minions which are:


Legion of Gall are a fantastic minion. Never would they have printed a 5 mana 5 power Airborne unit in Beta, but they did it in Gothic and gave it an upside. These guys are a monster to deal with, especially early with a tower. On top of them dominating the air, they also remove cards from your opponent's collection. So you get to see what kind of answers they may have and remove their best options.


Lord of Fear is a game ender. Enemies can't defend alone is a huge effect and makes your offense feel so much more powerful. You get to trade better. You get to attack without being blocked. And most importantly Death's Door is scarier than ever.


Lord of Greed is an answer to your opponent's artifacts and he has an upside of having some fun synergy with Rolling Boulder. I debated over 2 of Fear over Greed but there are just too many good artifacts in this game that you want to shut them down as often as you can. We don't have Swap so this is one of our best and consistent answers to artifacts.


---------- Magic:

There are a lot of typical tempo spells you will see in a deck like this but there are a few cards that I want to talk about. Namely Gift of the Wolf and Vanishment.


Gift of the Wolf is a fantastic new card and I feel it might be overlooked very often at first glance. This card is so good at making trades, or just getting extra damage in with a ranged strike or site attack. The fact that it replaces itself and also is a great target for Skeleton Mage is what helped it earn its slots in the deck. I replaced Gigantism with this because Gift of the Wolf more easily fits into turns. Gigantism is still good, but often your opponent will have chump blockers making it have less opportunities to be used.


Vanishment is another one of my own personal pet cards. I like cards that replace themselves, and this does so and protects your board state. Plenty of times I find myself just ahead enough and Vanishment guarantees I stay ahead on my opponent's next turn most of the time.


---------- Sites:


My site choices are very defensive. Stuff like Perilous Bridge, Mountain Pass, and No Man's Land let you take advantage of AoA's mobility while shutting down your opponent's ability to strike back. The quality of sites drastically increased in Gothic. Double threshold sites are an amazing new addition. Learning how to mulligan sites is a process with this deck. Placement of air sites and defensive sites is something you will get used to after playing for a bit. Wuthering Heights is a new site that replicates AoA's ability. This lets you double fly units and get them further in to enemy territory.

deckinfo.name: 2nd place Ascanrask III Water Pathfinder
deckinfo.primer:
Hello there! Hope you having a lovely day.


I was recently at a tournament in Krems, Austria and did preety well for myself! Even though I am playing only for 5 months I still have a lot to learn about this wonderful game and I do believe that this deck is currently one of the strongest water decks out there.


This deck is not my own creation. The mastermind behind it is @Hicham and you should check his main decklist out on curiosa. He is a great guy, and helped me out immensely on learning the deck properly, and understanding the underlying principles of how he imagined things working.


I enjoyed playing with this deck, it is very good and for someone like me, that hasn't played much competitive rl tournaments and it made me not overthink about a lot of things, but rather play aggressive and focus on my own game plan.


The basis of the deck, if you are a magic player, this would be the most Simic experience you will have.


You want to ramp out your big guys, you want to overflow the board, and you want to use your spells to out position your opponents and do valuable trades. Card draw is king in a lot of scenarios where things go a bit late game, but in reality, water is so strong right now, that in the end you will have more value on the board compared to your opponents.


Silver bullet, Snowball, good Swaps will finish on door.


The meta is strong with Necromancers, but a Pied Piper or a Mester Stoor Worm can do a lot of work.


Hopefully you will try it for yourself and enjoy it in its own glory!


Take care and have fun sorcery buddies!

deckinfo.name: Firefinder - SorceryCon 12th Place
deckinfo.primer:
Fire Pathfinder that I played at Sorcery Con 2026 - took 12th place on tiebreakers (6-2) with a very narrow loss in the last round (got the door first but didn't manage to top deck the kill - really epic fight and super well played by my opponent Ismark the Lesser). Pretty simple deck, not much to say about it. Definitely still lots of fine points to playing it though. In the current meta I think one of the big tricks with this deck is not overplaying onto the board while maintaining pressure. Especially into the "Creature Control" meta with lots of Water and Water/Air midrange decks this deck wins on tempo, but loses big to mass removal. You want to mulligan for minions early (maybe keep a single removal spell if you also have some low cost minions but top priority is having 2 and 3 drop minions to start the pressure game. Once you have a minion or two on board though you are just trying to maintain that.


The other common way to win with this deck is setting up a big turn where you blast in a bunch of damage with something like warp spasm, blaze of glory, betrayal, etc. Lots of other cards that go well in this deck, but everything is fighting for slots. Would love to run Shatter Strikes or maybe even Critical Strike to lean more into burst damage turns.


Really torn about Baba Yaga - I don't want more than 5 non fire sites (including mirror realm), so is the extra motion potential that is useful like 50% of the time it is played worth it, or am I better off just running a lone tower to get that ramp value..... Or wizard's Den for the extra card?

deckinfo.name: Silent Fury SorceryCon 17th place
deckinfo.primer:
This deck was very good, and I feel like a good choice for the field of decks present at SC. It's essentially the fury road shell with an emphasis on silence effects. I went 6-2 with this list at Sorcery Con 2026, losing round 2 to mud Geomancer, and round 8 to AoA. It won against 3 Necro decks, Avatar of Earth, fire pathfinder, and an Elementalist brew.


Notable cards:

Sister Stefánia - this card is a power house. I don't think any of the games I had it were close.

Sinterfee - this card is very good against the water decks. Paired with jihad it's amazing.

Corruptor freak - harasses well and can just move to sites forcing multiple interactions to answer it often into a just summoned fatty blocker

Rift valley/smokestacks - these are kind of the same slot because they let us bypass our opponents annoying sites. Expect your opponents to have very good sites. Having ways around them was very helpful.

Earthquake - this card does everything this deck wants. It helps get around sites, it kills stuff allowing you to attack, and most the time just moving the opposing avatar close to your attackers is good enough, get them on DD even if they are on all water sites.

Flame strike (collection) - I think I killed more avatars with this than anything else. You are pretty much always one step away from a hit on DD with this.

Onslaught - I think in many ways this is better than gift of the wolf even without the card draw. It makes spiders worthless, gives you a little charge when needed the spread out damage buff is often better than +2 on a single creature. It also lets you do silly things with your silence/disabled effects like play a slobermaw silenced then give it charge. Or allowing a sleeping giant to wake itself up by attacking a unit. I'll be testing with two copies.


Cards I'm considering cutting:

Blightstone - I got a little sold on this card by a friend. I didn't draw it very often, and each time it was kind of dead in my hand. There were a few times I wanted it. But sinterfee is almost always better.

Hyena - there's just not enough demons that are worth playing. I played it a lot as a 2 power creature, and had mixed feelings about it.

Leadworks - while annoying sites can be problematic for this deck this card never quite lined up the way I wanted. Its really hard in a deck that only wants to play 4 sites to have this line up with a threat in play and a site you need to deal with for a turn.

Slumbering giantess - this card was harder to wake up than I'd like. I still think it's good but it probably needs some other tweaks (more deserts?) to make worth it.

Critical strike (collection) - this was always supposed to be a spin attack, but I get these two chronically confused. Luckily they're pretty close to the same effect.

deckinfo.name: SorceryCon 11th place (6-2) Salt the Wound
deckinfo.primer:
This is a mean deck. It won’t win you many friends but it will win you many games. The name of the game is burn it down or beat them down fast. Using site destruction to slow down or cripple your opponent or minions with immediate impact (i.e. charge, damage on genesis, damage at end of turn). The deck is purposefully built low to the ground for a quick start and eventually multi-spelling at higher mana totals.


Site Destruction Strategies

The main strategy of this deck is site destruction. It utilizes [[Hamlets Ablaze]] and [[Castles Ablaze]] to target defensive sites and your opponents threshold. There’s nothing worse than having a hand full of double pip spells and you constantly lose the threshold to cast them. [[Raze]] can be used to destroy opponents sites but more importantly their artifacts. It’s great for dealing with [[Dank Omphalos]] and its brethren, [[Battlemage]] with a shload of equipment, and if need be popping [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] for a complete board clear. Twice in the tournament, I cast [[Raze]] on my avatar and destroyed Roots the turn it came into play and that won me the game.


TO BE CONTINUED

deckinfo.name: Silenced Bones - 3rd Place Elemental Series Q1 2026 (Sydney, Australia)
deckinfo.primer:
Silenced Bones is a Necromancer mid-range deck supported by a Beast package and a Silence package.


Silence got a huge buff in Gothic with [[Silent Hills]] (and [[Sister Stefania]]) and I believe the archetype can be a great anti-meta option.


The Silence part of the deck shuts down the majority of the card pool, and manh ability-based archetypes like Ward. It is also the enabler for many parts of the Beast package, and other above curve minions such as [[Pirate Ship]] and [[Dalcean Phalanx]]. [[Silence]] itself is (W), so we include this element in the deck.


(E), on the other hand, is the nature (pun not intended) of the Beast archetype, and it is also the only archetype that works with Silence. The mana efficient minions like [[Sedge Crabs]] become a menace, while [[Pudge Butcher]] can transition between a hook thrower and a 4-cost 5-power demon. [[Assorted Animals]] is a 2+ card advantage for you if [[Haystack]] is not in play.


The general strategy is to pump out skeletons to attack AND defend (Silenced skeletons are great blockers!) using [[Necromancer]] with spare mana whenever possible, while taking favourable trades with above-curve Silenced minions. The deck either overwhelms the board or stalls enough time with Silence and defensive sites like [[Troll Bridge]] and [[Babbling Brook]] for a [[Craterize]] straight to Death's Door, followed by a finisher such as [[Zap]] or [[Ice Lance]].


Peculiar card choices:

  • [[Sir Yvain]] screams BEAST. If you're playing Beast, you should play him.
  • [[Garden of Eden]] is your wincon against any draw-heavy decks like [[Sorcerer]] and [[Deathspeaker]]. HARD MULLIGAN for it (3 sites + scry the sites deck). Otherwise, you'd better pray you out-draw them with [[Algor Omphalos]] or win the game in 5-6 turns (you won't, but you can try!).
  • [[Carrion Beetles]] is the vegetable that everyone refuses to play (graveyard hate) and is searchable via [[Common Sense]] and [[Assorted Animals]] with just (1).
  • [[Porcupine Pufferfish]] is an Ordinary Beast with Lethal for (1) (Don't silence him, let him speak!).
  • [[Harvest Festival]] is essentially a (3) spell for 4 in the form of two 2-power bodies. Very underrated!
  • [[Goat for Azazel]] is another good (1) Beast. You can use Silence to turn off his ability when you need to put him down early.
  • [[The Flood]] is a very good late-game board wipe in this particular deck because we play so many types of minions, letting us keep our board while deleting everything without Submerged (Silence also remove Submerged!).
  • [[Forlorn Keep]] is a 3-power body in the form of a site. Sometimes you may want to play this turn 3 to churn out [[Penitent Knight]], or turn 4 with an extra skelly instead of playing cards from your hand. [[Peculiar Port]] serves similar roles, but having an Evil minion may be disadvantaged in some matchups such as [[Persecutor]] or any [[Consecrated Ground]] users.
  • [[Pebbled Paths]], [[Impenetrable Copse]], and [[Haystack]] are interchangeable depending on your local meta. My local meta loves cards like [[Grapple Shot]] and [[Firebolts]].


Overall, this is a really fun deck to play and learn the basics of the game while being very budget-friendly. The list is kept as-is and may need to be optimised for future tournament plays (for example, [[Sister Stefania]] would be a great inclusion, if I had it...).


Shout out to Dean Gouskos and Allen Thrun for hosting the event and carrying the Sydney community on their backs!

deckinfo.name: Greedy Displacement
deckinfo.primer:
Positioning & Movement Synergies

A major strength of the deck is its ability to actively reposition key minions to maximize their impact on both combat and Boulder lines.


Displacement Package

[[Displace]] is one of the most important enablers in the deck. If you are unable to use AoA's ability to move a minion around this allows you to move minions into ideal locations without spending movement actions, often swinging both tempo and board control. You could even double or triple move with AoA's ability along with a [[Displace]] or [[Wuthering Heights]].

The following spells are especially strong when repositioned:


  • [[Pudge Butcher]] – Displacing the Butcher allows you to line up opposing minions into contested or vulnerable lanes increases its impact and forces awkward responses from the opponent.
  • [[Headless Haunt]] – Repositioning Haunts lets you repeatedly apply pressure with a 3 mana cost minion if you get a bad roll.
  • [[Stygian Archers]] – Displace is particularly powerful here, letting you move Archers into safe firing positions or onto key lanes without exposing them to unnecessary risk. Getting skeleton tokens is a convenient annoyance.
  • [[Dalcean Phalynx]] -- Huge hitter that suffers from mobility issues. This mobility is fixed between the AoA and [[Displace]].
  • [[Thunderstorm]] and enemy auras. If they get away from your thunderstorm with a blink or a war horse, just displace it back onto them.


Lord of Greed

  • [[Lord of Greed]] hits hard, threatening 6 damage forcing opponents to answer it quickly or risk losing both board control and key resources.
  • Returns [[Rolling Boulder]] to his hands at the end of your turn, enabling repeated Boulder pressure.
  • Can steal valuable opposing artifacts, creating major tempo and resource swings.
